items.title: [Open Source] DDS AutoDiag v0.1.0 — ROS 2 DDS Diagnostics with AI-Assisted Troubleshooting
items.abstract: Hi ROS community! Ever had two ROS 2 systems that could ping each other, use the same ROS_DOMAIN_ID , but still couldn’t discover each other’s topics? I’ve encountered similar issues while working with distributed ROS 2 systems. Troubleshooting often means manually investigating DDS discovery, middleware configurations, QoS policies, and container networking. To make this process more systematic, I developed DDS AutoDiag v0.1.0, an independent, MIT-licensed open-source tool for diagnosing ROS 2 communication problems across robots, computers, and containers. items.title: livox_gz_sim: Livox Mid-360 and HAP simulation for Gazebo Harmonic
items.abstract: Hi all, I’ve released livox_gz_sim, a Gazebo Harmonic plugin that simulates Livox Mid-360 and HAP lidars and publishes exactly what livox_ros_driver2 publishes. As far as I know it’s the first gpu agnostic Livox simulator for Gazebo Harmonic; the existing ones target Gazebo Classic or require CUDA. What it does Uses Livox’s recorded non-repetitive scan patterns, so coverage builds up over frames like on the real sensor Publishes livox_ros_driver2/CustomMsg or PointCloud2 in the driver’s 26-byte layout ( xfer_format 0/1), with per-point timestamps Simulates the Mid-360’s IMU at 200 Hz Adds rang
items.titleKo: livox_gz_sim: Gazebo Harmonic용 Livox Mid-360 및 HAP 시뮬레이션
items.abstractKo:
안녕하세요. livox_gz_sim을 공개했습니다. 이 Gazebo Harmonic 플러그인은 Livox Mid-360 및 HAP 라이다를 시뮬레이션하며, livox_ros_driver2가 퍼블리시하는 데이터와 정확히 동일한 내용을 퍼블리시합니다. 제가 알기로 Gazebo Harmonic용으로 GPU에 구애받지 않는 최초의 Livox 시뮬레이터이며, 기존 시뮬레이터는 Gazebo Classic을 대상으로 하거나 CUDA를 필요로 합니다.
주요 기능:
- Livox가 기록한 비반복(Non-repetitive) 스캔 패턴을 사용하므로 실제 센서처럼 프레임을 거치며 커버리지가 누적됩니다.
- 드라이버의 26바이트 레이아웃(xfer_format 0/1)으로 livox_ros_driver2/CustomMsg 또는 PointCloud2를 포인트별 타임스탬프와 함께 퍼블리시합니다.
- Mid-360의 IMU를 200 Hz로 시뮬레이션합니다.
- Adds rang(원문이 중단됨)

items.title: A small deterministic gate between the planner and the wheels: ROS 2 Jazzy node, simulation and CI only
items.abstract: I’ve been building a small supervisor node for differential-drive mobile robots that sits between a high-level velocity source (such as Nav2, an LLM agent, or teleoperation) and the base controller. Following the classic Simplex architecture (Sha et al.), the node treats complex high-level planners as unverified proposers and acts as a minimal, deterministic gatekeeper on /cmd_vel. I work alone and I’m self-taught, based in Greece. I have no access to physical robot hardware, so everything described below is evaluated in Webots simulation (PAL Robotics TIAGo base) and verified in GitHub Action
items.titleKo: 플래너와 바퀴 사이의 소형 결정론적 게이트: ROS 2 Jazzy 노드 — 시뮬레이션 및 CI 전용
items.abstractKo: 저는 차동 구동 모바일 로봇을 위해 고수준 속도 명령원(예: Nav2, LLM 에이전트, 원격 조종)과 베이스 컨트롤러 사이에 위치하는 소형 감독 노드를 만들어 왔습니다. 고전적인 Simplex 아키텍처(Sha et al.)를 따르며, 이 노드는 복잡한 고수준 플래너를 검증되지 않은 제안자(unverified proposers)로 취급하고 /cmd_vel에 대해 최소한의 결정론적 게이트키퍼 역할을 수행합니다. 저는 그리스에 거주하는 독학의 단독 개발자이며 물리 로봇 하드웨어에 접근할 수 없기 때문에, 아래에 기술된 모든 내용은 Webots 시뮬레이션(PAL Robotics TIAGo 베이스)에서 평가되었고 GitHub Actions에서 검증되었습니다.

items.title: SwapBot: Tool-Centric Robot Manipulation via Interchangeable End-Effectors and Tactile Sensing
items.abstract: Robot manipulation in everyday environments inherently involves substantial tool usage. Seemingly simple household tasks, such as cooking pan-fried tofu, require forceful cutting, delicate brushing, and precise placement using different tools under contact-rich interaction. Thus, the ability to autonomously swap and use task-appropriate tools is important for tool-centric manipulation. We introduce SwapBot, a modular, tool-centric end effector system featuring low-cost adapters that quickly convert common household tools into robot end effectors. Rather than pursuing a single universal gripper, SwapBot adopts a unified design principle that combines a fixed robot-side coupling interface with low-cost, tool-side adapters, enabling compatibility with diverse tools, including articulated ones, and multiple robot platforms. Each adapter integrates compact tactile sensors, supports fast autonomous swapping, and interfaces with an intuitive teleoperation system for efficient demonstration collection. User studies show that, during teleoperation, SwapBot reduces task completion time and operator workload. Using collected demonstrations on the robot, we train imitation learning policies to successfully perform tool-centric tasks like cooking tofu, stirring salad, flipping meat. Our ablation study shows that using tactile-augmented demonstrations improves policy performance across contact-rich skills, increasing success rates by 15 to 25 percentage points over RGB-only policies. These results highlight modular, tactile-equipped tools as a practical and extensible pathway toward robust and capable robot manipulation. Project website https://personalrobotics.github.io/SwapBot.
items.titleKo: SwapBot: 교체 가능한 엔드이펙터와 촉각 센싱을 이용한 도구 중심 로봇 조작

items.title: SymAnt: Grounding Long-Horizon Action Anticipation with Adaptable Symbolic Priors
items.abstract: As robots and intelligent systems increasingly interact with humans, they must anticipate long sequences of future actions from only brief observations. While purely neural models typically require extensive observations to predict future actions and remain difficult to interpret and adjust, symbolic priors offer a structured alternative. To this end, we introduce SymAnt, a novel neuro-symbolic approach that unifies the expressiveness of neural networks with the structured reasoning of scene and knowledge graphs. Given a short video, SymAnt performs a joint-search over both graphs to construct a symbolic context, enabling unified reasoning over spatial relationships, object attributes, affordances, and associated actions. This symbolic context serves as a prior for an iterative refinement process that progressively generates and improves the sequence of future actions. By grounding predictions in symbolic context, SymAnt anticipates long-horizon actions from short observation windows in a parameter-efficient manner, while enabling users to directly edit the underlying knowledge to adjust predictions without further training. Through our experiments, we demonstrate the effectiveness of SymAnt, particularly when only short observation contexts are available, across five diverse datasets: Breakfast, 50 Salads, EPIC-KITCHENS, EGTEA Gaze+, and Assembly101.
items.titleKo: SymAnt: 적응 가능한 기호적 사전 지식을 통한 장기 행동 예측의 구체화

items.title: A Conveyor Belt Mechanism for Repositionable Magnetic Coupling Between Continuum Robots
items.abstract: This work proposes a novel conveyor belt mechanism enabling continuous, active repositioning of functional elements along the body of a tendon-driven continuum robot. Up to three conveyor belt mechanisms are integrated within a 9 mm diameter continuum robot. We demonstrate equivalent or reduced conveyor belt actuation forces compared to robot tendon actuation forces. As a case study, we mount permanent magnets along two conveyor belts, and demonstrate actively reconfigurable inter-robot coupling. Coupling point location and quantity can be adjusted during robot operation to actively tune the effective stiffness of the coupled multi-robot system. We show that effective stiffness follows a predictable inverse-cubic relationship with coupling location, and increases with the number of coupling points. These findings demonstrate that the conveyor belt mechanism enables active functional element repositioning for changing tasks requirements, with magnetic inter-robot coupling as one proof-of-concept.
items.titleKo: 연속체 로봇 간 재배치 가능한 자기 결합을 위한 컨베이어 벨트 메커니즘
items.abstractKo: 본 연구는 텐던 구동 연속체 로봇의 몸체를 따라 기능 요소를 연속적이고 능동적으로 재배치할 수 있게 해주는 새로운 컨베이어 벨트 메커니즘을 제안한다. 최대 세 개의 컨베이어 벨트 메커니즘이 직경 9 mm의 연속체 로봇 내부에 통합된다. 본 메커니즘은 컨베이어 벨트의 구동력이 로봇의 텐던 구동력에 비해 동등하거나 더 낮음을 보여준다. 사례 연구로 영구자석을 두 개의 컨베이어 벨트에 장착하여 능동적으로 재구성 가능한 로봇 간 결합을 시연한다. 결합 지점의 위치와 수는 로봇 동작 중에 조정할 수 있어 능동적으로 e를 조정할 수 있다.

items.title: Gym-Anything for Robotics: Scaling physical simulations with digital agents
items.abstract: Realistic, fast robotics simulations could enable large-scale training of embodied AI models that transfer to the real world. However, despite decades of progress, available simulations cover only a narrow range of real-world tasks and physical phenomena. The core bottleneck is that creating better simulations requires significant expert effort and therefore does not scale. To address this, we introduce Gym-Anything for Robotics, a framework in which coding agents create realistic robotics simulations. Our core insight is that simulation creation is a coding agent task, so improvements in coding agents translate directly into richer and more faithful simulations. We select simulations based on U.S. GDP data to cover economically valuable physical work, define what makes a good simulation and a good task, and develop an adversarial creation-audit loop that checks each simulation and task against these definitions. Using this pipeline, we build RoboWorld, a set of 25 simulations with 25 test and 175 training RL environments of varying difficulty. Even the best frontier models fail on every RoboWorld test task, achieving an average reward of only 0.06. Building on RoboWorld, we introduce several new ways for frontier models to improve, including in-context learning across repeated attempts, a privileged teacher that reads the simulator state and teaches a student in context, self-assisted learning from the model's own privileged experience, and code policies that generate demonstrations across varied scenes to train vision-language-action models (VLAs) such as $π_{0.5}$. Each of these substantially improves performance. We release our pipeline, RL environments, and benchmark to facilitate future research. Code and data are available at https://gym-anything.github.io/robotics
items.titleKo: 로보틱스용 Gym-Anything: 디지털 에이전트로 물리 시뮬레이션 확장
items.abstractKo: 현실적이고 빠른 로보틱스 시뮬레이션은 실제 세계로 전이되는 체현형(embodied) AI 모델을 대규모로 학습시키는 것을 가능하게 할 수 있다. 그러나 수십 년의 진전에도 불구하고, 현재 이용 가능한 시뮬레이션은 실제 작업과 물리적 현상의 좁은 범위만을 다룬다. 핵심 병목은 더 나은 시뮬레이션을 만드는 데 상당한 전문가의 노력이 필요하다는 점으로, 따라서 확장 가능하지 않다는 것이다. 이를 해결하기 위해 우리는 코딩 에이전트가 현실적인 로보틱스 시뮬레이션을 생성하는 프레임워크인 Gym-Anything for Robotics를 도입한다. 우리의 핵심 통찰은 시뮬레이션 생성이 코딩 에이전트의 과제라는 점이므로, 코딩... items.title: A Tutorial on Shape Servoing of Deformable Objects-Part I: Fundamentals
items.abstract: In robotics, shape control (or shape servoing) refers to the automatic manipulation of a deformable object to achieve a desired shape. It involves a feedback loop that exploits the relation between robot motion and changes in the measured shape. This relation, known as the interaction Jacobian or, in this context, the deformation Jacobian, depends on the object's mechanical properties, geometry, and boundary conditions (e.g., where the object is grasped). Because these factors are often difficult to model accurately, the deformation Jacobian can be estimated locally from observed shape changes produced by commanded robot motions, without requiring a fine-tuned mechanical model. This article is the first of a two-part tutorial on data-driven Jacobian-based shape control of deformable objects. It introduces the central elements of the approach: the formulation of the shape-control problem, shape representation, estimation and online update of the deformation Jacobian, and a standard control law from the literature. It then assembles these elements into a complete shape-servoing loop, derives a local stability condition for this loop, and illustrates why some target shapes cannot be reached. Part II covers more advanced topics. Throughout both parts, a simulated planar example in which two robot arms manipulate an elastic rod observed by a camera illustrates the concepts.
items.titleKo: 변형 물체의 형상 서보 튜토리얼 — 제1부: 기초
items.abstractKo: 로보틱스에서 형상 제어(또는 형상 서보)는 변형 가능한 물체를 원하는 형상으로 자동 조작하는 것을 말한다. 이는 로봇의 동작과 측정된 형상의 변화 사이 관계를 이용하는 피드백 루프를 포함한다. 상호작용 야코비안(interaction Jacobian)으로 알려진 이 관계는 본 문맥에서는 변형 야코비안이라 불리며, 물체의 기계적 특성, 기하학적 형태 및 경계 조건(예: 물체가 잡혀 있는 지점)에 따라 달라진다. 이러한 요인들은 정확히 모델링하기 어려운 경우가 많기 때문에 변형 야코비안은 관찰된 형상 변화로부터 국소적으로 추정될 수 있다.

items.title: PhysVLMM: Interaction-Conditioned Physical Belief Maps for Articulated Objects in Robot Scene Maps
items.abstract: Mobile robots must open doors and drawers, yet their scene maps record what each object is and whether it has moved, not how it will respond to a pull. This paper proposes PhysVLMM, a method that maintains a physical belief for every articulated part of a Vision-Language-Motion Map and answers a planner's queries about it, with two algorithms: a map update and a query. Watching a part move provably cannot identify its dynamics, and a measured pull identifies only the pulled part, up to one direction. PhysVLMM therefore (i) keeps that direction as a posterior instead of a point estimate, (ii) passes the evidence of each pull in closed form to the untouched look-alike parts of the map, and (iii) answers whether an action will succeed at a stated risk, or abstains. On real doors and drawers in 18 homes, it identifies the joint type in 86% of held-out pulls (48% for a learned single-view method) and predicts the response to a pull with 41% lower error than differentiable simulation (CRPS 0.323 vs. 0.544), four orders of magnitude faster (13 ms vs. 230 s per case). The posterior lowers the final-position error from 0.460 to 0.270, sharing lowers the force error of untouched parts from 56% to 42%, and at every stated risk from 0.02 to 0.30 the false-safe answers stay within it. Pooling all measured parts of a home does as well as the look-alike groups, and simpler variants predict where a pulled part stops at least as well.
items.titleKo: PhysVLMM: 로봇 장면 지도에서 관절형 객체를 위한 상호작용에 조건화된 물리적 신념 맵
items.abstractKo: 이동 로봇은 문과 서랍을 열어야 하지만, 장면 지도는 각 객체가 무엇인지와 이동했는지만 기록할 뿐, 당겼을 때 어떻게 반응할지는 기록하지 않는다. 본 논문은 PhysVLMM을 제안한다. 이 방법은 시각-언어-동작 맵(Vision-Language-Motion Map)의 각 관절 부분에 대해 물리적 신념을 유지하고, 플래너의 쿼리에 응답하는 두 가지 알고리즘(맵 업데이트와 쿼리)을 제공한다. 어떤 부품의 움직임을 관찰하는 것만으로는 그 역학을 식별할 수 없다는 것이 증명되며, 측정된 당김은 오직 당겨진 부품만을 방향의 부호 불확실성을 제외하고 식별한다. 따라서 PhysVLMM은 (i) 그 방향을 점 추정치 대신 사후확률로 유지하고, (ii) p

items.title: DAWN: Diffusion-based Alignment and unfastening Workflow Network
items.abstract: We present DAWN (Diffusion-based Alignment and unfastening Workflow Network), a hierarchical robotic framework designed to perform real-world, unfastening tasks through multi-modal sensory integration. Autonomous robotic unfastening is crucial for improving recycling processes, enhancing safety, and reducing operational costs; yet, it remains predominantly manual due to inherent challenges in precise screwdriver engagement with fasteners, detailed force execution, and robustness to environmental variability. To address the complexity of learning long-horizon, contact-rich manipulation tasks, we subdivide the unfastening task procedure into two sequential stages: (1) alignment & insertion, and (2) unfastening. DAWN consists of three key components: AlignNet, a diffusion-based policy ensuring precise screwdriver tip engagement; LatchNet, a multi-modal classifier reliably detecting successful stage transitions; and UnfastNet, which achieves stable, force-controlled screw removal. Experimental validation on a Franka Emika robot demonstrates that DAWN achieves alignment & insertion success rates comparable to trained human operators, robustly transitions between stages, and attains an impressive success rate in unfastening across various unseen scenarios. Ablation studies further elucidate critical input modalities and effective training strategies, highlighting DAWN's scalability, robustness, and data efficiency.
items.titleKo: DAWN: 확산 기반 정렬 및 풀기 워크플로우 네트워크
items.abstractKo: 우리는 DAWN(확산 기반 정렬 및 풀기 워크플로우 네트워크)를 제안한다. 이 계층적 로봇 프레임워크는 다중 모달 센서 통합을 통해 실제 환경에서의 풀기 작업을 수행하도록 설계되었다. 자율 로봇 풀기 작업은 재활용 공정의 개선, 안전성 향상, 운영 비용 절감에 중요한 역할을 하지만, 드라이버와 패스너의 정밀한 맞물림, 세밀한 힘 제어의 수행, 환경 변화에 대한 강건성 등 내재된 어려움으로 인해 여전히 대부분 수작업으로 이루어지고 있다. 장기간에 걸친 접촉 중심의 조작 과제를 학습하는 복잡성을 해결하기 위해, w

items.title: BURGER: Benchmarking and Understanding Robotic Generalization via Embodied Drawing
items.abstract: How effectively can vision-language-action (VLA) models learn diverse language-conditioned behaviors as training data scales? Investigating this question requires large and varied robot datasets, whose collection on physical robots remains costly. We introduce BURGER, a language-conditioned robotic drawing benchmark with a scalable, prompt-driven pipeline for generating continuous drawing trajectories, both in simulation and the real world. In BURGER, an agent starts from the same blank canvas and controls a robot arm to draw the object or spatial composition specified by language, while each instruction allows an open-ended variety of valid drawings and stroke orders. Using 28,200 simulated demonstrations spanning 282 drawing tasks, we evaluate five representative VLA models across data scales, language grounding, and multimodal behavior. BURGER supports fine-grained analysis of language grounding, spatial composition, and action generation, revealing distinct failure patterns across VLA models. Our experiments suggest that some VLA models can benefit from greater task diversity and demonstration scale, capture multimodal drawing behaviors, and generalize to unseen compositions of familiar objects. Finally, we deploy a trained policy on a Franka Panda arm, demonstrating the ability to draw reactively under human intervention. Project homepage and code can be found at https://siyingzhao.github.io/BURGER/.
items.titleKo: BURGER: 체현된 드로잉을 통한 로봇 일반화의 벤치마킹 및 이해
items.abstractKo: 학습 데이터가 증가할 때 비전-언어-행동(VLA) 모델이 언어 조건화된 다양한 행동을 얼마나 효과적으로 학습할 수 있는가? 이 질문을 조사하려면 크고 다양한 로봇 데이터셋이 필요하며, 물리적 로봇에서 이를 수집하는 비용은 여전히 매우 높다. 우리는 BURGER를 제안한다. items.title: A Two-Wheeled Quadrotor with All-Clockwise Tilted Rotors for Level-Attitude Surface Locomotnion
items.abstract: Conventional wheel-equipped quadrotor UAVs must tilt their bodies to generate lateral forces, limiting their ability to maintain a desired attitude during lateral motion. This paper proposes a wheeled quadrotor with all-clockwise tilted rotors that uses surface contact as a constraint to generate propulsion along the contact surface without tilting the vehicle. We analyze feasible forces and system controllability under surface contact and optimize the vehicle design considering different rotor-spin configurations. The optimization results show that a configuration in which all four rotors spin clockwise can generate a larger tangential force than the conventional alternating-spin configuration. This approach enables both aerial and contact-based locomotion without additional rotor-tilting actuators or mechanisms. Simulation results demonstrate both hovering in free space and horizontal locomotion on a floor while maintaining a level attitude.
items.titleKo: 수평 자세 유지형 표면 주행을 위한 모든 로터가 시계 방향으로 기울어진 2륜 쿼드로터
items.abstractKo: 기존의 바퀴 장착 쿼드로터 UAV는 횡방향 힘을 발생시키기 위해 기체를 기울여야 하므로 횡방향 이동 중 원하는 자세를 유지하는 능력이 제한된다. 본 논문은 모든 로터가 시계 방향으로 기울어진 바퀴 달린 쿼드로터를 제안하며, 이 기체는 표면 접촉을 제약 조건으로 활용해 기체를 기울이지 않고도 접촉면을 따라 추진력을 생성한다. 우리는 표면 접촉 하에서 가능한 힘과 시스템의 제어 가능성을 분석하고, 서로 다른 로터 회전 구성들을 고려하여 기체 설계를 최적화한다. 최적화 결과는 모든 네 로터가 회… [요약 원문이 중단됨]

items.title: Fundamental Limits of Sampling-Based Reachability: Geometry and Flow Distortion
items.abstract: Sampling-based reachability estimates reachable sets from finitely many simulated trajectory endpoints. Existing guarantees often control missed probability mass or approximation error relative to the convex hull of the reachable set, leaving the geometric error relative to the reachable set incompletely characterized. We study this error as a problem of support estimation under flow distortion. Our assumptions combine a uniform lower bound on the local volume density of the initial set, a lower bound on the sampling density, and a one-sided Lipschitz constant $μ$ for the vector field. These conditions admit initial sets with corners and dynamics that may expand or contract. In the fine-accuracy regime, $\tilde{\mathcal O}\bigl(2^ne^{nμT}(R/r)^n/(ρκ)\bigr)$ independent endpoint samples suffice for Hausdorff accuracy $r$ using the endpoint cloud. Here, $n$ is the state dimension, $T$ is the horizon, $R$ is the volume-equivalent radius, and $ρ$ and $κ$ quantify sampling density and local volume density. For $n\ge2$ and sufficiently small $κ$, a minimax lower bound over all estimators based only on independent endpoints matches these dependencies up to a dimension-dependent factor $2\cdot4^n$ and logarithmic factors, within the stated parameter range and when the state domain accommodates the construction. The exponential burden in dimension, and in the horizon for expanding systems, is therefore intrinsic to this observation model. Planar experiments illustrate the predicted effects of corners and contraction; robot-arm experiments show how empirical accuracy deteriorates with dimension.
items.titleKo: 샘플링 기반 도달성의 근본적 한계: 기하학과 흐름 왜곡
items.abstractKo: 샘플링 기반 도달성은 유한 개의 시뮬레이션된 궤적 종단점들로부터 도달 가능 집합을 추정한다. 기존의 보장들은 대개 놓친 확률 질량이나 도달 가능 집합의 볼록 껍질(convex hull)에 대한 근사 오차를 제어하는 데 중점을 두어, 도달 가능 집합 자체에 대한 기하학적 오차는 불충분하게 특성화되어 있다. 우리는 이 오차를 흐름 왜곡(flow distortion) 하에서의 지지(서포트) 추정 문제로 연구한다. 우리의 가정은 초기 집합의 국소 체적 밀도에 대한 균일한 하한, 샘플링 밀도에 대한 하한, 그리고 벡터장에 대한 단측 리프시츠 상수 μ를 결합한다. (원문이 'These c'로 미완성되어 있어 이후 내용은 제공된 원문에 없음)

items.title: Adaptive search with path-constrained mobile sensors using multi-arm bandits
items.abstract: We study a constrained sequential decision problem for detecting regions of interest from noisy online measurements collected by a team of energy-constrained mobile sensors. The sensor motion is restricted to a precomputed set of feasible paths that satisfy mobility constraints, limited available energy by requiring return to charging stations, and avoidance of known obstacles. We cast the resulting active path selection as a multi-armed bandit problem and propose an iterative search algorithm that adaptively assigns paths using confidence bounds computed from the collected data. We also propose a graph-based method to construct low-cardinality path covers under the team's constraints. We establish finite-time and anytime probabilistic correctness guarantees for the proposed algorithm, derive non-asymptotic upper bounds on the times required to detect all regions of interest and to label all nodes, and show that these bounds match algorithm-independent lower bounds up to constant factors for a broad class of problem instances. Using numerical simulations, we illustrate the behavior of the proposed approach and the effect of path redundancy and team size on search performance.
items.titleKo: 경로 제약이 있는 모바일 센서를 위한 멀티암드 밴딧 기반 적응적 탐색
items.abstractKo: 우리는 에너지 제약을 가진 모바일 센서 팀이 수집한 잡음이 섞인 온라인 측정값으로부터 관심 영역을 탐지하는 제약된 순차 의사결정 문제를 연구한다. 센서의 이동은 이동성 제약을 만족하고 충전소로 복귀해야 하는 제한된 가용 에너지 및 알려진 장애물의 회피를 고려하여 사전 계산된 유효 경로 집합으로 제한된다. 본 연구에서는 이러한 능동적 경로 선택 문제를 멀티암드 밴딧 문제로 정형화하고, 수집된 데이터로부터 계산한 신뢰구간을 사용해 경로를 적응적으로 할당하는 반복적 탐색 알고리즘을 제안한다. 또한 제안...

items.title: Improving Fine-Grained Manipulation through Demonstration Expansion and Execution Design
items.abstract: Fine-grained manipulation requires a robot policy to follow instructions, remain robust to visual variations, and translate predicted actions into precise robot control. We present Demonstration Expansion and Execution Design (DEED), a framework for adapting a pretrained vision-language-action policy to the five MetaFine tasks through structured demonstration expansion and execution design. DEED generates demonstrations for different instructions from the same initial scene and renders each physical trajectory under different camera positions and lighting conditions while preserving its original states and action targets. A hierarchical sampling strategy balances instructions, trajectories, and visual conditions during supervised adaptation. At deployment, DEED converts predicted action chunks into robot commands using inverse kinematics, gripper mappings selected for each task, and closed-loop replanning. DEED achieves an official Overall score of 85.55%. Fixed-policy evaluations show that performance varies with execution horizon, denoising budget, and gripper mapping.
items.titleKo: 시연 확장 및 실행 설계를 통한 세밀한 조작 성능 향상
items.abstractKo: 세밀한 조작은 로봇 정책이 지시를 충실히 따르고 시각적 변화에 강인하며, 예측된 동작을 정밀한 로봇 제어로 변환할 수 있어야 한다. 우리는 Demonstration Expansion and Execution Design(DEED)라는 프레임워크를 제시한다. DEED는 사전 학습된 비전-언어-동작 정책을 구조화된 시연 확장과 실행 설계를 통해 MetaFine의 다섯 과제에 적응시키기 위한 방법이다. DEED는 동일한 초기 장면으로부터 서로 다른 지시문에 대한 시연을 생성하고, 각 물리적 궤적을 원래의 물리적 특성을 보존하면서 서로 다른 카메라 위치와 조명 조건에서 렌더링한다.

items.title: Optimal Path Planning with Localization constraints
items.abstract: This paper studies UAV path planning in areas where GPS signals are not present. Because these drones can easily get lost when they don't have GPS, they must rely on dead reckoning and occasionally pass near cellular towers, which act as landmarks to reset and fix their position. The goal is to find the shortest path from a start to a goal location while keeping the estimation uncertainty within a given bound. To solve this problem, we propose a localization-constrained A* planner that treats uncertainty as a hard constraint during search. The robot state and covariance are propagated using an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF), and only paths that satisfy the covariance limit are considered. We also show that the proposed method does not affect heuristic used in A* and remains admissible and consistent, ensuring optimality among all feasible paths. Extensive Monte Carlo simulations and PyBullet quadrotor test show that the proposed method finds shorter and more reliable paths compared to RRT* and PRM, while always satisfying the uncertainty constraint.
items.titleKo: 로컬라이제이션 제약을 고려한 최적 경로 계획
items.abstractKo: 본 논문은 GPS 신호가 닿지 않는 지역에서의 UAV 경로 계획을 연구한다. GPS가 없으면 드론은 쉽게 위치를 잃을 수 있으므로 관성항법(데드 레코닝)에 의존하고, 때때로 셀룰러 기지국 근처를 지나 이들 기지국을 위치 재설정용 랜드마크로 활용한다. 목표는 추정 불확실성을 주어진 한계 이내로 유지하면서 시작 지점에서 목표 지점까지의 최단 경로를 찾는 것이다. 이를 해결하기 위해 탐색 중 불확실성을 강한 제약으로 취급하는 로컬라이제이션 제약 A* 플래너를 제안한다. 로봇 상태와 공분산은 사용하여

items.title: socx: GPU-Accelerated Chance-Constrained Stochastic Optimal Control using JAX
items.abstract: In this article, we present socx, a GPU-accelerated solver for lifted convex reformulations of linear stochastic optimal control under chance constraints, implemented in JAX. We demonstrate that by exploiting the sparse and independent structure of the problem, distributed optimization can reduce it to simpler problems: independent linear-quadratic tracking (LQT) problems and Euclidean projections onto sets. These simpler problems can be solved in parallel and then coupled using the constraints. To validate our solver, we run it on a hover-linearized 3D quadrotor and show a speed-up of up to $98\times$ over MOSEK and up to $2224\times$ over SCS. socx also solves horizons up to $N=1120$, whereas MOSEK runs out of memory at $N=320$. We present ablations to isolate the key components that enable the speed-up.
items.titleKo: socx: JAX를 이용한 GPU 가속 확률 제약 선형 확률적 최적 제어
items.abstractKo: 본 논문에서는 JAX로 구현한, 리프팅된 볼록 재수식화(lifted convex reformulation)를 이용한 확률 제약을 갖는 선형 확률적 최적 제어용 GPU 가속 솔버 socx를 소개한다. 문제의 희소하고 독립적인 구조를 활용하면 분산 최적화로 문제를 더 단순한 문제들—독립적인 선형-이차 추적(LQT) 문제들과 집합에 대한 유클리드 투영—로 환원할 수 있음을 보인다. 이러한 단순 문제들은 병렬로 해결한 뒤 제약을 통해 결합할 수 있다. 솔버를 검증하기 위해 호버 선형화된 3D 쿼드로터에 적용한 결과 최대 $의 속도 향상을 보였다.

items.title: Continuous-Action World Models: Learning Cross-Embodiment Spatiotemporal Dynamics Priors
items.abstract: We introduce Continuous-Action World Models (CoAWM), a framework for learning cross-embodiment spatiotemporal dynamics priors that support robot action generation across embodiments and execution frequencies. At its core is a shared latent function space that captures the spatial and temporal structure of robot actions. We learn this space through two stages. First, function pretraining brings trajectories from different embodiments and sampling frequencies into a common representation, learning shared dynamics priors through action reconstruction and consistency across temporal sampling views. By accommodating heterogeneous robot trajectories, this stage broadens the range of data sources available for pretraining and facilitates scaling to larger and more diverse datasets. Second, we connect the pretrained function space to a world-model backbone, enabling observations, language instructions, and the current robot state to condition the prediction of a latent action function. A single decoder takes any query time and returns the corresponding end-effector action. By separating shared dynamics priors from task-conditioned action selection and temporal sampling, our approach provides a unified foundation for transferring robot experience across embodiments and control frequencies.
items.titleKo: 연속 행동 월드 모델: 다양한 로봇 형상 간 시공간 동역학 사전 학습
items.abstractKo: 우리는 Continuous-Action World Models(CoAWM)를 도입한다. 이 프레임워크는 다양한 로봇 형상(embodiments)과 실행 빈도에 걸쳐 로봇 행동 생성을 지원하는 교차-형상 시공간 동역학 사전(cross-embodiment spatiotemporal dynamics priors)을 학습한다. 핵심은 로봇 행동의 공간적·시간적 구조를 포착하는 공유 잠재 함수 공간이다. 이 공간은 두 단계로 학습된다. 첫째, 함수 사전학습(function pretraining)은 서로 다른 형상과 샘플링 빈도의 궤적을 공통 표현으로 변환하여, 행동 재구성과 시간적 샘플링 관점 간의 일관성을 통해 공유 동역학 사전을 학습한다.

items.title: Securing the Robotics Supply Chain
items.abstract: This paper sets out what a sustained federal research and investment agenda would need to include to close that gap--not within a single budget cycle, but over the decade such an undertaking will realistically require. It identifies where the gap is most pronounced today: in the methods needed to verify and certify components of uncertain origin, in the foundational hardware research that has long been underfunded relative to software, in the physical infrastructure researchers need to test systems at scale, and in the workforce required to build and sustain all of it. Robotics should not be treated merely as a downstream beneficiary of a broader artificial intelligence investment strategy. It constitutes its own supply chain, with its own points of failure, and merits its own sustained federal commitment.
items.titleKo: 로봇 공급망 보안 확보
items.abstractKo: 이 논문은 그 격차를 해소하기 위해 장기적으로 연방 정부가 추진해야 할 연구 및 투자 의제가 어떤 내용을 포함해야 하는지를 제시한다—한 번의 예산 주기가 아니라, 이러한 과제가 현실적으로 요구하는 10년에 걸쳐서다. 현재 그 격차가 가장 두드러지게 나타나는 분야는 다음과 같다: 출처가 불확실한 구성 요소를 검증하고 인증하는 데 필요한 방법, 소프트웨어에 비해 오랫동안 상대적으로 저조한 자금 지원을 받아온 기초 하드웨어 연구, 연구자들이 시스템을 대규모로 시험하기 위해 필요한 물리적 인프라, 그리고 이 모든 것을 구축하고 유지할 인력이다. 로보틱스는...

items.title: HiFOR: Hierarchical Foresight with Action-Guided World Grounding for Vision-Language-Action Model
items.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have demonstrated promising capabilities in robotic manipulation by integrating visual perception, language understanding, and action generation. Recent advances have further incorporated future prediction to enhance the understanding of environmental dynamics and task progression. However, existing methods often model short-term dynamics and long-term task objectives separately, while directly incorporating predicted futures into action policies without sufficiently considering their relevance to current action requirements. To address these limitations, we propose HiFOR, a hierarchical foresight framework with action-guided world retrieval. Specifically, Hierarchical Foresight Prediction jointly predicts short-term state evolution, semantic milestones, and final goal states through a Hierarchical Dependency Mask (HDM), establishing dependencies across temporal horizons. Building upon these predictions, Structure-Aware Latent World Modeling organizes future latent representations along the horizon, view, and spatial dimensions to facilitate fine-grained retrieval. Furthermore, Action-Guided Factorized World Retrieval adaptively retrieves relevant future information from the structured latent world based on evolving action representations during denoising, providing targeted guidance for action generation. Extensive experiments on two simulation benchmarks and six real-world robotic manipulation tasks demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach.

items.title: Is It the Curriculum or Just the Easy Start? Benchmarking Unsupervised Environment Design on Quadrupeds
items.abstract: Unsupervised environment design (UED) methods such as PLR, ACCEL, SFL and PAIRED are compared mostly on 2D mazes, grid worlds and BipedalWalker, while terrain curricula for legged robots are hand-designed and evaluated against a few baselines. We present a benchmark that runs fourteen UED, domain-randomisation and robotics curricula under one protocol on five 3D quadrupeds in MuJoCo MJX: the closed-chain W01-TEK and the open-chain Unitree Go1 and Go2, Google Barkour vB and Boston Dynamics Spot. Levels are vectors of eight interpretable terrain parameters, and all curricula drive the same PPO student at matched environment-step budgets. The evaluation reports success on random and held-out structured terrains, interquartile means with stratified bootstrap intervals, capability envelopes and a level-by-level domination comparison. We compare methods within each robot and report, per level set, the top group of methods not significantly below the best. No method is in the top group on every robot and level set. Methods with easy or low-difficulty training levels, curated or not, fill the top groups on in-distribution random levels of Go1 and Barkour, and of W01-TEK apart from PAIRED+BiBC. The success-driven terrain curriculum from legged-robot practice is in a top group most often, domain randomisation on uniform levels in none, and PAIRED in none outside Spot, where the fourteen methods lie within 3.8 points on random levels of difficulty 0.25. On three robots the leader on in-distribution random levels is not the leader on held-out terrain. We collect the results into a per-robot guide to choosing a curriculum.

items.title: JEDI: Joint-Embedding Demonstration Compression for In-Context Imitation Learning
items.abstract: In-context imitation learning (ICIL) adapts robot policies through test-time demonstrations, but long multimodal trajectories constrain how many examples fit in context. We ask what a compressed demonstration should preserve. We propose JEDI, which compresses demonstrations into latent slots trained to predict the query episode's next-stage keyframe in a frozen video-JEPA space. Task and process counterfactuals help the slots preserve execution details, while the predictor selects demonstrations from a bank. Post-training with keypoint tokens enables human-hand conditioning on robots. Experiments on LIBERO and real robots show that JEDI supports many-shot context; LIBERO objective controls show improved success and demonstration following over action-only compression. These findings support query-future prediction as a training objective for preserving execution-relevant information in compressed demonstrations.
items.titleKo: JEDI: 문맥 내 모방 학습을 위한 공동 임베딩 기반 시연 압축
items.abstractKo: 문맥 내 모방 학습(ICIL)은 테스트 시점의 시연을 통해 로봇 정책을 적응시키지만, 길고 멀티모달한 궤적은 문맥에 들어갈 수 있는 시연 수를 제약한다. 우리는 압축된 시연이 무엇을 보존해야 하는지를 묻는다. 본 논문에서는 JEDI를 제안한다. JEDI는 시연을 잠재 슬롯으로 압축하며, 이 슬롯들은 동결된 비디오-JEPA 공간에서 질의 에피소드의 다음 단계 키프레임을 예측하도록 학습된다. 작업 및 수행 과정에 대한 반사실적(counterfactual) 예시는 슬롯이 실행 세부사항을 보존하도록 돕고, 예측기는 시연 뱅크에서 시연을 선택한다. 키포인트 토큰을 이용한 사후 학습은 인간 손 입력에 대한 로봇의 조건화를 가능하게 한다. items.title: ThinkWorld: World Imagination Reinforces Chain-of-Dynamics Reasoning
items.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have made substantial progress in robotic manipulation, but their generalization remains constrained by the diversity and coverage of action-labeled robot demonstrations. Human videos provide much broader behavioral and environmental experience, while learning from them faces a fundamental trade-off between scalable data and explicit action grounding. We introduce ThinkWorld, a VLA learning framework that grounds action reasoning in world dynamics and strengthens it through reinforcement learning with world imagination. ThinkWorld represents each action thought as a Chain-of-Dynamics (CoD), a sequence of discrete motion tokens that captures the intermediate dynamics connecting the current world to a future state and serves as a common action representation across embodiments. We first initialize CoD with action-labeled demonstrations, then predict the future induced by each CoD and reinforce those whose predictions better match the observed outcome. This enables videos without action annotations to provide direct supervision from observed state transitions, allowing human and robot experience to refine the same reasoning space. Experiments in simulation and on real robots demonstrate effective human-to-robot transfer and strong generalization to unseen tasks and environments.

items.title: Pushing Dexterity and Safety for In-Hand Object Pose Reaching That Works Remarkably Well
items.abstract: Dexterous manipulation with multi-fingered hands is the next frontier of robotics, yet learned hand skills remain limited to simple grasps or basic repeated motions, such as rotating an object. As robots attempt more demanding in-hand maneuvers, safety, such as not dropping the object, becomes critical, yet it is rarely measured. We study in-hand object pose reaching, a task that demands diverse and difficult grasps: moving an object to almost any position and orientation within reach of the fingers, at any wrist orientation, through long sequences of consecutive goals. We present a recipe for training such policies for a LEAP hand in simulation without human data, built on a range of insights, from diverse resets and goals via generated grasp datasets to an adaptive friction curriculum. With careful system identification, the policies transfer zero-shot to the real hand, using either motion capture or a single wrist-mounted depth camera, and prove remarkably capable and robust. On top of the task policy, we add a learned residual safety filter with adjustable conservativeness, letting us tune the balance between performance and safety and greatly reduce object drops. In 13.3 hours of real-robot evaluation over 4,800 unseen goals across 4 objects and diverse wrist orientations, the state-based policy reaches 95.2% of goals within 2 cm and 0.4 rad, and the filter cuts its drops by 75% while still reaching 91.5% of goals. The policies can also spin a lightbulb held in an arbitrary pose, reach out-of-distribution goals, withstand fast arm motion and perturbations, and, needing only a wrist camera, serve as portable skills such as screwing in a lightbulb. We release the full recipe as a platform for studying performance, reliability, and safety in high-dimensional dexterous systems. Videos and more are available at https://ian-chuang.github.io/dexsafe/.
items.titleKo: 놀랍도록 잘 작동하는 인핸드 물체 자세 도달을 위한 조작성 및 안전성 향상
items.abstractKo: 다지 손을 이용한 정교한 조작은 로보틱스의 다음 경계이지만, 학습된 손 기술은 여전히 단순한 파지나 물체를 회전시키는 것과 같은 기본적인 반복 동작에만 국한되어 있다. 로봇이 더 까다로운 인핸드 기동을 시도할수록 물체를 떨어뜨리지 않는 것과 같은 안전성이 중요해지지만, 이는 거의 측정되지 않는다. 우리는 인핸드 물체 자세 도달이라는, 다양한 어렵고 까다로운 파지를 요구하는 과제를 연구한다: 손목 자세에 관계없이 손가락의 도달 범위 안에서 물체를 거의 모든 위치와 자세로 이동시키고, 연속적인 긴 목표 시퀀스를 통해 이를 수행하는 것이다. 우리는 이를 위한 레시피를 제시한다.

items.title: Perceiving and Predicting Dynamic Sports: Spatiotemporal Intelligence in Vision Models for Egocentric Tennis Video
items.abstract: Agile robots require spatiotemporal intelligence to interpret scenes, reason about interactions, and anticipate future events. Yet it remains unclear how well foundation vision models support these capabilities, particularly from a moving egocentric camera, which is a natural view for robots. To investigate this, we collect an annotated tennis dataset and train a suite of vision models on spatiotemporal tasks. Our dataset contains egocentric video synchronized with five allocentric videos, estimated global positions, labeled contact times, and annotated stroke types. We then evaluate seven prediction tasks from egocentric images: 2D ego player and 3D ball localization, future player and ball trajectories, forehand or backhand stroke anticipation, time to the next ego player ball contact, and 3D ball position at that contact. We compare image encoders, video encoders, and vision-language models with jointly trained prediction heads. The best performing models achieve mean current-frame localization errors of 0.14 m for the ego player and 0.54 m for the ball, future forecasting errors of 0.34 m for the ego player and 0.91 m for the ball over 1.1 s, and a mean contact-time prediction error of 0.14 s. Auxiliary depth information substantially improves 3D ball localization, suggesting that inferring metric depth remains a challenge. Longer image histories do not improve ball forecasting, indicating that representations exploit scene context rather than rely solely on inter-frame motion. Finally, we propose a conditional diffusion model to generate whole-body kinematic tennis motion from vision encoder predictions on egocentric video at real-time rates, adapting movements as predictions are refined. These results move towards a deeper understanding of how foundation vision models can support real-time dynamic robots using egocentric video.

items.title: RESPLE2: Inertial-Informed Recursive Non-Uniform Spline Estimation for Multi-Sensor Odometry with Global Refinement
items.abstract: We present RESPLE2, a recursive multi-sensor state estimation framework using non-uniform B-splines for 6-DoF motion representation. By exploiting the knot-clamping boundary property, we propose a theoretically grounded mechanism for exact control-point prediction directly informed by inertial kinematics along the trajectory, with knot placement adapted to motion and measurement availability. Within an iterated extended Kalman filter, we perform this prediction using a subset of inertial measurements. A subsequent reset step preserves trajectory consistency as the knots extend. The update step further incorporates heterogeneous sensor measurements at their native timestamps through continuous-time observation models, supporting flexible combinations of LiDARs, cameras, inertial measurement units, and leg kinematics. We further develop a lightweight global optimization module that directly refines non-uniform B-spline control points by incorporating loop-closure constraints derived from LiDAR-visual cues. We conduct extensive evaluations on public and experimental datasets across handheld, tracked, legged, and hybrid aerial-legged platforms, covering highly dynamic maneuvers with extreme accelerations. Compared with state-of-the-art multi-sensor odometry systems, RESPLE2 achieves competitive or superior estimation accuracy and robustness in the corresponding sensor configurations, particularly under aggressive motion, while maintaining real-time operation. We publicly release our code and experimental datasets at https://github.com/ASIG-X/RESPLE2.
items.titleKo: RESPLE2: 전역 정제 기능을 갖춘 관성 정보 기반 재귀적 비균일 B-스플라인 추정을 이용한 다중 센서 오도메트리
items.abstractKo: 우리는 6자유도(6-DoF) 동작 표현을 위해 비균일 B-스플라인을 사용하는 재귀적 다중 센서 상태 추정 프레임워크 RESPLE2를 제시한다. 매듭 클램핑(knot-clamping) 경계 특성을 활용하여 궤적을 따라 관성 기반 운동학에 의해 직접 정보가 제공되는 제어점의 정확한 예측을 위한 이론적 근거를 갖춘 메커니즘을 제안하고, 매듭 배치는 운동과 측정의 가용성에 맞춰 조정된다. 반복형 확장 칼만 필터 내에서 우리는 관성 측정의 부분집합을 사용해 이 예측을 수행한다. 이후의 리셋 단계는 매듭이 확장될 때 궤적 일관성을 보존한다. 업데이트 단계

items.title: EgoThumb: A Vision-Driven Supernumerary Robotic Thumb for Autonomous Grasp and Holding Assistance
items.abstract: Supernumerary robotic fingers augment human dexterity by enabling a single hand to perform complex "hold-and-manipulate" tasks that typically require bimanual coordination. However, existing devices are often hindered by bulky hardware that limits interaction to large objects and rely on explicit hand motion triggers that lack environmental context. To address these challenges, we present EgoThumb, a fully open-source, vision-driven supernumerary robotic thumb. EgoThumb features a compact, dual tendon-driven finger whose actuation is relocated to the forearm, reducing distal weight while enabling precise active joint control. The system utilizes a visual imitation learning policy that maps egocentric images from a palm-facing camera directly to continuous joint positions. By implicitly decoding human intent from visual cues capturing both the hand and the object of interest, EgoThumb achieves robust autonomous manipulation and strong generalization across diverse users and environments. All hardware designs and software implementations are fully open-sourced at https://ego-thumb.github.io.
items.titleKo: EgoThumb: 자율 파지 및 고정 보조를 위한 비전 기반 여분 로봇 엄지
items.abstractKo: 여분의 로봇 손가락은 일반적으로 양손 조작이 필요한 복잡한 '잡고-조작' 작업을 단일 손으로 수행할 수 있게 해 인간의 기민성을 향상시킨다. 그러나 기존 장치들은 종종 거대한 하드웨어로 인해 상호작용이 큰 물체로 제한되고, 환경 문맥이 결여된 명시적 손 동작 트리거에 의존한다. 이러한 문제를 해결하기 위해, 우리는 완전 오픈소스이자 비전 구동 방식의 여분 로봇 엄지 EgoThumb를 제안한다. items.title: Learning Visuomotor Quadrotor Flight Through Dynamic Narrow Gaps via Differentiable Simulation
items.abstract: Threading a quadrotor through a moving narrow gap is a demanding test of agile flight, requiring centimeter-level spatial alignment and precise temporal execution. We address this challenge using a control policy that operates directly on onboard visual and inertial measurements to output collective thrust and body-rate commands. The task is difficult because success lies on a thin feasible manifold: small errors in timing, position, attitude, or visual observability cause collision. Prior planning and learning methods rely on privileged state, teachers, planners, or distillation; learning dynamic narrow-gap traversal directly, from scratch, remains open. We introduce a differentiable moving-gap formulation that gates centering, alignment, and smooth collision terms by signed distance to a time-varying gap plane, turning a sparse traversal event into a dense pathwise objective. We integrate this formulation into a visual-feature-to-command policy trained in one stage from random initialization, without a teacher, planner, or distillation. We validate our approach in both synthetic and real-world experiments. In controlled benchmarks, we demonstrate that pathwise gradients significantly outperform score-function gradients for precision-critical tasks, yielding a 99.3% success rate in simulation after only a few minutes of training on a single GPU. Furthermore, the policy transfers directly to a real quadrotor, successfully crossing a dynamic narrow gap from varied initial conditions using onboard sensing and inertial measurements, achieving an 80% success rate over 10 physical trials.
items.titleKo: 미분 가능 시뮬레이션을 통한 동적 협소 통로 통과 시각-운동 쿼드로터 비행 학습
items.abstractKo: 움직이는 좁은 틈을 쿼드로터가 통과하는 과제는 민첩한 비행 능력을 평가하는 고난도 시험으로, 센티미터 수준의 공간 정렬과 정밀한 시간적 수행을 요구한다. 우리는 온보드 시각 및 관성 측정값을 직접 입력으로 사용해 집합 추력과 자세 각속도 명령을 출력하는 제어 정책으로 이 문제에 접근한다. 이 과제는 성공이 가능한 영역이 매우 좁은 실행 가능 매니폴드 상에 놓여 있기 때문에 어렵다: 타이밍, 위치, 자세 또는 시각적 관측성의 작은 오차도 충돌을 초래한다. 이전의 계획 및 학습 방법들은 특권적 상태, 교사, 플래너 또는 지식 증류에 의존한다; learning dyn

items.title: Kinematic Constraint-Referenced Evaluation for Articulated Object Manipulation
items.abstract: Manipulation policies are evaluated predominantly by binary task success, which cannot tell whether the commanded gesture is the one the object's kinematics admit. We introduce Constraint-Referenced Strategy (CRS), which projects the commanded end-effector twist onto the object's joint axis, separating progress along the joint from off-constraint waste. CRS requires a joint model and a joint-following scripted controller derived from it, but no recorded demonstration or learned judge. On 74 simulated articulated objects, success registers three transfer failures as lower rates but attributes none, while the two CRS channels give each a distinct signature. A door-trained behavior-cloning policy opens drawers in 59 of 110 episodes, and in these passes it commands about $40\times$ the off-axis rotation of a drawer-trained policy's passes ($1.27$ vs.\ $0.032$~rad/s). Relative to a scripted controller scored with the same axis, CRS verdicts are unchanged under joint-axis errors up to $30^\circ$; absolute thresholds tolerate about $8^\circ$.
items.titleKo: 관절형 객체 조작을 위한 운동학 제약 기반 평가
items.abstractKo: 조작 정책은 주로 이진적 과제 성공으로 평가되어, 명령된 동작이 객체의 운동학이 허용하는 동작인지 판단할 수 없다. 우리는 명령된 엔드이펙터의 트위스트를 객체의 관절 축으로 사영하여 관절을 따라 진행된 부분과 제약을 벗어난 낭비를 분리하는 제약-참조 전략(Constraint-Referenced Strategy, CRS)을 제안한다. CRS는 관절 모델과 이로부터 도출된 관절 추종 스크립트 제어기를 요구하지만, 기록된 시연이나 학습된 판정기는 필요로 하지 않는다. 74개의 시뮬레이션된 관절형 객체에서, 성공은 세 가지 전이 실패를 낮은 비율로 기록하지만 n에 귀속시킨다.

items.title: When, Where, and What to Correct: Human-Guided Adaptive Residual Correction for Robot Policies
items.abstract: Imitation policies that reliably execute most of a manipulation trajectory can still fail in localized regions requiring last-mile precision. Updating the full policy or exploring residual actions everywhere treats this local failure as a global learning problem. We introduce Adaptive Residual Correction (ARC), a lightweight post-training module that uses reinforcement learning (RL) to learn a residual correction on top of a frozen policy while using sparse human corrections to structure autonomous exploration. Rather than treating human corrections as imitation targets, ARC uses pre-intervention states to determine 'when' residual control should become active and correction geometry to determine 'where' in residual action space autonomous refinement should explore; task reward determines 'what' residual is ultimately executed. Across three precision-manipulation tasks on a real robot, ARC improves average task success from 33.3% to 75.0%. The human corrections define task-dependent 2-3 dimensional subspaces of the seven-joint residual space that retain 96.0-97.7% of squared correction magnitude. Together, these results show that sparse human corrections can localize and constrain autonomous post-training without requiring the observed correction itself to serve as the final action target.
items.titleKo: 언제, 어디서, 무엇을 수정할 것인가: 로봇 정책을 위한 인간 지도 적응형 잔차 보정(ARC)
items.abstractKo: 조작 궤적의 대부분을 안정적으로 수행하는 모방 정책이라도 마지막 단계의 정밀성을 요구하는 국소적 구간에서는 여전히 실패할 수 있다. 전체 정책을 업데이트하거나 모든 구간에서 잔차 행동을 탐색하는 접근은 이러한 국소적 실패를 전역적 학습 문제로 취급한다. 우리는 Adaptive Residual Correction(ARC)를 소개한다. ARC는 경량의 사후 학습 모듈로, 동결된 정책 위에서 잔차 보정을 학습하기 위해 강화학습(RL)을 사용하며, 희소한 인간의 교정을 활용해 자율 탐색의 구조를 잡는다. 인간의 교정을 단순한 모방 대상(imitation targets)으로 취급하는 대신, ARC는 pre-intervent... (원문이 중단됨)

items.title: Rendering-Free Event Frame Simulation for Fast Reinforcement Learning of Autonomous Robot Navigation
items.abstract: Event cameras offer low latency, high dynamic range, and milliwatt-level power consumption, making them ideal for agile robots such as tiny drones navigating through cluttered environments. However, existing simulators generally render photorealistic images before converting them into events, making large-scale reinforcement learning prohibitively slow. We propose an analytic event simulator that exploits what event cameras fundamentally measure - moving contrast edges - to synthesize event streams directly from scene geometry and ego-motion without visual rendering. Our simulator generates a 64x64 event observation in 17 microseconds on a single GPU - over 400x faster than a state-of-the-art rendering pipeline - enabling end-to-end reinforcement learning for goal-directed obstacle avoidance to converge in under 30 minutes - three orders of magnitude faster than training on rendered events. Policies transfer zero-shot to physically based event simulations (ray-traced Isaac Sim). Our policy reaches 83% success in cluttered courses unseen during training (mid-difficulty, traversability probability approx. 0.57), at 2.4 m/s average goal velocity, and retains 70% in a simulated texture-dense indoor hall. Furthermore, we quantized the policy to a 1.2 MB int8 network running fully onboard a 56-gram Crazyflie equipped with a Prophesee GenX320 event camera and an OpenMV N6 microcontroller board. Without any fine-tuning, external processing, or positioning, the policy achieves an average success rate of 82% (5/5, 5/6, 4/6 flights) across three real-world obstacle courses of increasing difficulty. Code: https://github.com/tudelft/rendering-free-event-nav
authors: Guido C. H. E. de Croon
items.titleKo: 렌더링 없는 이벤트 프레임 시뮬레이션을 이용한 자율 로봇 내비게이션의 고속 강화학습
items.abstractKo: 이벤트 카메라는 저지연, 높은 동적 범위, 밀리와트 수준의 전력 소모를 제공하여 복잡한 환경을 항해하는 소형 드론과 같은 민첩한 로봇에 적합하다. 그러나 기존 시뮬레이터는 일반적으로 포토리얼리스틱 이미지를 렌더링한 후 이를 이벤트로 변환하므로 대규모 강화학습을 수행하기에는 속도가 매우 느리다. 우리는 이벤트 카메라가 근본적으로 측정하는 것—움직이는 명암 경계(moving contrast edges)—을 활용하여 시각적 렌더링 없이 장면 기하와 에고 모션(ego-motion)으로부터 직접 이벤트 스트림을 합성하는 해석적 이벤트 시뮬레이터를 제안한다. 우리 시뮬레이터는 ...

items.title: Predict the Swing, Match the Speed: Robotic Pipe Stabbing With Learned Stereo Vision and Residual Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: A joint of pipe run into the hole swings from the elevator over the well and strikes a fixed stabbing guide at whatever speed the swing has. StabBot, a robotic stabbing system, predicts the swing and meets the pipe at its own speed. A pendulum Kalman filter tuned from the pipe tally tracks the joint in stereo images. A six-axis arm with an open V-shaped roller head closes in at matched velocity, confirms the last millimetres by touch, aims the pin over the box when the elevator hangs off centre, and follows the block down with lateral compliance. A ResNet-18 keypoint network locates the pipe, pin nose and box mouth in 3-D, and a residual reinforcement-learning policy refines the capture. On 200 paired random jobs with nine sizes from 2-3/8-in. tubing to 20-in. casing, StabBot seated every joint with the pipe touching only rollers, against 74% for a conventional fixed guide. Median contact speed fell from 18.4 to 2.3 cm/s and median peak head-pipe force from 11.3 to 1.4 kN, and the force was lower in all 200 jobs (Wilcoxon $p < 10^{-30}$). The network locates the pipe with 0.4-mm median error in 2.3 ms per stereo pair. With the network in the loop, success stayed at 100% under 20 mm of added noise, 300-ms delay, 85% frame loss, 20-mm calibration offset, 20-cm elevator offset and 40-cm swings. All results come from a 1:4 Froude-scaled MuJoCo model and are reported at full scale.
items.titleKo: 흔들림을 예측하고 속도를 일치시킨다: 학습 기반 스테레오 비전과 잔여 강화학습을 이용한 로봇 파이프 삽입
items.abstractKo: 홀로 투입되는 파이프 조인트는 엘리베이터에서 우물 위로 진자처럼 흔들리며 그 흔들림의 속도로 고정된 삽입 가이드를 타격한다. StabBot이라 불리는 로봇 삽입 시스템은 진자 운동을 예측하고 파이프의 속도에 맞춰 대응한다. 파이프 대장(tally)으로 보정된 진자형 칼만 필터가 스테레오 영상에서 조인트를 추적한다. 오픈 V형 롤러 헤드를 장착한 6축 암은 속도를 맞춰 접근하고, 마지막 몇 밀리미터는 접촉으로 확인하며, 엘리베이터가 중심에서 벗어나 매달려 있을 때는 핀을 박스 위로 정렬하고, 블록이 내려갈 때는 측면 컴플라이언스로 함께 따라간다.
