items.title: Which Hand Was Late? Diagnosis for Robot Failure Recovery in Bimanual Tool Use
items.abstract: Failure diagnosers for robot manipulation are increasingly vision--language models (VLMs), trained and evaluated on single-arm failures produced by perturbing a successful demonstration. Bimanual tool use adds failures of other kinds: a tool that slips out of its socket while still held, two correct gestures made at different times, and attempts that fail for two reasons at once. On a simulated bimanual tool-use task whose failure causes are read from the recorded trace, we measure what each sensing channel lets a diagnoser tell. The tool's slip is read on the tool hand; which hand was late is read on both arms, while a sensor on one hand reads its own hand's delay and at most part of the other's; and whether a late attempt was also pushed too weakly is not identifiable from passive sensing when the tool hand is late. Within two attempts, a repair policy that escalates when the cause is not identifiable repairs as many failures as one told the true cause. A VLM's internal state carries the late hand almost perfectly, along a direction no closer to the one its answer reads than a random one; whether the answer reports it depends on the wording of the question.
items.titleKo: 어느 손이 늦었나? 양손 공구 사용에서의 로봇 실패 복구 진단
items.abstractKo: 로봇 조작의 실패 진단기는 점점 비전-언어 모델(VLM)이 되고 있으며, 이는 성공적인 시연에 섭동을 가해 생성된 단일 팔 실패를 대상으로 학습·평가된다. 양손 공구 사용은 다른 유형의 실패를 추가한다: 공구가 여전히 잡혀 있는 상태에서 소켓에서 미끄러져 나오는 경우, 두 개의 올바른 동작이 서로 다른 시점에 수행되는 경우, 그리고 두 가지 이유로 동시에 실패하는 시도. 기록된 트레이스에서 실패 원인을 읽어낼 수 있는 시뮬레이션된 양손 공구 사용 과제에서, 우리는 각 센싱 채널이 진단기에게 어떤 정보를 제공하는지를 측정한다. 공구의 미끄러짐은 공구를 쥔 손에서 읽히며; 어느 손이 늦었는지는

items.title: Leveraging Distributed Sensing and Hyperdimensional Computing for Non-Line-of-Sight Passive Object Sensing
items.abstract: In smart factory environments, passive entities such as humans and movable obstacles may interfere with autonomous robot operations, posing significant safety risks. Detecting potential conflicts between robots and entities outside their field-of-view (FoV) is therefore of paramount importance. However, conventional passive object detection systems rely on sensors such as LiDAR, radar, or cameras, which operate under direct line-of-sight (LoS) and are limited by obstacles and occlusions. To overcome these limitations, integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) enables environmental perception via the communication infrastructure thanks to cooperation among distributed wireless devices. In this paper, we propose a framework for passive entity sensing beyond the robot's FoV that relies solely on distributed channel measurements from the communication infrastructure to perform risk-aware classification. These measurements are embedded into high-dimensional representations using hyperdimensional computing (HDC), enabling robust and scalable learning without explicit channel reconstruction. Numerical simulations based on a commercial ray tracer and ROS-based validation in realistic smart factory scenarios demonstrate improved safety and enhanced path planning with up to 89% accuracy under severe occlusions, while maintaining low computational complexity.
items.titleKo: 분산 센싱과 초차원 컴퓨팅을 활용한 비시선 수동 객체 감지
items.abstractKo: 스마트 팩토리 환경에서는 사람이나 이동 가능한 장애물과 같은 수동적 객체가 자율 로봇의 작동을 방해하여 심각한 안전 위험을 초래할 수 있다. 따라서 로봇의 시야(Field-of-View, FoV) 밖에 있는 객체와 로봇 간의 잠재적 충돌을 감지하는 것이 매우 중요하다. 그러나 기존의 수동 객체 감지 시스템은 LiDAR, 레이더, 카메라 등과 같은 센서에 의존하며, 이러한 센서들은 직접적인 시선(Line-of-Sight, LoS) 하에서만 동작하므로 장애물과 가림 현상에 의해 제약을 받는다. 이러한 한계를 극복하기 위해 통합 센싱 및 통신(Integrated Sensing and Communication, ISAC)은 환경 인식을 가능하게 한다.

items.title: World Dreamer v5-lite: A Multi-Robot World Action Model with One Dreamer
items.abstract: Multi-robot control requires integrating distributed camera views while predicting separate action sequences. Most vision-language-action and world-action models target one robot. Combining multiple views alone does not establish spatial correspondence between them. World Dreamer v5-lite is a multi-robot world-action model built around a shared world state for robot-specific action prediction. Calibrated features from a pretrained video encoder populate this state in workspace coordinates; its spatial size remains fixed as views are added. A vision-language model provides scene context and one query per robot. The queries read the shared state and exchange pose-aware information, while their action streams remain separate. Masked-view cooperative training withholds selected camera views from both visual branches while retaining all action targets. This encourages the use of observations shared by other robots. Pretraining uses more than 10,000 hours of trajectories from 20 simulated robot types, RoboFactory, and real robots. On RoboFactory, World Dreamer v5-lite achieves 74.0% mean success, 23.7 percentage points above the strongest evaluated baseline. Across four real-robot tasks, it reaches 78.8% mean success, a margin of 13.8 points. It also reaches 58.08% overall on RoboCasa365.
items.titleKo: World Dreamer v5-lite: 하나의 Dreamer로 다중 로봇 월드 액션을 처리하는 모델
items.abstractKo: 다중 로봇 제어는 분산된 카메라 뷰를 통합하면서 로봇별로 별도의 동작 시퀀스를 예측해야 한다. 대부분의 비전-언어-액션 및 월드-액션 모델은 단일 로봇을 대상으로 한다. 단순히 여러 뷰를 결합하는 것만으로는 뷰들 간의 공간적 대응관계가 성립하지 않는다. World Dreamer v5-lite는 로봇별 동작 예측을 위해 공유되는 월드 상태(shared world state)를 중심으로 구성된 다중 로봇 월드-액션 모델이다. 사전 학습된 비디오 인코더로부터 얻은 보정된 특징들이 작업공간 좌표계로 이 상태를 채우며, 뷰가 추가되어도 그 공간적 크기는 고정된다. 비전-언어 모델은 장면 컨텍스트와 그리고 하나

items.title: Ego-CEVR: Learning Cross-Embodiment Visual Representations from Human Egocentric Videos
items.abstract: As egocentric video becomes increasingly available for embodied learning, an important research question is how to turn this low-cost, scalable source of data into robot manipulation capabilities. Egocentric videos naturally provide rich context for high-level task understanding, while real-robot demonstrations with wrist observations and action annotations provide supervision for fine-grained action alignment. We present Ego-CEVR, a data-native framework for hierarchical visual representation learning that assigns distinct learning objectives to global and interaction representations. The global module learns object relations, task state, and temporal progress through future prediction on egocentric video. The Interaction module interprets wrist observations in global context and learns local alignment and contact cues through robot action supervision. Separate residual paths expose both representations to the action policy, preserving direct access to task context alongside fine-grained execution information. Ego-CEVR supports independent pretraining of its global video module on large-scale human egocentric videos and videos from diverse robot embodiments, without requiring robot action labels or paired wrist observations.
items.titleKo: Ego-CEVR: 인간 일인칭 영상으로부터의 이종 신체성 간 시각 표현 학습
items.abstractKo: 일인칭 비디오(egocentric video)가 체화 학습에 점차 널리 활용됨에 따라, 이 저비용·확장 가능한 데이터 원천을 로봇의 조작 능력으로 전환하는 방법이 중요한 연구 과제로 떠오르고 있다. 일인칭 영상은 고수준 작업 이해를 위한 풍부한 문맥을 자연스럽게 제공하는 반면, 손목 관측과 행동 주석이 포함된 실제 로봇 시연은 세부 동작 정렬을 위한 지도 신호를 제공한다. 본 논문에서는 전역 표현(global representations)과 상호작용 표현(interaction representations)에 각각 구별된 학습 목표를 할당하는 데이터 기반(data-native) 계층적 시각 표현 학습 프레임워크인 Ego-CEVR을 제안한다. (요약 원문이 중단됨)

items.title: Autonomous fixed-wing interception using reinforcement learning
items.abstract: Medium altitude, long endurance unmanned aerial systems such as Shahed-type strike drones are an unanswered threat in modern conflicts. Conventional air defense systems are too expensive to provide a feasible large-scale solution. Quadcopter interceptors are a cheap, battle-proven alternative, but their extremely limited flight time restricts them to low altitude targets at short range, whereas fixed-wing platforms have the endurance to reach higher altitude targets from longer distances. However, such interceptors are still operated manually. Recent developments in learning-based controllers show potential for automation. In this work, a fixed-wing interceptor is presented that is controlled by a neural network that maps filtered monocular vision observations directly to actuator commands. The policy was trained in a custom Python environment using reinforcement learning and proximal policy optimization. The policy was then deployed on a fixed-wing platform and tested in real interception scenarios. As a baseline, two classical guidance controllers were also developed and tested in simulation. The policy is able to intercept targets both in simulation and in real flight. In simulation, the policy outperforms the classical controllers under most conditions. The interceptor was ultimately successfully validated in real flight by intercepting maneuvering fixed-wing targets. This novel system shows the potential of artificial intelligence for autonomous control of fixed-wing interceptor drones.
items.titleKo: 강화학습을 이용한 자율 고정익 요격
items.abstractKo: 중고도 장시간 체공 무인항공체계(예: 샤헤드형 공격 드론)는 현대 분쟁에서 대응책이 마련되지 않은 위협이다. 재래식 대공 방어체계는 비용이 지나치게 높아 대규모로 실현 가능한 해결책을 제공하지 못한다. 쿼드콥터 요격기는 저비용에 실전 검증된 대안이지만, 극히 제한된 비행 시간으로 인해 단거리의 저고도 표적에만 국한된다. 반면 고정익 플랫폼은 더 긴 체공시간을 바탕으로 더 먼 거리에서 고고도 표적에 도달할 수 있다. 그러나 이러한 요격기들은 여전히 수동으로 운용된다. 학습 기반 제어기들에 대한 최근의 발전

items.title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning of Co-Adaptive Hip Exoskeleton Control (MARL-Exo) for Metabolic Energy Reduction
items.abstract: Objective: This study aims to determine whether a hip-exoskeleton policy trained in simulation, by co-adapting with a musculoskeletal human model under a metabolic-energy reward, reduces the metabolic cost of walking in new users without per-user tuning, and how mechanical-power shaping affects the learned assistance. Methods: We developed MARL-Exo, a multi-agent reinforcement learning framework in which a full-body human model (304 muscle actuators; randomized anatomy, gait, and speed) and a bilateral hip-exoskeleton policy are trained concurrently in two stages. The exoskeleton observes only delayed hip kinematics and its past commands; its reward includes muscle metabolic power from a physiologically based energetics model, alone (Metabolic) or with mechanical-power shaping (Metabolic + Power). The Metabolic policy was deployed and tested without retraining in eight healthy adults walking at 1.25 m/s, using indirect calorimetry. Results: In simulation, the Metabolic policy reduced modeled muscle metabolic power by 13.8% relative to no-device walking, versus 8.8% for Metabolic + Power. On hardware, MARL-Exo reduced net metabolic rate by 18.3 $\pm$ 6.6% relative to Passive in all eight participants. Relative to No-Exo, the mean reduction was 7.4 $\pm$ 10.0%; six participants more than offset the 13.1% device-wearing penalty, walking up to 24.2% below their No-Exo cost. Conclusion: A metabolically informed policy co-adapted in simulation transferred to users without per-user tuning and consistently reduced the metabolic cost of walking with the device, while explicit power shaping reduced the simulated benefit. Significance: Unlike per-user human-in-the-loop optimization, this approach yields a single population-level controller and allows assistance objectives to be screened in simulation before human testing.
items.titleKo: 대사 에너지 감소를 위한 공동 적응형 고관절 외골격 제어의 다중 에이전트 강화학습(MARL-Exo)
items.abstractKo: 목적: 본 연구는 대사 에너지 보상을 사용하여 근골격계 인간 모델과 공동 적응(co-adapting)하면서 시뮬레이션에서 학습된 고관절 외골격 정책이, 사용자별 튜닝 없이 신규 사용자의 보행 대사비용을 감소시키는지와 기계적 동력 셰이핑이 학습된 보조에 어떤 영향을 미치는지를 규명하고자 한다. 방법: 우리는 MARL-Exo를 개발하였다. 이는 전신 인간 모델(304개의 근육 구동기; 해부학, 보행 및 속도를 무작위화)과 양측 고관절 외골격 정책이 두 단계로 동시에 학습되는 다중 에이전트 강화학습 프레임워크이다. 외골격은 오직

items.title: AuRaSim: A Ray-Tracing Based Automotive FMCW Radar Simulator for Dynamic Scenarios
items.abstract: Modern simulators can generate synthetic camera and LiDAR data with accurate annotations for downstream tasks. In contrast, automotive radar simulation remains less mature because it requires not only a 3D engine to model dynamic objects in the scenes but also electromagnetic material properties, antenna configurations, wave propagation mechanisms, and coherent signal synthesis. Existing frameworks are either proprietary or overly simplified, limiting the scalability of radar raw measurements. This paper presents AuRaSim, a ray-tracing-based automotive frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar simulation framework for dynamic scenarios. Rather than implementing all components from scratch, AuRaSim builds on Blender for efficient dynamic-scene construction and Sionna RT for graphics processing unit (GPU) accelerated electromagnetic ray tracing, while introducing radar-specific adaptations for path-resolved propagation with complex coefficients, motion-aware Doppler modeling, and subsequently coherent multi-channel analog-to-digital converter (ADC) cube synthesis based on waveform configurations. Quantitative comparison between simulated and measured range-Doppler maps in digital-twin scenarios achieves a root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 0.147 and a peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) of 16.93 dB, demonstrating the accuracy and fidelity of the synthetic signal. AuRaSim therefore provides a complete and extensible platform for reproducible automotive radar simulation and research. Project homepage: https://wangzhaoze.github.io/aurasim.
items.titleKo: AuRaSim: 동적 시나리오를 위한 레이 트레이싱 기반 자동차용 FMCW 레이더 시뮬레이터
items.abstractKo: 현대의 시뮬레이터는 합성 카메라와 LiDAR 데이터를 다운스트림 작업을 위한 정확한 어노테이션과 함께 생성할 수 있다. 반면, 자동차 레이더 시뮬레이션은 장면 내 동적 객체를 모델링하는 3D 엔진뿐만 아니라 전자기적 물질 특성, 안테나 구성, 전파 전달 메커니즘 및 코히어런트 신호 합성도 요구되기 때문에 아직 덜 성숙하다. 기존 프레임워크는 독점적이거나 지나치게 단순화되어 있어 레이더 원시 측정값의 확장성을 제한한다. 본 논문은 AuRaSim을 제시하는데, 이는 레이 트레이싱 기반의 자동차 주파수 변조 연속파(FMCW

items.title: Learning Quality-Controllable Robot Policies with Iterative Hindsight Relabeling
items.abstract: Robot policy evaluation often relies on a binary success signal for task completion. In real-world deployment, however, desired execution behaviors are also defined by quality attributes such as execution speed and motion smoothness, which need to be dynamically controlled according to task requirements. To address this, we introduce Quality-Controllable Policy (QCP), a robot policy that enables inference-time control over both individual quality attributes and their combinations. To extend the controllable quality range beyond initial demonstrations, we further propose an iterative hindsight relabeling loop: QCP collects online rollouts under target quality labels, adds successful trajectories to the dataset, relabels the accumulated trajectories in hindsight according to their measured quality, and fine-tunes the policy. Experiments on Robomimic and RoboEval demonstrate that QCP consistently improves both task execution quality and success rates across iterations, producing successful rollouts that exceed the quality of the initial demonstrations. Finally, we validate QCP on real-world manipulation tasks, where controlling speed increases throughput in conveyor operations and controlling transport stability improves success when carrying wine glasses, demonstrating that quality-controllable policies yield practical gains in physical deployment.
items.titleKo: 반복적 히인드사이트 재라벨링을 통한 품질 제어 가능한 로봇 정책 학습
items.abstractKo: 로봇 정책 평가는 종종 작업 완료 여부에 대한 이진 성공 신호에 의존한다. 그러나 실제 배치 환경에서는 원하는 실행 행태가 실행 속도나 동작의 매끄러움과 같은 품질 속성으로 정의되며, 이러한 속성들은 작업 요구사항에 맞춰 동적으로 제어되어야 한다. 이를 해결하기 위해 우리는 개별 품질 속성과 이들의 조합을 추론 시점에서 제어할 수 있는 Quality-Controllable Policy(QCP)를 도입한다. 초기 시연을 넘어 제어 가능한 품질 범위를 확장하기 위해, 우리는 반복적 히인드사이트 재라벨링(iterative hindsight relabeling)을 추가로 제안한다.

items.title: PDRVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model with Physical Dynamics Representations
items.abstract: Vision--Language--Action (VLA) models generate robot actions from visual observations and language instructions, but their understanding of physical dynamics remains limited. Video world models can capture scene dynamics, yet generating future videos introduces high latency into the control loop. We introduce PDRVLA, whose lightweight Physical Dynamics Module extracts physical tokens from vision--language features to condition action generation without online video generation. The module learns through direct prediction of future RGB, depth, and optical-flow features, with auxiliary supervision through a frozen pretrained video world model. Training relies entirely on publicly available data, expanded through human-to-robot synthesis, subtask annotation, and embodied chain-of-thought (ECoT) annotation. Across four simulation benchmarks, PDRVLA achieves success rates of 99.3% on LIBERO, 89.9% on LIBERO-Plus, 93.6% on RoboTwin~2.0, and 81.5% on SimplerEnv. Ablations show improved future prediction with world-model supervision and evaluate how subtask conditioning, future object-pose supervision, and ECoT training affect action success.
items.titleKo: PDRVLA: 물리적 동역학 표현을 갖춘 비전-언어-행동 모델
items.abstractKo: 비전-언어-행동(VLA) 모델은 시각 관찰과 언어 지시로부터 로봇 동작을 생성하지만, 물리적 동역학에 대한 이해는 여전히 제한적이다. 비디오 월드 모델은 장면의 동역학을 포착할 수 있으나, 미래 비디오를 생성하면 제어 루프에 높은 지연이 발생한다. 우리는 PDRVLA를 제안한다. 이 모델의 경량 물리 동역학 모듈은 온라인 비디오 생성 없이 비전-언어 특징으로부터 물리 토큰을 추출하여 동작 생성을 조건화한다. 이 모듈은 미래의 RGB, 깊이, 광류 특징을 직접 예측하는 방식으로 학습되며, 보조 감독 신호를 통해 학습된다.

items.title: Learning Force-Reactive Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
items.abstract: Many everyday tasks require controlling contact force as well as motion. On a humanoid, this force must often be coordinated across both hands and the whole body, and cannot be specified by kinematic trajectories alone. Therefore, we present FLORE, a framework for learning force-reactive humanoid loco-manipulation. We collect robot-free demonstrations using two force-sensing UMI-style handheld grippers for hand motion and contact wrenches, and wearable trackers for body motion. A force-reactive diffusion policy takes vision, proprioception, and measured wrenches as input, then predicts actions and per-hand force commands. A hybrid compliance whole-body controller with force tracking executes these commands while maintaining balance: an integral of the force error measured by real force/torque (F/T) sensors lets each hand track force accurately along the commanded direction and remain compliant along the others. In simulation, the controller tracks per-hand force commands of varied magnitude and direction, with little loss in whole-body motion accuracy. Across three contact-rich tasks on the robot, the force-reactive policy succeeds in 80% of rollouts, compared with 26.7% for a position-only policy trained on the same demonstrations and executed by the same controller. For more details, please visit our website: https://louis-leee.github.io/FLoRe/.
items.titleKo: 힘 반응형 휴머노이드 이동·조작 학습
items.abstractKo: 많은 일상 과제는 운동뿐 아니라 접촉력을 함께 제어해야 한다. 휴머노이드에서는 이러한 힘이 종종 양손과 전신에 걸쳐 조정되어야 하며 단순한 기구학적 궤적으로는 지정할 수 없다. 따라서 우리는 힘 반응형 휴머노이드 이동·조작 학습을 위한 프레임워크 FLORE를 제시한다. 손의 동작과 접촉 렌치(힘 및 토크)를 위해 두 개의 힘 센싱 UMI 스타일 휴대형 그리퍼를, 신체 동작을 위해 착용형 트래커를 사용하여 로봇 없이 수행한 시연을 수집한다. 힘 반응형 확산(디퓨전) 정책은 시각 정보, 고유 감각(proprioception) 및 측정된 렌치를 입력으로 받아 행동을 예측한다.

items.title: Differentiable Contact Dynamics for Legged Locomotion: Policy Learning and Contact-Implicit Trajectory Optimization
items.abstract: This paper proposes a smooth analytic gradient for frictional contact and applies it to policy learning and contact-implicit trajectory optimization for legged locomotion. The exact contact sensitivity is available in closed form but describes changes within the current contact mode, providing no first-order information toward neighboring contact modes. The proposed gradient replaces this sensitivity only in the backward pass, leaving the hard-contact forward solve unchanged and the realized rollout feasible. A central-path relaxation of the de Saxcé-corrected second-order-cone complementarity problem for Coulomb friction smooths the conditions defining the separating, clamping, and sliding modes. The relaxed sensitivity is evaluated at a point on the central path obtained by a Newton iteration initialized from the hard-contact solution. The sensitivity remains continuous through contact-mode transitions and converges to the exact sensitivity as the relaxation vanishes. Using 100,000 samples and less than 2 min of training on a desktop PC, policy learning with the proposed gradient produces a policy that transfers to hardware without fine-tuning. On hardware, the robot under a trotting policy withstands pushes and traverses debris and slippery ground. In trajectory optimization, the proposed gradient reaches contact-rich solutions missed by exact and Signorini-relaxed gradients. Project page: https://diffcontact.github.io
items.titleKo: 다족 보행을 위한 미분 가능한 접촉 동역학: 정책 학습 및 접촉-암묵적 궤적 최적화
items.abstractKo: 본 논문은 마찰 접촉에 대해 매끄러운 해석적 기울기를 제안하고 이를 다족 보행을 위한 정책 학습 및 접촉-암묵적 궤적 최적화에 적용한다. 정확한 접촉 민감도는 폐형식으로 얻을 수 있으나 이는 현재 접촉 모드 내의 변화만을 기술하며 인접한 접촉 모드에 대한 일차 정보는 제공하지 않는다. 제안하는 기울기는 역전파 단계에서만 이 민감도를 대체하여 하드 접촉에 대한 순방향 해법은 변경하지 않고 실제 롤아웃의 타당성을 유지한다. de Saxcé 보정된 2차 원뿔 상보성 조건의 중심 경로 완화

items.title: Nonprehensile Robotic Catching Using Virtual Constraints
items.abstract: The problem of nonprehensile robotic catching is addressed using virtual nonholonomic constraints (VNHCs); the motion of the robot end-effector is designed and controlled directly in terms of the states of the object before it is caught on the surface of the end-effector. In contrast to contemporary approaches, our approach avoids the need for object trajectory prediction, and consequent time-varying robot trajectory generation. With a focus on the planar case, we demonstrate that our VNHC approach can be used to catch an object on an end-effector at a desired height, with minimal relative normal velocity at the contact instant. Moreover, the VNHC function depends only on the desired catching height, and the same VNHC can be used for a range of initial conditions. We use model predictive control (MPC) to bring the object and end-effector to rest at a desired location after contact is made. The approach is validated in simulation.
items.titleKo: 가상 제약을 이용한 비파지 로봇 포획
items.abstractKo: 가상 비홀로노믹 제약(VNHCs)을 사용하여 비파지 로봇 포획 문제를 다룬다. 로봇 엔드이펙터의 운동은 엔드이펙터 표면에 물체가 포착되기 전의 물체 상태를 기준으로 직접 설계되고 제어된다. 기존의 접근법과 달리 본 접근법은 물체 궤적 예측 및 그에 따른 시간 가변적 로봇 궤적 생성의 필요를 피한다. 평면 사례에 중점을 두어 본 VNHC 접근법이 원하는 높이에서 엔드이펙터 위에 물체를 포착하는 데 사용될 수 있음을 보이며, 원문이 'with minimal relative nor'에서 중단되어 이후 문장이 생략되어 있습니다.

items.title: OSWAM: An Effective World Action Model with One-Step Action Generation
items.abstract: Direct-policy World Action Models (WAM) have demonstrated the benefits of decoupling action generation from explicit future visual prediction for efficient inference in autonomous driving and embodied control. However, they still require tens of denoising steps to achieve competitive action quality, incurring substantial latency and hindering real-time deployment. Simply reducing the number of denoising steps will collapse the nonlinear multi-step denoising trajectory into coarse updates, substantially degrading action quality. To reduce the denoising steps while enabling real-time action generation, we present an effective world action model with one-step action generation, namely OSWAM, for autonomous driving and embodied control. We argue that it is the absence of structured action priors in random noise initialization that forces direct-policy WAMs to recover coherent action sequences through iterative denoising. Hence, we construct imagination tokens to initialize the diffusion process, providing physical priors and action-conditioned representations. We further introduce privileged information distillation with future conditioning to enhance future-aware action generation. As a result, OSWAM can efficiently and effectively generate high quality actions in just one diffusion step. Our experiments demonstrate that OSWAM achieves comparable or even better results in both autonomous driving and embodied control than direct-policy WAM and Joint-WAM that require tens of steps. It obtains approximately $3\times$ speedup over direct-policy WAM baselines and supports real-time compiled inference with latency as low as 40ms on an NVIDIA RTX 5090 GPU. The project page is available at https://gwenzhang.github.io/OSWAM/
items.titleKo: OSWAM: 한 단계 행동 생성을 이용한 효율적인 월드 액션 모델
items.abstractKo: 직접 정책 기반 월드 액션 모델(Direct-policy WAM)은 자율주행 및 임베디드 제어에서 행동 생성(action generation)을 명시적인 미래 시각 예측(explicit future visual prediction)과 분리함으로써 효율적인 추론의 이점을 보여주었다. 그러나 경쟁력 있는 행동 품질을 달성하려면 여전히 수십 단계의 디노이징(denoising) 단계가 필요하여 상당한 지연을 초래하고 실시간 배포를 방해한다. 디노이징 단계 수를 단순히 줄이면 비선형의 다중 단계 디노이징 궤적이 거친 업데이트로 붕괴되어 행동 품질이 크게 저하된다. 디노이징 단계를 줄이면서 실시간 행동 생성을 가능하게 하기 위해…(원문 일부가 누락되어 있습니다.)

items.title: Profiling a Frontier Agent with EBench: From Direct Control to Harness with Policy
items.abstract: Frontier multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can control robots without robot-specific training, but how their capabilities compare and interact with post-trained vision-language-action (VLA) and world action model (WAM) policies across manipulation demands remains to be thoroughly evaluated. In this report, we evaluate GPT-6-Astra on EBench as the core of an agent that controls a robot through an agent harness under the same visual and proprioceptive observation protocol as post-trained policies. We study two agent configurations: direct control, in which the agent generates waypoint commands directly, and harness with policy, in which it can also invoke a post-trained VLA or WAM policy for action execution. Under direct control, the agent achieves competitive overall performance relative to post-trained policies. It leads on short-horizon tasks and exhibits the least performance variation across generalization dimensions, whereas it underperforms post-trained policies on long-horizon tasks, tabletop manipulation, and high-precision contact-rich tasks. In the harness with policy, invoking a post-trained VLA or WAM combines the complementary strengths of both components, raising overall task success to the level of the strongest compared post-trained policies while substantially reducing token cost. However, performance remains below the per-task upper bound of the standalone components due to suboptimal policy invocation, fixed-instruction execution without subgoals, and grasp disruption when the agent resumes control. Overall, our study characterizes the capability boundary of a frontier MLLM agent and suggests directions for improving future agent harness design. Project page: https://internrobotics.github.io/EBench-Astra-Tech-Report/
items.titleKo: EBench로 프런티어 에이전트 프로파일링: 직접 제어에서 정책 기반 하니스까지
items.abstractKo: 최첨단 다중모달 대형 언어 모델(MLLM)은 로봇 전용 학습 없이도 로봇을 제어할 수 있지만, 이러한 모델의 능력이 조작 과제에 따른 다양한 요구에서 사후 학습된 시각-언어-행동(VLA) 및 세계 행동 모델(WAM) 정책과 어떻게 비교되고 상호작용하는지는 여전히 충분히 평가되지 않았다. 본 보고서에서는 GPT-6-Astra를 EBench에서 평가하여, 사후 학습된 정책과 동일한 시각 및 고유감각 관찰 프로토콜 하에서 에이전트 하니스(agent harness)를 통해 로봇을 제어하는 에이전트의 중심 구성 요소로서 성능을 분석한다. 우리는 두 가지 에이전트 구성──에이전트가 웨이포인트 com

items.title: Pretraining Knows What, Simulation Teaches How: Compositional Generalization in a Sim-Trained Robot Agent
items.abstract: A robot policy needs to understand what a task is asking for in a scene, and how to move the robot to accomplish that task. To achieve these two skills, we introduce Zero-real Agent Policy (ZAP), a recipe that teaches a small off-the-shelf vision-language model to control a robot via a simple tool harness. We use a pretrained 27B parameter model to bootstrap world understanding and reasoning, followed by supervised fine-tuning and GRPO on simple simulated tasks to teach it how to move the robot. Without any real-world robot data during training, ZAP reaches 96.7% success on real-world tasks, matching GPT-6 Astra in our harness and outperforming the MolmoAct2 VLA (33.3%), while running 3x faster and 17x cheaper than GPT-6 Astra. We demonstrate that ZAP also generalizes to completely new objects, goals, strategies, and language by seating a test tube in a rack (and choosing a different hole in the rack when prompted), handing a test tube between arms mid-air, drawing an X on a tic-tac-toe board, and playing chess. These goals and types of manipulation don't appear in our training data. Furthermore, ZAP also transfers to an unseen embodiment. On a single-arm Franka, ZAP reaches 55.9% on RoboLab-120, 4.9 percentage points ahead of the leading VLA/WAM baseline.
items.titleKo: 사전학습은 ‘무엇’을 알고, 시뮬레이션은 ‘어떻게’를 가르친다: 시뮬레이션으로 훈련된 로봇 에이전트의 구성적 일반화
items.abstractKo: 로봇 정책은 장면에서 과제가 무엇을 요구하는지(무엇)와 그 과제를 달성하기 위해 로봇을 어떻게 움직여야 하는지(어떻게)를 이해해야 한다. 이 두 능력을 달성하기 위해, 우리는 Zero-real Agent Policy(ZAP)를 도입한다. items.title: Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning Using Routed Ensembles and Trajectory Attribution
items.abstract: Multi-objective reinforcement learning is a fundamental problem for modern AI, with applications spanning post-training, reasoning models, and robotic control. A central challenge is to learn policies that balance competing objectives, such as helpfulness versus honesty in safety and alignment, or speed versus energy in robotics. The optimal policy can vary sharply with objective-weighting combinations, and the extent of this variation depends crucially on the degree of conflict among objectives, making per-preference policy learning sample-inefficient. In this paper, we introduce objective-conflict coefficients and derive near-optimal regret bounds for online settings using this measure, thereby quantifying the impact of misalignment on learning efficiency. Then, we design routed ensemble policy learning, an algorithm that maintains a small set of basis policies and dynamically routes trajectories to the policy with the highest potential reward. Finally, we consider trajectory selection as another approach to mitigate objective conflict, and design a kernel surrogate trajectory attribution algorithm that estimates how feedback signals from a set of trajectories influence policy learning on other trajectories. The kernel can capture nonlinear interactions such as synergy and antagonism between trajectories. We evaluate our approach across diverse environments and benchmarks: routed ensembles improve average performance by 4.3% over baselines for online environments from Meta-World and MO-Gymnasium, and kernel surrogate attribution improves correlation with leave-one-out analysis over existing baselines by 50%. When applied to trajectory selection, kernel-based attribution yields a 27% improvement in reward over baseline attribution methods.

items.title: SPECOLA: A Tool for Specification Driven Robot Evaluation
items.abstract: Simulation benchmarks are a useful way to measure progress in robotics; typically they provide success rate as the dominant measure of performance. However, success rate reports only whether a rollout completed the task, hiding by what margin it succeeded, how sensitive the success is to goal parameter changes, requirements it may have violated, and whether success persisted. Signal Temporal Logic (STL) provides a formal language for capturing specifications; it can be used to define requirements, and measure how close a robot behavior is to satisfying or violating them. Using STL monitors in a simulator, however, requires exposing simulator state and mapping it to specification-relevant signals. We present Specola, a tool for evaluating robot behaviors in simulation with respect to STL specifications. Specola provides an interface for writing specifications over simulator signals, and creates and manages the relevant monitors while a policy executes. We provide a Python API and command-line interface for integrating monitoring into existing policy execution loops. We provide an adapter interface for connecting new simulators, and provide adapters for nine simulation environments and benchmarks, including LIBERO, RoboCasa, Isaac Lab, and RoboDojo. We provide case studies that illustrate the nuanced evaluation that Specola enables. Code and adapters are available at https://github.com/specola-eval/specola.
items.titleKo: SPECOLA: 사양 기반 로봇 평가 도구
items.abstractKo: 시뮬레이션 벤치마크는 로보틱스의 진척을 측정하는 유용한 수단이다. 일반적으로 성능의 주요 지표로 성공률을 제공한다. 그러나 성공률은 실행이 과업을 완료했는지만 보고하므로, 얼마나 여유 있게 성공했는지, 목표 파라미터 변화에 대한 성공의 민감성, 위반했을 수 있는 요구사항, 그리고 성공이 지속되었는지 여부 등을 드러내지 않는다. items.title: TrySee: Modular Perception-Enhanced VLM Grounding for Closed-Loop Robot Task Planning in Specialized Domains
items.abstract: Vision Language Models (VLMs) have shown impressive capabilities in high-level reasoning and task planning for robots. However, specialized domains remain a challenge for VLMs' image interpretation and grounding abilities. We introduce TrySee, a modular closed-loop robot task planning pipeline integrating general-purpose VLM reasoning with domain-specific perception and established robotics components. The system consists of an inherently reactive cyclic planning pipeline, augmented with domain-specific modular vision preprocessing, to provide online grounding. Finally, a dynamic preprocessing selection mechanism contributes to the scalability of the pipeline. The system requires neither VLM fine-tuning nor end-to-end demonstrations and adapts through replaceable perception modules and motion planning. The approach is evaluated on planning tasks across 5 widely different domains, including a real-world robot disassembly task. The field tests in a brownfield environment demonstrate the approach's practicality in integrating VLM planning into specialized robotic systems with limited domain-specific training data.

items.title: FISRF: Flexible Instructional Scaffolding Reflection Framework for Robotics Task Planning with Large Language Model
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are widely adopted for reflective error correction in task planning; however, existing approaches primarily rely on autonomous exploration, rendering them prone to accumulating erroneous experiences during early interactions with new environments. To address this limitation, we propose the Flexible Instructional Scaffolding Reflection Framework (FISRF), an agent--mentor architecture that estimates the robot's Zone of Proximal Development (ZPD) in task planning and adaptively selects reflection strategies and mentor guidance, thereby facilitating the accumulation of effective error-correction experience. Experiments in ALFWorld and on real-world robotic platforms demonstrate that FISRF reduces the average number of error-correction rounds by 37% and redundant reasoning by 25.1%, while improving the overall task success rate by 8%. Project webpage : https://fisrfplanning.github.io/

items.title: Continuous-Time Safe Planning and Control for Agile Quadrupeds
items.abstract: Agile quadruped navigation in dynamic environments demands trajectories that are both dynamically feasible and provably collision-free. Most real-time planners achieve tractability through a convex reduction that requires simplified kinematic models, discarding motion that the robot can readily execute, and certify safety only at discretization points, leaving open possible inter-sample collisions with moving obstacles. We present a real-time motion planning framework that retains the fully-actuated $SE(2)$ model of a quadruped, with its anisotropic, heading-coupled velocity bounds, and accepts the resulting nonconvexity. By parameterizing trajectories as composite Bernstein polynomials, we exploit the convex hull property to certify collision avoidance and the input bounds over the entirety of each planning horizon. Solved at online replanning rates, the optimization runs in closed loop, commanding body velocities to the locomotion controller. We validate the approach in simulation against ablations and external baselines, and in hardware experiments on a quadruped navigating among unknown moving obstacles, recovering both lateral and heading-coupled motion that simplified models exclude.

items.title: Environment Edits as a Corrective Signal for Reward Learning
items.abstract: Robot corrections allow people to adjust a robot's behavior, but a single correction changes many features. Also, preferences about object attributes and relationships between objects cannot be expressed by moving the robot. We propose environment edits as a complementary form of feedback. The robot's motion is held constant as the human edits the scene, so the only explanation for the edit is the moved object. We introduce Feature Learning from Environmental and Robot-Relational Edit Traces (FERRET), which learns preferences from both robot and environment corrections. We show that environment edits are able to disambiguate features and learn preferences that robot corrections alone cannot.
items.titleKo: 보상 학습을 위한 교정 신호로서의 환경 편집

items.title: VPR-Space: A Benchmark for Visual Place Recognition in Space Analog Domains
items.abstract: Visual Place Recognition (VPR) is an important means for loop closure detection in visual Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM). While state-of-the-art VPR and SLAM approaches excel in urban and feature-rich natural environments, the vast and feature-poor environments of extraterrestrial surfaces like on the Moon or Mars pose severe challenges for existing approaches. This paper presents a novel benchmark, VPR-Space, to evaluate VPR capabilities on extraterrestrial surfaces. There are three contributions: (1) We collected sixteen VPR database-query datasets based on existing data from Space Analog Domains (SAD), terrestrial environments that resemble properties of the Moon or Mars. The collection includes a range of challenges regarding environment, viewpoint change, and illumination conditions. (2) To address the ill-posed nature of VPR, we propose a novel approach to generate the ground-truth information in VPR benchmarks. Instead of defining that a query and datbase image show the same place if and only if their camera poses are within fixed position and viewing direction thresholds, we propose to make the decision dependent on whether the match would be valuable in the downstream SLAM task. To avoid the overhead and restrictions of evaluating VPR in-the-loop within SLAM systems, we provide VPR ground-truth (GT) matrices based on the performance of an ensemble of state-of-the-art Relative Pose Estimators (RPE). Under this GT we require a VPR method to identify exactly those image pairs for which a subsequently applied RPE is expected to provide a valuable pose estimate in a SLAM context. (3) We evaluated nine state-of-the-art VPR approaches. The results show considerable room for improvement and indicate directions for future research. We provide a pre-release version of the dataset on github: $\texttt{https://github.com/rfechner/VPR-Space}$
items.titleKo: VPR-Space: 우주 유사 도메인에서의 시각적 장소 인식 벤치마크
items.abstractKo: 시각적 장소 인식(Visual Place Recognition, VPR)은 비주얼 SLAM(시각 기반 동시적 위치추정 및 지도작성, SLAM)에서 루프 클로저 검출을 위한 중요한 수단이다. 최신 VPR 및 SLAM 기법은 도시 및 특징이 풍부한 자연 환경에서는 우수한 성능을 보이지만, 달이나 화성 같은 외계 표면의 광대하고 특징이 빈약한 환경은 기존 기법에 심각한 도전 과제를 제기한다. 본 논문은 외계 표면에서의 VPR 성능을 평가하기 위한 새로운 벤치마크인 VPR-Space를 제시한다. 기여는 세 가지이다: (1) 우리는 S로부터의 기존 데이터를 기반으로 16개의 VPR 데이터베이스-쿼리 데이터셋을 수집했다

items.title: Adapt for Planning, Not just Prediction: Optimistic Test-Time World Model Adaptation
items.abstract: Latent world models are typically pre-trained offline and kept frozen at test time, so planning with them can degrade under distribution shift. Test-time adaptation (TTA) can mitigate this degradation by updating the model during deployment. Unlike pre-training on fixed data, TTA for planning is closed-loop: the planner uses model rollouts to select actions, and the resulting transitions drive the next update. This raises the question: which objective should guide TTA for planning? Under a prediction-only objective, the model is fit only to the outcomes of its own actions, so it can remain wrong about the actions that would reach the goal, and low prediction error need not translate into better planning. Inspired by reward-biased maximum likelihood from adaptive control, we introduce Optimistic Test-Time Adaptation (OpTTA). Its objective has two terms, the prediction loss on observed transitions and the planner's goal-reaching cost on its candidate rollouts, both minimized over the model parameters. The planning term biases adaptation toward models that are optimistic about reaching the goal, without any additional environment interaction. Across visual and environment shifts on manipulation, reaching and navigation tasks, OpTTA raises final planning success over the frozen model by 13.5 percentage points on average, compared with 6.9 for the prediction-only objective (AdaJEPA), when only the predictor is adapted. When the encoder is adapted as well, the gains are 13.5 and 7.5 points. These experiments span three JEPA world models with different encoders and training objectives and, for temporal straightening, both CEM and gradient-based planners. Our results suggest that test-time adaptation of world models for planning benefits from an optimistic, task-aware term in addition to the prediction loss.
items.titleKo: 예측에만 국한되지 않고 계획을 위해 적응하라: 낙관적 테스트 시 월드 모델 적응
items.abstractKo: 잠재 월드 모델은 일반적으로 오프라인에서 사전학습되고 테스트 시에는 고정된 상태로 유지되므로, 분포 변화 하에서 이를 이용한 계획 성능이 저하될 수 있다. 테스트 시 적응(Test-time adaptation, TTA)은 배포 중 모델을 갱신함으로써 이러한 성능 저하를 완화할 수 있다. 고정된 데이터에 대한 사전학습과 달리, 계획을 위한 TTA는 폐회로(closed-loop)적이다: 플래너는 모델 롤아웃을 사용해 행동을 선택하고, 그로부터 발생한 전이들이 다음 갱신을 유도한다. 이는 다음과 같은 질문을 제기한다: 계획을 위한 TTA는 어떤 목적함수(objective)에 의해 안내되어야 하는가? 예측만을 목표로 할 경우 모델은 오직 자신의 행동으로 얻어진 결과에만 맞춰 학습되므로 계속 잘못된 상태로 남아 있을 수 있다. (원문이 'wro'로 중단됨)

items.title: Revisiting Direct Control: A Field Evaluation of Sensor Fusion Efficacy in Teleoperating Full-Scale Autonomous Vehicles via Bird's Eye View
items.abstract: In autonomous driving, robot teleoperation serves as a critical safety fallback mechanism, requiring operators to assume direct control in the event of system failure. While recent research has pivoted toward high-level supervisory control or simulation-based studies, these approaches often fail to capture the physical dynamics and sensory demands of driving a full-scale vehicle. To address this gap, we evaluated the impact of spatial data representation on operator performance using a real car-sized vehicle in a field experiment with $N = 18$ participants. We compared three visualization interfaces: (i) a standard camera feed baseline, with two bird's-eye views (BEV) from (ii) a raw LiDAR point cloud, and (iii) a sensor fusion of LiDAR and camera data streams. Contrary to prior passive observation studies suggesting that sensor-fusion BEV may hinder awareness, our active-control results demonstrate that such representation significantly outperforms the standard LiDAR BEV in perceived usability ($p \leq 0.0001$) and cognitive task load ($p = 0.01$, NASA-TLX score: 34.58/100) while also being significantly better than the Camera-only view ($p = 0.043$). The fused interface also led to statistically significant reductions in task completion time ($p = 0.0461$) and superior usability (SUS: 77.9/100) compared to those of the Camera-only and LiDAR-only views. By synthesizing objective performance data with comprehensive subjective assessments, we demonstrate that BEV fusion maximizes safety margins while minimizing the operator's mental demand. These findings challenge existing teleoperation conventions and provide an empirically validated approach for designing robust remote piloting systems.
items.titleKo: 직접 제어의 재검토: 버드아이뷰를 통한 풀스케일 자율주행차 원격조작에서 센서 융합 효율성의 현장 평가

items.title: From Language to Drives: A Multimodal Framework for Aligning Autonomous Robots with Human Purposes
items.abstract: This work explores a multimodal approach to the alignment of the behavior of open-ended learning autonomous robots with human purposes through the use of large language models as cultural enablers. While autonomous robots can generate their own skills and goals through interaction with the environment, they often lack mechanisms to ensure that these remain relevant and aligned to those of human users. The proposed approach makes use of the general and cultural knowledge contained in LLMs and VLMs to establish a multimodal interactive alignment process in which human purposes, expressed in natural language, are transformed into motivational components of a robot architecture in the form of robot missions and drives that guide the behavior of the robot. The system is structured into three layers for semantic alignment, mission generation, and drive modeling. This design enables a bidirectional interaction loop: human inputs define high-level purposes, robots expand them into executable missions making use of multimodal information relayed by LLMs and VLMs, and feedback maintains alignment with human intent. Experiments in simulation and with a physical robot demonstrate that the process produces valid missions and behaviors, supporting effective human-agent alignment in interactive scenarios with autonomous robots.
items.titleKo: 언어에서 동기로: 인간의 목적에 정렬된 자율 로봇을 위한 멀티모달 프레임워크
items.abstractKo: 본 연구는 대규모 언어 모델을 문화적 촉진자로 활용하여 개방형 학습을 수행하는 자율 로봇의 행동을 인간의 목적과 정렬하기 위한 멀티모달 접근법을 탐구한다. 자율 로봇은 환경과의 상호작용을 통해 스스로 기술과 목표를 생성할 수 있으나, 이러한 것들이 인간 사용자들의 목적과 계속해서 관련성을 유지하고 정렬되어 있는지를 보장할 메커니즘이 부족한 경우가 많다. 제안된 접근법은 대규모 언어 모델(LLM)과 비전·언어 모델(VLM)에 내재된 일반적·문화적 지식을 활용하여, 자연어로 표현된 인간의 목적을 포함하는 멀티모달 상호작용적 정렬 과정을 수립한다. items.title: Robot-Aligned 3D Gaussian Splatting for Precise Reaching with Wrist-Camera VLA Policies
items.abstract: Efficient robotic data collection remains a major bottleneck for vision-language-action (VLA) policy learning, especially for tasks requiring accurate end-effector positioning and camera-action alignment. This challenge is particularly severe in electronic-waste disassembly, where robots operate in cluttered assemblies of densely packed, visually similar components. Full digital-twin simulation is difficult because many parts are thin, reflective, or mechanically complex, making accurate object-level meshes and contact models difficult to obtain. In this work, we focus on pre-contact reaching and propose a 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)-based data generation pipeline for wrist-camera VLA adaptation. Our method reconstructs the real workspace with 3DGS and renders diverse wrist-camera observations from robot-aligned poses. These observations are paired with smooth, structured reaching trajectories to provide robot-aligned visual-action supervision for VLA fine-tuning. We further augment the VLA policy with an instruction-conditioned reach verifier that estimates target proximity and provides reliable termination before physical interaction. Experiments in motherboard disassembly demonstrate precise VLA-based reaching using wrist-camera observations alone, without an external side-view camera. With $π$0.5, 1,500 generated trajectories achieve 80.0\% precise-reaching success across three targets, compared with 58.7\% using 150 teleoperated demonstrations, while requiring less than 10 minutes of active human capture. Project website: https://001-wang.github.io/PrecisionReach-GS/

items.abstractKo: 효율적인 로봇 데이터 수집은 특히 엔드 이펙터의 정확한 위치 결정과 카메라-행동 정렬이 요구되는 작업에서 비전-언어-행동(VLA) 정책 학습의 주요 병목으로 남아 있다. 이 문제는 밀집하고 시각적으로 유사한 부품들로 이루어진 복잡한 전자 폐기물 해체 작업에서 특히 심각하다. 많은 부품이 얇거나 반사성이 있거나 기계적으로 복잡하여 정확한 객체 수준 메시와 접촉 모델을 얻기 어려워 전체 디지털 트윈 시뮬레이션이 어렵다. 본 연구에서는 접촉 전 도달(pre-contact reaching)에 초점을 맞춘다.

items.title: Context-Aware Generation and Modulation of Expressive Motion Behavior using Multimodal Foundation Models
items.abstract: Expressive robot motion positively impacts human-robot interaction by improving user engagement, likability, or task performance. We present a novel approach to automatically generate and modulate complex, expressive full-body gesture sequences from a multimodal (text, audio, video) context description. Based on a unified mathematical implementation of the Principles of Animation using Dynamic Movement Primitives, we use multimodal foundation models to generate such sequences along with parametric motion variations that are highly context-aware. This method extends the state of the art in terms of flexibility and generality by being interpretable, composable, and working across different robot morphologies. Moreover, we integrate the system into a continuous control framework and leverage knowledge distillation to learn a much smaller model, significantly improving token efficiency and system latency. Results from a user study with a human-like platform indicate that participants judged our system's motions to be better aligned with the interaction context than motions produced under a non-modulated or API-level condition. We also demonstrate how the system generates expressive motion for robots with different kinematics, showcasing its versatility. Paper webpage: https://gen-mod-expressive-motion-behavior.github.io/.

items.title: RoboDoctor: Training-Free Recursive Self-Improvement for Robot Policies
items.abstract: Generalist robot policies and language-model agents provide complementary capabilities, but completing a task also requires adapting their use to the consequences of physical interaction. We study execution as a locus of adaptation: feedback guides the current action and supplies evidence for revising subsequent decisions under fixed model weights. We introduce RoboDoctor, a training-free framework that connects diagnosis, grounded action, and persistent experience across three revision targets. The harness allocates control between policy and agent; intervention determines when to assist while preserving useful policy behavior; and operation refines physical methods through observed effects. Linked experience records retain the reason for a decision, the attempted method, its outcome, and conditions for reuse. On a curated archive of 54 RoboDojo-Sim task entries, RoboDoctor achieves a five-dimension mean score of 57.10, with a native success rate of 49.44%. Recorded interactions illustrate strategy changes, selective correction, and grasp revision. These findings characterize execution-time adaptation in the evaluated system; controlled trials remain necessary to isolate the contribution of cross-episode experience.
items.titleKo: RoboDoctor: 훈련 없이 재귀적으로 자기 개선하는 로봇 정책
items.abstractKo: 범용 로봇 정책과 언어 모델 기반 에이전트는 상호 보완적인 능력을 제공하지만, 작업을 완수하려면 물리적 상호작용의 결과에 따라 이를 활용하는 방식을 적응시키는 것도 필요하다. 우리는 적응의 장으로서 실행을 연구한다: 피드백은 현재 행동을 안내하고 고정된 모델 가중치 하에서 이후 결정들을 수정하기 위한 근거를 제공한다. 우리는 진단, 환경 기반 행동, 그리고 지속적인 경험을 세 가지 수정 대상에 걸쳐 연결하는 훈련 불필요 프레임워크인 RoboDoctor를 소개한다. 이 하니스는 정책과 에이전트 사이의 제어를 할당하고, 개입은 언제 지원할지를 결정하...

items.title: Distributed Predictive Flocking for a Swarm of Miniature Vibration-Driven Robots in a Confined Arena
items.abstract: Coordinating many miniature robots in a confined arena, with no leader, central planner, or global map, is a core challenge for swarm robotics. As the swarm grows denser, collision avoidance becomes the limiting factor, and the number of safely coexisting robots depends on the formulation of the inter-robot safety constraint. We present a distributed predictive flocking controller in which each robot solves its own nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) problem, optimizing swarm cohesion and alignment costs, inter-robot and obstacle safety, and a task objective, while exchanging only predicted trajectories with local neighbors. Within this generalized controller architecture, solved in real time, we compare six barrier and control-barrier-function (CBF) safety formulations on a digital twin of an open-source vibration-driven bristlebot in a $0.64\,\mathrm{m^2}$ arena. A look-ahead discrete-time CBF performs best overall, with the fewest collisions and the widest inter-robot margins across nearly every swarm size tested. We deploy it on phototaxis, phototactic orbiting, and cohesion without a stimulus tasks, using swarm sizes starting from ten robots and up to the geometric packing limit. The swarm holds well: collisions stay low in small swarms, rising steeply as the packing limit approaches, while coordination and cohesion degrade gently rather than collapsing. The swarm is found not to trade safety for order, keeping both across the confined arena, with local alignment high at every swarm size.
items.titleKo: 제한된 공간 내 소형 진동 구동 로봇 군집을 위한 분산 예측 플로킹
items.abstractKo: 리더나 중앙 계획자, 전역 지도가 없는 제한된 공간에서 다수의 소형 로봇을 조정하는 것은 군집 로보틱스의 핵심 과제이다. 군집이 밀집해질수록 충돌 회피가 병목 요인이 되며, 안전하게 공존할 수 있는 로봇 수는 로봇 간 안전 제약의 정식화 방식에 따라 달라진다. 본 연구에서는 각 로봇이 자체 비선형 모델 예측 제어(NMPC) 문제를 해결하여 군집 응집성 및 정렬 비용, 로봇 간 및 장애물에 대한 안전성, 작업 목표를 최적화하는 분산 예측 플로킹 제어기를 제시한다. 각 로봇은 예측 정보만을 교환하면서...

items.title: SceneBloom: Agentic Indoor Environment Generation with Realistic and Diverse Layouts for Embodied Learning
items.abstract: Training generalizable embodied agents requires realistic, varied, and simulation-ready indoor environments. Language-guided methods support semantic planning and object-level reasoning, but precise spatial grounding remains difficult. Visual generative models offer rich priors over plausible arrangements, yet their outputs require geometric reasoning to become physically valid 3D scenes. We introduce SceneBloom, an agentic framework that combines visual layout sampling with contract-guided 3D compilation. A hierarchical sampler uses diffusion priors to generate furniture arrangements within functional zones. A compiler then uses relations extracted from each proposal to guide geometric fitting and local pose correction. Across five room types, SceneBloom attains the highest visual quality and physical stability among the compared methods and is the only method with no detected mesh collisions and out-of-bounds objects. Its layouts are also closer to the distribution of real rooms than those of all compared baselines. Object navigation policies trained in these realistic scenes achieve a higher success rate in held-out real scans than those trained on an equal number of real training scans. Code is available at https://github.com/Tinaliu0123/scenebloom.

items.abstractKo: 일반화 가능한 체현 에이전트를 훈련하려면 현실적이고 다양하며 시뮬레이션 사용에 바로 적합한 실내 환경이 필요하다. 언어 유도 방법은 시맨틱(의미적) 계획과 객체 수준 추론을 지원하지만, 정밀한 공간적 그라운딩은 여전히 어렵다. 비주얼 생성 모델은 그럴듯한 배치에 대한 풍부한 선험적 지식을 제공하지만, 그 출력물을 물리적으로 유효한 3D 장면으로 만들려면 기하학적 추론이 필요하다. 우리는 SceneBloom을 소개한다. SceneBloom은 시각적 배치 샘플링과 규약(컨트랙트) 기반 3D 컴파일을 결합한 에이전트 주도형 프레임워크다. 계층적 샘플러는 확산 선험을 사용하여 가구 배치를 within f

items.title: RobustRLlib: A Unified Library and Benchmark for Robust Reinforcement Learning Algorithms
items.abstract: Robust reinforcement learning (RL) is critical for reliable real-world deployment, where policies may fail under diverse shifts and disruptions. Existing robust RL algorithms offer a rich set of mechanisms and principles, yet two major barriers limit their broader potential: limited algorithm reusability and an unclear empirical capability boundary. We introduce RobustRLlib, an algorithm-centric library and benchmark that addresses both challenges. It integrates 17 representative robust online, offline, and safe RL algorithms under a unified interface for substantially improved reusability, together with an enhanced evaluation platform spanning diverse real-world shifts and advanced humanoid and vision-language-action tasks. Systematic evaluation over 273 perturbation configurations provides an up-to-date capability map of current robust RL algorithms, revealing where they remain effective and where substantial robustness gaps persist. As an open-source, user-friendly platform, RobustRLlib offers a reproducible and extensible codebase for applying existing methods to new problems and developing new robust RL algorithms.
items.titleKo: RobustRLlib: 강건한 강화학습 알고리즘을 위한 통합 라이브러리 및 벤치마크
items.abstractKo: 강건한 강화학습(RL)은 정책이 다양한 변화와 교란 하에서 실패할 수 있는 실제 환경에 신뢰성 있게 배포하기 위해 매우 중요하다. 기존의 강건한 RL 알고리즘들은 풍부한 메커니즘과 원리를 제공하지만, 두 가지 주요 장벽이 그들의 광범위한 잠재력을 제한한다: 알고리즘 재사용성의 제한과 실증적 능력의 경계가 불명확하다는 점이다. 우리는 이 두 문제를 해결하는 알고리즘 중심의 라이브러리이자 벤치마크인 RobustRLlib을 소개한다. items.title: DexPort: A Hand-Held Skill Interface for Dexterous Hand Data Collection
items.abstract: Collecting high-quality demonstrations remains a central bottleneck for learning dexterous manipulation. Teleoperation records executable robot actions, but it requires a complete robot setup and places the burden of coordinating many finger joints on the operator. Human demonstrations are easier to collect, but their motions must be estimated and retargeted to the robot, and they do not directly provide robot actions. In this paper, we introduce DexPort, a portable data-collection interface for high-DoF robot hands. It uses the same hand hardware for collection and deployment, avoiding a hand embodiment gap, and records both commanded joint targets and measured joint states. Our key observation is that a small set of skills can support a wide range of dexterous tasks. During collection, the operator moves the hand-held interface to specify the robot wrist motion and selects or adjusts skills that coordinate the finger motion. This removes the need to control each joint independently while retaining behaviors such as precise grasping and in-hand manipulation. We collect demonstrations across several real-world tasks and in unstructured environments without a robot arm. We then use behavior cloning to train visuomotor policies directly on the recorded wrist motions and hand commands, without skill labels. We evaluate across 4 tasks: pick-and-place with diverse objects, screwing with in-hand tool use, drawer stowage which requires simultaneous grasp and pulling, and a bimanual scanning task. We collect over 2,500 demonstrations with our portable device, in both laboratory and in-the-wild settings. Across our tasks, we see an improvement from 11% to 64% when using recorded robot commands instead of states, and an improvement from 36% to 78% for task success when using in-the-wild data.
items.titleKo: DexPort: 정교한 로봇 손 데이터 수집을 위한 휴대형 스킬 인터페이스
items.abstractKo: 고품질 시연 수집은 정교한 조작 학습에서 여전히 주요 병목이다. 원격조작(teleoperation)은 로봇이 실행할 수 있는 동작을 기록하지만, 완전한 로봇 구성(setup)을 필요로 하고 다수의 손가락 관절을 조정하는 부담을 조작자에게 전가한다. 인간의 시연은 수집이 더 쉽지만, 그 동작을 추정하고 로봇에 맞게 재매핑해야 하며 로봇 동작을 직접 제공하지는 않는다. 본 논문에서는 고자유도(High-DoF) 로봇 손을 위한 휴대형 데이터 수집 인터페이스인 DexPort를 소개한다. DexPort는 수집과 배포에 동일한 손 하드웨어를 사용하여 손...

items.title: ViT-H: Generative Video-To-Humanoid Control with Motion Tracking Feedback
items.abstract: Learning humanoid control from monocular human videos offers a scalable way to acquire diverse whole-body behaviors. Yet, existing reconstruction-retargeting-tracking pipelines are limited in system-level scalability by separately optimized intermediate stages and cannot directly optimize reference motion executability using downstream tracking feedback. We present ViT-H, a video-to-humanoid control framework following a generation-and-tracking paradigm. ViT-H directly generates humanoid reference motions from videos with a diffusion model, bypassing human motion reconstruction and retargeting, and uses motion-tracking outcomes to post-train the generator with direct preference optimization. We further introduce an autoregressive variant that enables real-time humanoid video teleoperation with sub-400 ms latency. Extensive experiments on the Unitree G1 demonstrate that ViT-H outperforms state-of-the-art reconstruction-retargeting-tracking pipelines in both motion quality and executability. We further show that ViT-H scales favorably with model size and with both pre-training and post-training data scale, while motion-tracking feedback consistently improves executability across different motion trackers.
items.titleKo: ViT-H: 모션 추적 피드백을 이용한 생성형 비디오 기반 휴머노이드 제어
items.abstractKo: 단일 카메라로 촬영한 인간 비디오로부터 휴머노이드 제어를 학습하는 것은 다양한 전신 행동을 확보할 수 있는 확장 가능한 방법을 제공한다. 그러나 기존의 재구성·리타게팅·추적 파이프라인은 중간 단계들이 각각 따로 최적화되어 있어 시스템 수준의 확장성에 제약이 있으며, 하위 추적 피드백을 이용해 참조 모션의 실행 가능성(executability)을 직접 최적화할 수 없다. 본 연구에서는 생성-추적 패러다임을 따르는 비디오-투-휴머노이드 제어 프레임워크 ViT-H를 제안한다. ViT-H는 확산 모델을 사용하여 영상으로부터 휴머노이드 참조 모션을 직접 생성함으로써 인간 모션 재구성 및 리타게팅 과정을 우회한다.

items.title: RynnUnify: Towards Unified Embodied Brain
items.abstract: We introduce RynnUnify, a 16B unified embodied model that combines strong embodied understanding with long-horizon visual planning through interleaved video--language reasoning. With capabilities spanning spatial reasoning, physical prediction, and grounding, RynnUnify connects an understanding of the physical world with visual anticipation of how it evolves across successive subtasks. Building on these capabilities, we further develop an agentic extension through reinforcement learning to selectively use video predictions for reasoning about unobserved states and interaction outcomes. We also develop a world-action extension of the full RynnUnify model, translating its understanding and prediction capabilities into robot control. To evaluate these capabilities, we introduce Rynn-VP and Rynn-GEU for long-horizon visual planning and anticipatory reasoning. Experiments show that RynnUnify achieves the highest average embodied understanding score among the evaluated unified multimodal models and improves the Rynn-VP overall score by 9.75 points over Cosmos 3 Nano. Its agentic extension improves the Rynn-GEU average by 6.0 points over direct reasoning, while the world-action extension achieves 51.5\% success on 20 selected composite RoboCasa365 tasks and 46.7\% average success across three real-robot tasks. Together, these results establish RynnUnify as a shared foundation for embodied understanding, visual planning, and robot control, taking a step toward a unified embodied brain.
items.titleKo: RynnUnify: 통합 체화형 브레인으로의 접근
items.abstractKo: 우리는 RynnUnify를 소개한다. RynnUnify는 16B(160억 파라미터) 규모의 통합 체화형 모델로, 교차적 비디오-언어 추론을 통해 강력한 체화적 이해와 장기적 시야의 시각적 계획을 결합한다. 공간 추론, 물리적 예측, 그라운딩에 걸친 능력을 바탕으로 RynnUnify는 물리 세계에 대한 이해를 연속적인 하위 과제들에 걸쳐 그것이 어떻게 변화할지를 시각적으로 예측하는 능력과 연결한다. 이러한 능력을 바탕으로 우리는 강화학습을 통해 에이전트 확장을 추가로 개발하여 미관측 상태와 상호작용 결과에 대해 추론할 때 비디오 예측을 선택적으로 사용하도록 했다. 또한...

items.title: If at First You Don't Succeed, Backtrack: Lightweight Recovery for Frozen VLAs
items.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models perform well on robotic manipulation, yet remain brittle once their own actions carry them into states their training data barely covers. Recovering from such failures usually requires recovery demonstrations, policy retraining, or a separate model at inference time. We introduce Backtrack, a lightweight failure detection and recovery mechanism for frozen VLAs that needs none of these. A small failure prediction head, trained only on outcome-labeled rollouts of the frozen policy, reads the VLA's existing internal representations to estimate whether the current episode will fail. When the predicted failure probability exceeds a threshold, a controller pauses the policy, retraces the arm's recently achieved motion, and hands control back to the unchanged policy so it can retry from an earlier configuration. The head adds only 0.48-0.88% to the policy's parameter count. We evaluate Backtrack on LIBERO with three VLAs spanning two action-generation families: SmolVLA and $π$0.5, which use flow-matching action experts, and the autoregressive $π$0-FAST. On LIBERO-Long, the suite of long-horizon multi-step tasks and the one on which all three policies fail most often, Backtrack reduces each policy's failure rate by 19-48%, raising success by up to 7.4 percentage points; on the three shorter suites, where control success is already 85-99%, its effect is smaller. On MetaWorld, all twelve controller configurations tested with SmolVLA improve on the unassisted policy.
items.titleKo: 처음에 성공하지 못하면 되돌아가라: 동결된 VLA를 위한 경량 복구 기법
items.abstractKo: Vision-Language-Action(VLA) 모델은 로봇 조작에서 우수한 성능을 보이지만, 자체적인 행동이 훈련 데이터가 거의 다루지 않는 상태로 이끌 때 취약하게 남아 있다. 이러한 실패에서 회복하려면 보통 복구 시연, 정책 재학습 또는 추론 시 별도의 모델이 필요하다. 우리는 Backtrack을 소개한다. 이는 동결된 VLA에 대해 이들 중 어느 것도 필요로 하지 않는 경량 실패 감지 및 복구 메커니즘이다. 동결된 정책의 결과 라벨이 붙은 롤아웃만으로 학습된 작은 실패 예측 헤드는 VLA의 기존 내부 표현을 읽어 현재...

items.title: HoloBoxing: A Simple Recipe for Humanoid Boxing with 7 Minutes of Single-GPU Training
items.abstract: HoloBoxing presents a simple recipe for learning humanoid boxing by building on a pretrained whole-body controller. The recipe separates reusable motor skills from task decisions: a compact planner requests future body-point targets, while the frozen controller handles joint-level execution. A learned decoder maps 32-dimensional actions to structured target windows, and measured-state imitation initializes the planner before reinforcement learning. Task learning then refines interaction behavior while reusing the decoder and controller, avoiding the need to relearn whole-body control. This combination keeps task optimization focused on a compact upper policy and supplies an initial behavior before reward-driven exploration. Starting from that available controller, the recipe accounts for about seven minutes of additional training, including reused representation fitting and a single-GPU task run. This excludes controller pretraining, data preparation, evaluation, and search. Simulated boxing experiments and component controls evaluate the resulting behavior and the roles of imitation initialization and the target representation.
items.titleKo: HoloBoxing: 단일 GPU 7분 학습으로 구현하는 휴머노이드 권투의 간단한 레시피
items.abstractKo: HoloBoxing은 사전 학습된 전신 컨트롤러를 기반으로 휴머노이드 권투를 학습하는 간단한 방법을 제시한다. 이 레시피는 재사용 가능한 운동 기술을 작업 결정과 분리한다. 간결한 플래너는 미래의 신체 지점 목표를 요청하고, 파라미터가 고정된 컨트롤러는 관절 수준의 실행을 담당한다. 학습된 디코더는 32차원 행동을 구조화된 목표 영역으로 매핑하며, 측정 상태 모방(measured-state imitation)을 통해 강화학습 전에 플래너를 초기화한다. 이후 작업 학습은 디코더와 컨트롤러를 재사용하면서 상호작용 행동을 정교화하여 전신 제어를 다시 학습할 필요를 없앤다. items.title: When Human Corrections Travel: Safety in Federated VLA Adaptation
items.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies can adapt to local human intervention, while federated learning can combine distributed robot experience without pooling raw records. We examine their prospective intersection: sharing adaptations derived from diverse human corrections across tasks, environments, people, and robot embodiments. Corrections differ in modality, safety semantics(urgency, behavioral scope, etc.), and privacy sensitivity. A shared update that improves mean task success may suppress a rare safety intervention or produce an unsafe response on another robot. We argue for three requirements: preserve the context and uncertainty of multimodal corrections when deciding what to share; assess candidate updates in each receiving robot's closed loop before deployment; and evaluate leakage alongside retention of safety-critical evidence. Immediate, legible defensive behavior remains necessary during human interaction. We offer counterexamples and a falsifiable evaluation agenda, not experimental results.
items.titleKo: 사람의 수정이 전파될 때: 연합 학습 기반 비전-언어-행동(VLA) 적응에서의 안전성
items.abstractKo: 비전-언어-행동(VLA) 정책은 로컬 인간 개입에 적응할 수 있으며, 연합 학습은 원시 기록을 통합하지 않고 분산된 로봇 경험을 결합할 수 있다. 우리는 작업, 환경, 사람 및 로봇 구현 전반에 걸쳐 다양한 인간 수정으로부터 도출된 적응을 공유하는 이들의 잠재적 교차점을 검토한다. 수정은 모달리티, 안전의 의미(긴급성, 행동 범위 등), 그리고 프라이버시 민감성 측면에서 서로 다르다. 평균 작업 성공률을 개선하는 공유 업데이트가 드문 안전 개입을 억제하거나 다른 로봇에서 불안전한 반응을 유발할 수 있다. 우리는 세 가지 요구사항을 제시한다(요약 원문이 중단되어 이후 내용이 생략됨).

items.title: Regularised RL improves sim-to-real transfer
items.abstract: Regularised reinforcement learning (RL) has provable robustness guarantees that should ease the transfer of policies from simulation to robots, known as sim-to-real. Yet, weakly regularised algorithms like Proximal Policy Optimisation (PPO) remain the de facto choice in sim-to-real pipelines, while the practical benefits of regularisation for transfer remain poorly characterised. In this work, we study the sim-to-real performance of commonly used RL algorithms, with the aim of characterising the effects of regularisation on robotic performance. To that end, we derive Soft MellowMax Actor-Critic (SMM-AC), a novel regularised RL algorithm based on the soft mellowmax value function, which carries strong robustness guarantees. On MuJoCo continuous control benchmarks, SMM-AC is competitive with baselines like Soft Actor-Critic (SAC). On real robots, SMM-AC achieves higher return, while exhibiting greater robustness to perturbations in observations, the environment, and dynamics than baselines. Together, these results demonstrate that regularised RL improves real-world policy deployment through better robustness to the sim-to-real gap, and changing real-world conditions.
items.titleKo: 정규화된 강화학습(RL)은 시뮬레이션→실세계 전이를 개선한다
items.abstractKo: 정규화된 강화학습(RL)은 시뮬레이션에서 로봇으로의 정책 전이(시뮬-투-리얼)를 용이하게 하는 증명 가능한 강건성 보장을 제공한다. 그럼에도 불구하고 Proximal Policy Optimisation(PPO)과 같이 약하게 정규화된 알고리즘은 시뮬-투-리얼 파이프라인에서 사실상 표준으로 남아 있으며, 전이에서 정규화가 주는 실무적 이점은 아직 충분히 규명되지 않았다. 본 연구에서는 정규화가 로봇 성능에 미치는 영향을 규명하기 위해, 일반적으로 사용되는 RL 알고리즘들의 시뮬-투-리얼 성능을 조사한다. 이를 위해 우리는 Soft MellowMax 액터-크리틱...

items.title: Predictive Long-Horizon Progress Modeling with Action-Aware Quantification
items.abstract: Quantitative and dense task progress feedback is essential for robotic manipulation across data curation, policy evaluation, and reinforcement learning. Existing progress annotations often rely on sparse keyframe markings derived from subjective manual judgments, limiting their scalability and cross-task consistency, particularly in long-horizon manipulation. To overcome these challenges, we propose action-aware quantification, a unified progress specification that decomposes long-horizon trajectories into object-level subtasks via a vision-language model (VLM) and assigns weighted action credits to capture fine-grained execution dynamics. Using VLM auto-labeling and human calibration, we construct an 800+ hour training video dataset and LOOM, a long-horizon progress benchmark containing 19,618 human-calibrated evaluation frames. To model these dense progress dynamics, we introduce NimCritic, a predictive progress critic trained via Joint Video-Progress Learning. We further incorporate Historical Progress Perturbation to mitigate sequential drift, and design a contrastive Video-Progress Alignment objective that bridges asymmetric expert streams by mutually grounding intermediate visual dynamics and denoised progress trajectories. NimCritic matches or outperforms state-of-the-art process reward models (PRMs) on the established Video Progress Benchmark (VPB) and LOOM, surpassing GVL (GPT-6-Sol) on VPB by about 65% in terminal success accuracy (TSA). On the large-scale RoboArena policy evaluation benchmark, it also retrieves human-selected successful rollouts with about 97% overall recall. These results establish action-aware quantification as a scalable foundation for dense progress feedback in robotic manipulation.
items.titleKo: 행동 인지 기반 정량화를 통한 예측형 장기 진행도 모델링
items.abstractKo: 정량적이고 조밀한 작업 진행도 피드백은 데이터 큐레이션, 정책 평가 및 강화학습에 이르기까지 로봇 조작 전반에서 필수적입니다. 기존의 진행도 주석은 종종 주관적인 수작업 판단에서 유래한 희소한 키프레임 표시에 의존하여 확장성과 작업 간 일관성이 제한되며, 특히 장기간(롱호라이즌) 조작에서 그 한계가 더욱 뚜렷합니다. 이러한 문제를 극복하기 위해 우리는 행동 인지 정량화(action-aware quantification)를 제안합니다. 이는 비전-언어 모델(VLM)을 통해 장기간 궤적을 객체 수준의 하위 과제로 분해하고 가중치가 부여된 행동 cred

items.title: Adaptive World-Models for Anomaly Recognition (AWARE): A Framework for Robot Dynamics Prediction and Introspection
items.abstract: Unrecognized anomalies in critical infrastructure can rapidly cascade into catastrophic physical or operational failures. Current anomaly detection approaches often rely on direct access to the monitored system by utilizing onboard sensors, such as motor encoders, to detect anomalous states. However, legacy hardware often lacks these sensors, or strict security protocols may prohibit access altogether. We therefore present AWARE, a world model framework that is capable of anomaly detection using only external camera monitoring via system dynamics estimation and state prediction. Evaluated across 240 real-world robotic crane trajectories, including payload collisions and motor degradations, AWARE demonstrates a 26% improvement in anomaly classification over our strongest baseline under noisy, camera-only state estimation. Furthermore, the inferred dynamics parameter can be decoded to identify the source of faults, localizing the degrading motor with 88% accuracy.
items.titleKo: 이상 인식을 위한 적응형 월드 모델(AWARE): 로봇 동역학 예측 및 자기진단 프레임워크
items.abstractKo: 중요 인프라에서 인식되지 않은 이상은 빠르게 연쇄되어 치명적인 물리적 또는 운영적 장애로 이어질 수 있다. 현재의 이상 탐지 접근법은 종종 모터 엔코더와 같은 온보드 센서를 활용해 모니터링 대상 시스템에 직접 접근함으로써 이상 상태를 감지하는 데 의존한다. 그러나 레거시 하드웨어는 이러한 센서를 갖추지 않은 경우가 많고, 엄격한 보안 프로토콜로 인해 접근이 전면 금지될 수도 있다. 따라서 본 논문에서는 외부 카메라 관찰만을 통해 시스템 동역학을 추정하고 상태를 예측함으로써 이상을 탐지할 수 있는 월드 모델 프레임워크인 AWARE를 제시한다. items.title: Conditional Neural Processes for Self-Supervised Goal Discovery in Action Imitation
items.abstract: Inspired by infants' ability to learn novel tasks by imitating others, in this work we evaluate to what extent Conditional Neural Processes can autonomously learn representations of actions that are informative about their underlying goal. We show that the addition of an attention mechanism in the hidden space fosters the emergence of robust goal representations early on in the observation of an action sequence, making it a promising model for a robotic self-supervised general learner.
items.titleKo: 행동 모방에서 자기지도적 목표 발견을 위한 조건부 신경 프로세스
items.abstractKo: 유아가 타인을 모방하여 새로운 과제를 학습하는 능력에서 영감을 받아, 본 연구에서는 조건부 신경 프로세스(Conditional Neural Processes)가 행동의 근본적 목표에 대한 정보를 담는 행동 표현을 얼마나 자율적으로 학습할 수 있는지를 평가한다. 은닉 공간에 어텐션 메커니즘을 추가하면 행동 시퀀스 관찰 초반에서부터 강건한 목표 표현의 출현을 촉진함을 보였으며, 이는 로봇의 자기지도 학습 기반 범용 학습자 모델로서 유망함을 시사한다.

items.title: Retiming Robot Demonstrations with a Learned Speed Prior
items.abstract: The pace of a robot demonstration is often determined by the teleoperator rather than by the task itself. As a result, the same motion can appear at widely different speeds across demonstrations, and policies trained on such data may inherit operator-specific timing along with task behavior. We propose to learn a speed prior directly from large-scale demonstration data. Given a task instruction, a motion path and the images along it, it predicts a distribution over execution speed along the path, from which a chosen quantile defines a consistent clock for retiming each demonstration. Existing methods derive the acceleration signal from the very data they accelerate, so each new task costs another fit, annotation, or pair of predefined rates. A single trained speed prior instead covers every task in a corpus. We fit a speed prior on both robot teleoperation data and handheld demonstrations in which a human arm, rather than a robot arm, moves the gripper, and use it to retime robot demonstrations to the handheld pace before fine-tuning a vision-language-action policy. For execution, we pair the policy with a real-time optimal-control layer that tracks predicted action chunks under robot constraints using the predicted pace. On 120 RoboLab tasks, policies fine-tuned on our learned clocks succeed more often and move with up to half the jerk compared with policies fine-tuned on the original demonstration timing and uniformly accelerated to the same speed. On a real robot, our policy stacks cups in 3.50s, 1.72$\times$ faster than the default policy's 6.02s while succeeding as often, in 29 of 30 trials. Videos and further material are available at https://mllab.snu.ac.kr/projects/learned_speed_prior.
items.titleKo: 학습된 속도 사전분포를 이용한 로봇 시연의 시간 재조정
items.abstractKo: 로봇 시연의 속도는 대개 작업 자체가 아니라 원격 조작자(teleoperator)에 의해 결정된다. 그 결과 동일한 동작이 시연마다 매우 다른 속도로 나타날 수 있으며, 그러한 데이터로 학습된 정책은 작업 동작뿐 아니라 조작자 고유의 타이밍까지 함께 물려받을 수 있다. 본 연구에서는 대규모 시연 데이터로부터 속도 사전분포(speed prior)를 직접 학습할 것을 제안한다. 작업 지시문, 운동 경로 및 경로를 따라 촬영된 이미지들이 주어지면, 모델은 경로를 따라 실행 속도에 대한 분포를 예측하고, 여기서 선택된 분위수가 각 시연을 재타이밍하기 위한 일관된 시간 기준을 정의한다. 기존의

items.title: Robust Offset-Free Lane-Keeping Control Framework for Vision-Only Automated Vehicles
items.abstract: Achieving accurate, real-time lane-keeping control during high-speed cornering on large-curvature roads while ensuring robust vehicle stability is a critical challenge in autonomous driving. To address this challenge, this study developed a robust offset-free model predictive control (OF-MPC) framework for vision-based autonomous vehicle lane-keeping. The regulation problem in this framework is solved using several algorithms. Numerical simulation results indicated that the interpolation-tube-based constrained iterative linear quadratic regulator (itube-CILQR) algorithm outperformed solvers based on the standard Interior Point Optimizer (IPOPT) and Operator Splitting Quadratic Program (OSQP), achieving a mean computation time of less than 5 ms. The itube-CILQR algorithm was then used for vehicle control in vision-based lane-keeping experiments in a simulation environment to quantify the perceptual uncertainty of a visual perception model (multitask UNet). This quantification was performed using the OF-MPC framework for traffic scenes that were not encountered during model training. Overall, the developed OF-MPC framework and the proposed method for characterizing the perceptual uncertainty of a visual perception system in unseen environments can contribute to the future development of advanced autonomous driving systems.

items.title: Monte Carlo-Based Indoor UAV Localization in Dynamic Environments Using Only Four Onboard Range Sensors
items.abstract: Indoor UAV localization with minimal onboard sensing remains challenging, particularly in dynamic environments. We propose augmented filtered Monte Carlo localization (AF-MCL) for 2D localization using only four single-point range sensors and measured heading. AF-MCL rejects range measurements inconsistent with the known static map and adaptively injects particles to recover from localization divergence and kidnapping. Beam classification is performed only at the previous position estimate, making its ray-casting cost independent of the particle count. The particle distribution additionally provides an online measure of localization uncertainty. Real-world experiments in a 2.10x1.63 m environment yield mean position errors of 6.4-7.7 cm under static and dynamic conditions. Simulations in 6x6 m and 10x10 m environments yield 4.5-5.2 cm mean errors; under dynamic obstacles, standard MCL reaches 12.3 cm and reliable MCL 7.7 cm. The results show that robust indoor localization under dynamic obstacles is achievable with only four single-point range measurements and heading.

items.abstractKo: 최소한의 온보드 센싱으로 실내 UAV 위치추정은 여전히 어려우며, 특히 동적 환경에서 그 난이도가 크다. 본 논문에서는 네 개의 단일 지점 거리 센서와 측정된 헤딩만을 사용한 2D 위치추정을 위한 확장 필터형 몬테카를로 위치추정(Augmented Filtered Monte Carlo Localization, AF-MCL)을 제안한다.
