items.title: Natural-Language to Nav2: Operational Policies for Costmap-Based Navigation
items.abstract: Autonomous mobile robots support material transport in warehouses and industrial facilities, where navigation must adapt to changing operating conditions. Sensor observations reveal physical obstacles, but do not by themselves specify temporary access rules, route preferences, or exceptions known to operators. This paper presents a natural-language policy interface that brings this knowledge into ROS 2 Nav2. A local large language model converts instructions into JSON policies specifying destinations, spatial constraints, and temporal or event conditions. Deterministic checks govern mission acceptance, and three costmap adapters project accepted policies into the existing navigation stack without changing its planner or controller. On 150 researcher-authored English commands, four local models produce 107-142 correct accepted policies, compared with 44 for a rule-based parser, with 3-20 incorrect acceptances per model. Fault injection records rejection of eight endpoint/JSON faults and 29 validator-stage faults. Navigation experiments use correct task policies to evaluate keepouts, zone costs, person-dependent regions, and event-conditioned passage in simulation and on a TurtleBot3. For Tasks 1-3, mean travel times are 18.4-24.5% lower in simulation and 23.1-35.0% lower on the physical testbed than with the baseline lacking those policies. A native KeepoutFilter comparison and two-robot demonstrations examine basic keepout behavior and shared policy projection. The interface connects operator instructions to explicit navigation policies while retaining Nav2's planning and control components.
items.titleKo: 자연어에서 Nav2로: 코스트맵(costmap) 기반 내비게이션을 위한 운용 정책
items.abstractKo: 자율 이동 로봇은 창고와 산업 시설에서 자재 운송을 지원하며, 이때 내비게이션은 변화하는 운용 조건에 적응해야 한다. 센서 관측은 물리적 장애물을 드러내지만, 임시 출입 규칙, 경로 선호도, 또는 작업자가 알고 있는 예외 사항을 스스로 명시하지는 않는다. 본 논문은 이러한 지식을 ROS 2 Nav2에 도입하는 자연어 기반 정책 인터페이스를 제시한다. 로컬 대형 언어 모델은 지시문을 목적지, 공간 제약, 시간적 또는 이벤트 조건을 지정하는 JSON 정책으로 변환한다. 결정론적 검사가 미션 ac

items.title: OWLS: Open-world Language-conditioned Speed Fields for Zero-Shot Rover Navigation
items.abstract: Semantics can provide a proxy for physical traversability. Terrain that looks like loose sand or a rock field is likely to have similar physical properties. Open-vocabulary vision-language models (VLMs) enable this physical reasoning over terrain outside any fixed label set. We present Open-world Language-conditioned Speed Fields (OWLS), which plans directly over the dense feature map of a VLM. Prompted with a description of traversable terrain, the VLM scores every pixel of a single camera image; OWLS projects these scores onto the ground, adapts them to the platform with two morphological operations, and uses the result as the speed field of a minimum-time planner, so terrain appearance and obstacle clearance shape one trajectory. OWLS needs no task-specific training, no terrain annotation, no persistent map, and no exteroceptive sensor beyond the camera. We evaluate it on a physical rover indoors and off-road, on simulated Mars and Moon rovers over 200 procedurally generated terrains, and on real planetary imagery.
items.titleKo: OWLS: 제로샷 로버 내비게이션을 위한 오픈월드 언어 조건화 속도 필드
items.abstractKo: 의미 정보는 물리적 주행성의 대리 지표가 될 수 있다. 느슨한 모래나 암석 지대처럼 보이는 지형은 유사한 물리적 특성을 가질 가능성이 높다. 오픈 어휘 비전-언어 모델(VLM)은 고정된 라벨 집합을 벗어난 지형에 대해 이러한 물리적 추론을 가능하게 한다. 우리는 Open-world Language-conditioned Speed Fields(OWLS)를 제안하며, OWLS는 VLM의 밀집 특징 맵 상에서 직접 경로 계획을 수행한다. 주행 가능한 지형에 대한 설명을 프롬프트로 제공하면 VLM은 단일 카메라 영상의 모든 픽셀에 점수를 부여하고, OWLS는 이 점수들을 지면에 투영한 뒤 두 가지 형태학적 연산으로 플랫폼에 맞게 조정한다.

items.title: UAV-SwarmAgent: Scalable Multi-UAV Reconnaissance and Task Allocation via Code Generation and Vision-Language Reasoning
items.abstract: Supervising a multi-UAV reconnaissance mission usually means plotting waypoints and watching every drone. We present UAV SwarmAgent, a hierarchical multi-agent system in which an operator states the mission in one natural-language sentence and a ground-station agent writes and executes code that turns it into per-UAV routes. The agent grounds inspection targets in an aerial map with a vision-language model, splits them among N UAVs by balancing route length, and dispatches worker agents that verify incidents with a compact onboard decision model. In simulation over 4 incident types and 3 foundation models, the swarm located the incident in 244 of 255 missions (95.7%). A paired scaling study with one to 5 UAVs shows that flight time follows an Amdahl-type law. The second UAV delivers half of the attainable saving and the speedup is bounded at 1.52x. We discuss what this predictability, and the false alarms we observed, imply for an operator who supervises the swarm, and outline the user study needed to test it.
items.titleKo: UAV-SwarmAgent: 코드 생성 및 비전-언어 추론을 통한 확장 가능한 다중 UAV 정찰 및 임무 할당
items.abstractKo: 다중 UAV 정찰 임무를 감독하는 일은 보통 웨이포인트를 계획하고 각 드론을 감시하는 것을 의미한다. 우리는 UAV SwarmAgent를 제안한다. 이 계층적 다중 에이전트 시스템에서 운용자는 자연어 한 문장으로 임무를 명시하면 지상 관제 에이전트가 이를 개별 UAV 경로로 변환하는 코드를 작성·실행한다. 에이전트는 비전-언어 모델로 항공 지도에서 검사 대상을 그라운딩(위치 대응)하고, 경로 길이를 균형 있게 맞춰 N대의 UAV에 분배하며, 경량화된 온보드 의사결정 모델로 사건을 검증하는 작업자 에이전트들을 파견한다. 시뮬레이션에서 4가지 사건 유형과 3개의 발견

items.title: Sensorimotor Alignment: A Platonic Proxy for Embodied Policy Success
items.abstract: Robotic foundation models are typically evaluated through costly closed-loop rollouts, which motivates cheap offline proxies for model capability. The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) suggests that as representations improve, different modalities such as vision and language converge toward a shared statistical model of reality. We ask whether motion trajectories form another such modality: as embodied models become more capable, should their sensory representations converge toward the structure of physical motion? To examine this, we propose Sensorimotor Alignment ($S^2$), a training-free offline metric that measures how well a model's sensory representation aligns with the geometry of physical motion. We find that $S^2$ correlates positively with downstream robot task success across embodied model families, making it a low-cost offline proxy for prioritizing models before closed-loop evaluation. $S^2$ can also identify promising vision-language model (VLM) backbones even before costly fine-tuning into vision-language-action models (VLAs). Beyond this correlation, $S^2$ offers representation-level explanations for phenomena observed in VLAs and world action models (WAMs). With $S^2$, we extend PRH to embodied models and make sensorimotor alignment empirically measurable, offering insight into why an embodied model succeeds beyond its closed-loop success rate.
items.titleKo: 감각운동 정렬: 체현된 정책 성공을 위한 플라톤적 대리
items.abstractKo: 로봇용 파운데이션 모델은 대개 비용이 큰 폐쇄 루프 롤아웃을 통해 평가되며, 이는 모델 능력을 저렴한 오프라인 대리 지표로 대체하려는 동기를 부여한다. 플라톤적 표상 가설(Platonic Representation Hypothesis, PRH)은 표상이 개선됨에 따라 시각 및 언어와 같은 서로 다른 모달리티들이 현실에 대한 공통의 통계적 모델로 수렴한다고 제안한다. 우리는 모션 궤적이 또 다른 이러한 모달리티를 형성하는지 묻는다: 체현된 모델의 능력이 향상될수록 그들의 감각 표상은 물리적 운동의 구조로 수렴해야 하는가? 이를 검증하기 위해 우리는 Sensorimotor Alignment(S^2)를 제안한다. 훈련-

items.title: OpenTac: An Open Ecosystem for Customizable, Scalable, and Transferable 3D Tactile Sensing
items.abstract: We present OpenTac, a novel sensor and a full-stack ecosystem for tactile skins that are highly customizable, scalable, and readily deployed in downstream robot control and learning applications. Our core contribution is twofold. First, we develop a scalable resistive tactile skin with a structured deformable overlay that converts tangential loading into spatially varying pressure. Differential responses across neighboring "taxels" support decoding of local shear vectors, and the common-mode response encodes normal force. Second, we provide a highly customizable sensor design tool that is able to automatically generate fabrication files for these tactile skins from 2D outlines and developable 3D surfaces, including from abstract descriptions such as text (e.g., "design a sensor for a size 9 shoe insole"). We develop an ecosystem around the OpenTac sensor, including the CAD design tool, a sensor simulator, cross-sensor transfer, and fast/adaptive data acquisition. We demonstrate the broad applicability of the OpenTac-CAD sensor design tool by designing and fabricating more than 30 sensors across a variety of robot embodiments. We characterize the three-dimensional tactile fields produced by OpenTac with a commercial, high-precision force/torque sensor. We demonstrate the broad applicability of 3D tactile sensing across contact-rich feedback control and manipulation policy learning on four real-world robot embodiments. Additionally, adaptive acquisition enables kilohertz-rate partial readouts, exceeding full-array raster scanning on the same sensor by 19.2X at 16 sampled taxels per update for a 1024-taxel skin. We provide all hardware, software, and result videos are at opentac.github.io
items.titleKo: OpenTac: 맞춤형·확장 가능·이식 가능한 3D 촉각 센싱을 위한 오픈 생태계
items.abstractKo: 우리는 OpenTac을 소개한다. items.title: Extending Harmonic Function Methods via Root Locus for Coordinated Path Generation
items.abstract: We consider the offline generation of coordinated paths for N interchangeable robots and N goals in planar environments with polygonal obstacles. After a conformal map to a circular domain, starts and goals become the poles and zeros of a rational function R, and the paths are the branches of its Generalized Root Locus (GRL), i.e. the streamlines of the logarithmic potential -log R. We show that, for every phase outside a finite set of critical phases and a set of boundary phases, the induced gradient motion drives each robot to a distinct goal along pairwise disjoint paths that never reach the obstacles; the robot-goal assignment is produced by the construction, and with the gain used as a clock all robots move as the closed-loop roots of the GRL and arrive together at a prescribed time. Obstacles become streamlines through successive Milne-Thomson reflections, and for a finite number of reflections a finite test certifies safety for the potential that is actually computed. Reciprocal root-locus planning is recovered as a special case. The method is illustrated on two polygonal workspaces, 100 random instances compared with independent harmonic planning and artificial potentials, and a scene with ten robots and ten obstacles.
items.titleKo: 협동 경로 생성을 위한 루트 로커스 기반 조화 함수 기법의 확장
items.abstractKo: 우리는 다각형 장애물이 있는 평면 환경에서 N개의 교환 가능한 로봇과 N개의 목표에 대한 오프라인 협동 경로 생성을 다룬다. 원형 영역으로의 정형 사상(conformal map) 이후 시작점들과 목표점들은 유리함수 R의 극점(poles)과 영점(zeros)이 되며, 경로들은 그 일반화된 루트 로커스(Generalized Root Locus, GRL)의 가지들, 즉 로그 퍼텐셜 -log R의 유선(streamlines)이다. 우리는 유한한 수의 임계 위상(critical phases)들과 일부 경계 위상들의 집합을 제외한 모든 위상에서 유도된 그래디언트 운동이 각 로봇을 서로 겹치지 않는 경로를 따라 서로 다른 목표로 이동시키며(원문이 중단됨)

items.title: DiffDreamer: Coupling World Models with Differentiable Simulation for Agile Quadrotor Control
items.abstract: Tasks such as quadrotor dynamic-gate racing require agents to anticipate external motion while maintaining precise high-frequency control. World-model-based reinforcement learning provides a natural solution by learning latent dynamics for future imagination, yet it often entangles environmental evolution and the robot's own dynamics in a single learned rollout, where model bias can affect policy optimization efficiency. We propose DiffDreamer, a differentiable reinforcement learning framework that tightly couples a learned world model with differentiable simulation for actor optimization. In one optimization step, the learned world model propagates latent states that capture external dynamics and history-dependent features, while the differentiable simulator propagates the robot's explicit physical state. We further decompose the actor objective into a critic-driven pathway for non-differentiable task rewards and a simulator-driven pathway for differentiable motion rewards. Experiments on aggressive tracking and dynamic-gate racing show that DiffDreamer improves training convergence over the model-free, model-based, and differentiable-RL baselines, and final performance over these baselines and classical planning and control methods. Additional experiments assess reward decomposition and the odometry-conditioned relative-state representation through ablations. We also provide proof-of-concept real-world flight experiments for validation.
items.titleKo: DiffDreamer: 세계 모델과 미분 가능한 시뮬레이션의 결합을 통한 고기동 쿼드로터 제어
items.abstractKo: 쿼드로터 다이내믹-게이트 레이싱과 같은 과제는 에이전트가 외부의 움직임을 예측하는 동시에 정밀한 고주파수 제어를 유지해야 한다. 세계 모델 기반 강화학습은 미래를 상상하기 위한 잠재 동역학을 학습함으로써 자연스러운 해결책을 제공하지만, 학습된 롤아웃에서 환경의 변화와 로봇 자체의 동역학이 하나로 얽히기 쉬워 모델 편향이 정책 최적화 효율에 악영향을 미칠 수 있다. 우리는 DiffDreamer를 제안한다. DiffDreamer는 학습된 세계 모델을 미분 가능한 시뮬레이션과 긴밀히 결합하여 액터 최적화를 수행하는 미분형 강화학습 프레임워크이다. In

items.title: Progress Probes $P^2$: Lightweight Runtime Monitoring for Vision-Language-Action Models
items.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models can perform diverse manipulation tasks directly from visual observations and natural language instructions, but they remain prone to mistakes and unpredictable failures. Deploying these policies without continuous human supervision will require robust runtime monitors that detect when the policy has gone off-course. Existing monitors use external foundation models, such as vision-language models (VLMs) to supervise the policy, introducing significant complexity and computational cost for monitoring at runtime. In this work, we investigate an alternate approach: \textit{can a VLA's own internal activations provide the information needed to monitor its execution?} Our method trains linear probes on policy activations from demonstrations to estimate progress, then flags executions that deviate from expected progress. In experiments with the open-source VLA $π_{0.5}$ and across simulated and real-world manipulation tasks, this approach is competitive with or outperforms VLM-based monitors in task failure detection, as well as methods which require failure data for training. These findings suggest that simple probes of VLA internals can be used to develop reliable runtime monitors, opening a path toward building policies that can act reliably and monitor their execution without external foundation models.
items.titleKo: Progress Probes P^2: 비전-언어-액션 모델을 위한 경량 런타임 모니터링
items.abstractKo: 비전-언어-액션(VLA) 모델은 시각적 관찰과 자연어 지시만으로 다양한 조작 작업을 직접 수행할 수 있지만, 여전히 실수와 예측 불가능한 실패에 취약합니다. 지속적인 인간 감독 없이 이러한 정책을 배포하려면 정책이 탈선했을 때 이를 감지하는 강건한 런타임 모니터가 필요합니다. 기존의 모니터는 정책을 감독하기 위해 비전-언어 모델(VLM)과 같은 외부 파운데이션 모델을 사용하여 런타임 모니터링에 상당한 복잡성과 계산 비용을 도입합니다. 본 연구에서는 대체 접근법을 조사합니다.

items.title: Humanoid Mobility via Attention-based Contacts
items.abstract: Humanoid mobility over complex terrain requires accurate foot placement and coordinated whole-body motion capable of robust adaptation. Reinforcement learning (RL) policies trained without motion references generalize well across terrains, yet eliciting effective whole-body coordination through reward design and exploration alone remains challenging. In contrast, reference-based methods yield natural motions but struggle to adapt beyond the predefined trajectories in their training data. We introduce a learning framework that bridges these two approaches by using motion data strictly as a training prior. An explicit, self-supervised, attention-based contact planner predicts future body-environment contacts, while a contact-conditioned tracker translates these plans into coordinated whole-body motion. Together, they establish contact as an interface between sensory observations and control actions. This abstraction allows the policy to internalize the contact-aware structure of locomotion rather than directly replicating kinematics. Consequently, a single policy can exploit data-driven motion priors for natural whole-body coordination while retaining the flexibility to discover environment-dependent behaviors through reinforcement learning. Building on the learned contact planner and tracker, a subsequent fine-tuning stage bootstraps their acquired capabilities to explore environment variations beyond those covered by the original motion data. Operating entirely from onboard observations without any reference inputs at deployment, this framework enables versatile humanoid mobility in challenging environments.
items.titleKo: 어텐션 기반 접촉을 이용한 휴머노이드 이동성
items.abstractKo: 복잡한 지형에서의 휴머노이드 이동은 정확한 발 위치 선정과 강인하게 적응할 수 있는 전신 조정 동작을 필요로 한다. 모션 레퍼런스 없이 학습된 강화학습(RL) 정책은 다양한 지형에 대해 잘 일반화되지만, 보상 설계와 탐색만으로 효과적인 전신 조정을 이끌어내는 것은 여전히 어렵다. 반면 레퍼런스 기반 방법은 자연스러운 동작을 생성하지만, 학습 데이터에 미리 정의된 궤적을 넘어 적응하는 데에는 한계가 있다. 우리는 모션 데이터를 엄격히 trai로 사용함으로써 이 두 접근을 잇는 학습 프레임워크를 소개한다.

items.title: Echo: Coupled Action and Task Status Signal Denoising for Vision Language Action Models
items.abstract: Recognizing task completion and failure enables robots to stop upon success and initiate recovery or replanning after failure. Existing methods augment Vision Language Action (VLA) policies with task status signal prediction to support these execution decisions. However, learning and integrating these signals can require fine-grained supervision, external monitoring models, or complex architectural designs. Moreover, the potential of task status signals to directly guide action generation remains underexplored. We present Echo, a framework that combines task status signal learning without frame-level progress annotations with a compact design for status prediction and action generation within a single VLA. Specifically, Echo represents task status with stop and failure signals, added as two dimensions of each action chunk and denoised together with robot actions. Their combination distinguishes ongoing execution, successful completion, and failure. To learn these signals without fine-grained progress annotations, Echo constructs successful, failed, and recovery trajectories with complementary supervision properties. To enable status signal-guided action generation, Echo controls interactions between the signals and actions and denoises the signals faster than the actions. These allow later action denoising steps to condition on cleaner status estimates while preserving accurate signal prediction. Extensive real-world manipulation experiments show that Echo accurately predicts task status and consistently improves policy performance.
items.titleKo: Echo: 비전-언어 액션(VLA) 모델을 위한 동작 및 작업 상태 신호의 결합적 디노이징
items.abstractKo: 작업 완료와 실패를 인식하면 로봇은 성공 시 동작을 중단하고, 실패 시 복구나 재계획을 시작할 수 있다. 기존 방법들은 이러한 실행 결정을 지원하기 위해 비전-언어 액션(VLA) 정책에 작업 상태 신호 예측을 추가한다. 그러나 이러한 신호를 학습하고 통합하려면 세분화된 감독, 외부 모니터링 모델, 또는 복잡한 아키텍처 설계가 필요할 수 있다. 게다가 작업 상태 신호가 동작 생성 자체를 직접적으로 유도할 수 있는 가능성은 아직 충분히 탐구되지 않았다. 우리는 Echo를 제안한다. 이 프레임워크는 작업 상태 신호 학습을 결합하며, ...

items.title: Decentralized Bi-Level Optimization for Cooperative Orbital Transportation of a Rigid Payload
items.abstract: The rapid growth of the space economy, alongside increasing orbital congestion and debris, is driving demand for reliable on-orbit transportation of large and non-cooperative objects. Performing such transportation with a swarm of small spacecraft distributes risk and removes the single point of failure inherent to monolithic architectures, but requires solving a non-convex trajectory optimization coupling every agent's cone-constrained thrust to the payload's rotational dynamics. Existing approaches span decentralized control laws with asymptotic guarantees but limited constraint enforcement, and centralized and partially centralized planners that reintroduce a single point of failure. In this work, we present a decentralized bi-level framework driven by exact gradients: the problem is split into an inner convex thrust allocation and an outer search over payload torque trajectories. This decomposition yields fuel-efficient solutions quickly, without requiring full NLP convergence, and at short timescales its performance scales with the number of agents. Theoretical convergence guarantees are established, and the method is validated through extensive Monte Carlo simulation, including closed-loop recovery from in-flight faults. These properties make the framework well suited to spacecraft swarm applications.
items.titleKo: 강체 페이로드의 협력적 궤도 수송을 위한 분산형 바이레벨 최적화
items.abstractKo: 우주 경제의 급속한 성장과 더불어 궤도 혼잡 및 우주 잔해의 증가는 대형 및 비협력 객체의 신뢰성 있는 궤도 내 수송에 대한 수요를 촉진하고 있다. 소형 우주체들의 스웜으로 이러한 수송을 수행하면 위험이 분산되고 모놀리식 아키텍처에 내재한 단일 실패 지점이 제거되지만, 각 에이전트의 원뿔 제약 추력과 페이로드의 회전 동역학을 결합하는 비볼록 궤적 최적화 문제를 해결해야 한다. 기존 접근법은 점근적 보장을 제공하는 분산 제어 법칙에서부터 제약 조건의 강제 이행이 제한적인 방법에 이르기까지 다양하다.

items.title: Dispersive Tree Agreements for Multi-Robot Coordination
items.abstract: Multi-robot coordination of nonlinear systems is naturally formulated as joint-space optimal control subject to constraints over groups of robots. Existing methods that approach joint optimality remain largely centralized, offline, and confined to collision-free motion planning, while decentralized, real-time counterparts target safe navigation without pursuing the joint optimum. This paper develops a decentralized, real-time planner that approaches the joint optimum as an anytime process. We extend a recent single-robot framework that searches dispersive trees of forward-propagated commands for differentially flat systems to coordinate a multi-robot team near-optimally. We first show that the inter-robot coupling can be effectively replaced by some local constraints, under which locally grown dispersive trees contain a near-optimal agreement. It is this structure that the robots pursue by decentralized column generation, negotiating rents on the shared space that guide the search of each robot's tree. The negotiation settles on an agreement whose near-optimality is certified at quiescence. Our protocol, WarpWeaver, implements this negotiation as an asynchronous real-time loop over a receding horizon, and demonstrates effective closure to quiesced agreements even when real-time deadlines cut the negotiation short. In simulation, WarpWeaver reduces total travel time by up to 22% against centralized offline planners on the Dynobench suite and by up to 37% against a decentralized real-time baseline, and nearly doubles the success rate of a task-specific planner on graph connectivity. Hardware experiments on six robots planning onboard demonstrate real-world implementability.
items.titleKo: 다중 로봇 협조를 위한 분산 트리 합의
items.abstractKo: 비선형 시스템의 다중 로봇 협조 문제는 로봇 그룹에 대한 제약을 포함하는 결합 공간 최적 제어로 자연스럽게 정식화된다. 결합 최적성을 지향하는 기존 방법들은 대체로 중앙집중식·오프라인이며 충돌 회피 동작 계획에 한정되는 반면, 분산형 실시간 기법들은 결합 최적해를 추구하지 않고 안전한 주행만을 목표로 한다. 본 논문은 언제든 개선 가능한(anytime) 과정으로 결합 최적해에 근접하는 분산형 실시간 플래너를 제안한다. 우리는 전진 전파된 명령들의 분산 트리를 탐색하는 최근의 단일 로봇 프레임워크를 확장한다...

items.title: SCOPE: Scene-graph Construction Optimized by Plan Error-correction for Robot Long-term Planning Datasets
items.abstract: Task and Motion Planning (TAMP) stands as a fundamental challenge in robotics, essential for enabling autonomous agents to execute complex, long-horizon tasks in diverse environments. While Large Language Models (LLMs) introduce a new paradigm for TAMP by leveraging extensive common sense, their inherent reasoning limitations hinder direct application, and fine-tuning strategies to enhance these capabilities are currently bottlenecked by the scarcity of high-quality datasets. Existing automated generation methods often suffer from homogeneity, limiting model generalization, and unsolvability, where hallucinated scene graphs create physical mismatches with task goals. To address these issues, we propose Scene-graph Construction Optimized by Plan Error-correction (SCOPE), an automated framework designed to generate diverse and executable TAMP datasets. SCOPE incorporates multi-level diversity metrics to maximize the information entropy of scenarios. Crucially, it introduces a Plan Feedback Error-correction pipeline that utilizes planner execution failures as feedback signals to retroactively rectify logical inconsistencies in scene graphs, ensuring physical feasibility. Experimental results demonstrate that SCOPE exhibits greater robustness to erroneous scene graphs and generates higher-quality data. When utilized for LLM fine-tuning, SCOPE-generated data yield a downstream TAMP model that achieves an absolute 12.33% gain in success rate over its counterpart fine-tuned with data generated by DELTA, a state-of-the-art PDDL-based planner.
items.titleKo: SCOPE: 로봇 장기 계획 데이터셋을 위한 계획 오류 보정으로 최적화된 장면 그래프 구성
items.abstractKo: 작업 및 운동 계획(Task and Motion Planning, TAMP)은 로보틱스에서 근본적인 도전 과제로, 자율 에이전트가 다양한 환경에서 복잡하고 장기적인 과업을 수행할 수 있도록 하는 데 필수적이다. 대형 언어 모델(LLM)은 방대한 상식을 활용해 TAMP에 새로운 패러다임을 제시하지만, 고유한 추론 한계로 인해 직접 적용이 어려우며, 이러한 능력을 향상시키기 위한 미세조정 전략은 고품질 데이터셋의 부족으로 병목 현상을 겪고 있다. 기존의 자동 생성 방법들은 종종 동질성으로 인해 모델의 일반화를 제한하고, 해결 불가능성 문제도 수반한다.

items.title: Point-Level Refinable Semantic Mapping for Spatial Understanding
items.abstract: Open-vocabulary 3D semantic maps have emerged as a key spatial memory representation for long-horizon robot autonomy, enabling robots to reason about objects, their spatial relationships, and past observations across time. However, existing object-centric semantic maps are primarily designed for static environments and rely on an append-only point integration strategy, where newly observed points are accumulated but previously integrated points are rarely reevaluated. Consequently, perception errors accumulate over time, and outdated points persist after objects move or disappear. Although recent dynamic mapping methods update object-level representations in changing scenes, they do not explicitly revise noisy or obsolete points within each object. We propose an online refinable semantic mapping framework that continuously refines object representations through probabilistic point-level confidence updating. Each object point maintains a confidence score that is updated online using multi-view temporal evidence: consistent observations reinforce reliable points, while inconsistent segmentation masks, depth measurements, and visibility cues suppress spurious and outdated points. Combined with object tracking and re-identification to preserve instance identities under motion and relocation, our framework enables object-centric semantic maps to be continuously refined rather than monotonically accumulated. Experiments demonstrate improved mapping accuracy over the previous method by 3.46% on Replica and 2.55% on ScanNet, show robustness in dynamic environments and under perception noise, and provide an effective spatial memory for object navigation and embodied question-answering with success rates of 82.4% and 76.7%.
items.titleKo: 공간 이해를 위한 점 수준 정제 가능한 시맨틱 매핑
items.abstractKo: 개방형 어휘를 지원하는 3D 시맨틱 맵은 장기 로봇 자율성을 위한 핵심 공간 메모리 표현으로 부상했으며, 로봇이 객체와 객체 간의 공간적 관계 및 시간에 따른 과거 관측을 추론할 수 있게 한다. 그러나 기존의 객체 중심 시맨틱 맵은 주로 정적 환경을 전제로 설계되었고, 새로 관측된 포인트만 누적하고 이미 통합된 포인트는 거의 재평가하지 않는 추가 전용(append-only) 포인트 통합 전략에 의존한다. 결과적으로 지각 오류가 시간이 지남에 따라 누적되고, 객체가 이동하거나 사라진 이후에도 오래된 포인트가 남아 있게 된다...

items.title: Skeleton-Grounded Latent Action Model for Robot World Models
items.abstract: Robot world models simulate how environments evolve in response to robot actions. Latent action models enable learning dynamics from videos by encoding visual transitions as proxy actions. However, reconstruction-driven latent actions mix robot motion with object responses and other scene changes, complicating their correspondence with robot controls. We propose SkeLAM, a skeleton-guided latent action model for controllable robot world modeling. SkeLAM decomposes latent actions into a kinematic component grounded by robot skeleton supervision and a residual component retaining complementary visual dynamics. Cross-modal swap reconstruction encourages RGB-derived and skeleton-derived kinematic representations to be interchangeable during video reconstruction. The world model incorporates both components through separate conditioning pathways, while branch dropout reduces its dependence on future-derived residual information. A lightweight adapter maps robot actions to the kinematic space, and subsequent world-model fine-tuning adapts generation to these predicted conditions. At inference, the model generates future observations from the current observation and robot actions. On DROID, SkeLAM reduces end-effector ADE by 19.5% and LPIPS by 11.1% compared with DreamDojo. Motion probing supports kinematic specialization, while qualitative results demonstrate zero-shot human-to-robot motion transfer in generated rollouts. Policy evaluation shows agreement between predicted success rates and those measured in real robot executions.
items.titleKo: 로봇 월드 모델을 위한 스켈레톤 기반 잠재 행동 모델
items.abstractKo: 로봇 월드 모델은 로봇의 행동에 따라 환경이 어떻게 변화하는지를 시뮬레이션한다. 잠재 행동 모델은 시각적 전이를 대리 행동으로 인코딩함으로써 영상으로부터 동역학을 학습할 수 있게 한다. 그러나 재구성 중심의 잠재 행동은 로봇의 운동과 객체 반응 및 기타 장면 변화가 혼재되어 로봇 제어와의 대응을 복잡하게 만든다. 우리는 제어 가능한 로봇 월드 모델링을 위해 스켈레톤 기반 잠재 행동 모델인 SkeLAM을 제안한다. SkeLAM은 잠재 행동을 로봇 스켈레톤 지도에 의해 그라운딩된 운동학적 성분과 보완적인 vi를 유지하는 잔여 성분으로 분해한다.

items.title: VecTile: A Low-Cost Flexible Tactile Array for 3-DoF Force Sensing
items.abstract: Tactile sensing provides robots with contact information difficult to obtain from vision alone. Shear force is particularly important for understanding tangential contact, guiding corrective motions, and maintaining grasp stability, yet flexible and low-cost tactile arrays often measure only normal force. We introduce VecTile, a low-cost, 6 mm thin, flexible tactile array capable of three-axis force sensing. VecTile combines a piezoresistive layer with passive silicone nubs that convert normal and shear forces into distinguishable pressure patterns. The sensor can be fabricated in-house without specialized equipment. The complete system costs less than 35 USD for a 4x4 array. We validate the sensing mechanism through finite element analysis and hardware experiments. In controlled single-taxel tests over 1-5 N normal force and up to 1.5 N shear force, VecTile achieves root-mean-square errors of 0.39 N and 0.16 N for normal and shear forces. A VecTile calibrated while flat retains accuracy when curved, while a five-minute manual calibration is sufficient for practical use. Two applications demonstrate its utility. First, shear readings are sensitive enough to stop a sharp scalpel from puncturing a balloon after contact. Second, the sensor substantially improves Diffusion Policy-guided power-plug insertion. All designs and code will be released upon paper acceptance. Project website: https://jiannnh.github.io/VecTile/.
items.titleKo: VecTile: 3자유도(3-DoF) 힘 감지를 위한 저비용 유연 촉각 배열
items.abstractKo: 촉각 감지는 시각만으로 얻기 어려운 접촉 정보를 로봇에 제공한다. 전단력은 접선 방향의 접촉을 이해하고 보정 동작을 유도하며 그립 안정성을 유지하는 데 특히 중요하지만, 유연하고 저비용인 촉각 배열은 종종 법선력만을 측정한다. 우리는 VecTile을 소개한다. VecTile은 저비용·두께 6 mm의 유연 촉각 배열로, 세 축(3자유도)의 힘을 감지할 수 있다. VecTile은 피에조저항층과 법선력 및 전단력을 구별 가능한 압력 패턴으로 변환하는 수동 실리콘 돌기를 결합한다. 센서는 사내에서 특수 장비 없이 제작할 수 있...

items.title: A Sparse Topometric Graph for Scalable Cross-Session Indoor Navigation
items.abstract: A conventional embodied agent in an indoor environment builds a map by accumulating noisy real-world measurements and results from heavy inference to guide navigation. While the detailed measurements may differ due to scene changes or sensor settings, the unique topological structure of navigable passages or the connectivity between rooms may provide training-free guidance that complements local observations. We propose a sparse topometric graph as an efficient structural representation for robust indoor navigation, alleviating the need for fine-grained matching, which is computationally expensive, memory-intensive, and prone to real-world variations. The map consists of nodes that encode local 3D geometry and distance-weighted edges that capture traversable connectivity. A learned graph-matching network finds consistent subgraph structures across sessions by considering both node-level geometric descriptors and neighborhood connectivity. The holistic contextual matching is robust to local ambiguities caused by weak distinctiveness or repetitive structure, and establishes stable correspondences despite local scene changes, different sensor modalities, or limited spatial overlap. We analyze the practicality of the graph through cross-session point-goal navigation, where a goal specified in a prior reference map must be reached from an unknown initial pose in a later session. Experiments show that our method achieves the highest success rates (77.1% on Gibson and 40.0% under 3D-FRONT scene changes), while reducing memory by more than two orders of magnitude compared to point-level representations. The proposed approach further supports cross-session alignment and goal-directed navigation with strong scalability and robust real-world transfer.
items.titleKo: 확장 가능한 교차 세션 실내 내비게이션을 위한 희소 토포메트릭 그래프
items.abstractKo: 전형적인 실내 환경의 임베디드 에이전트는 항해를 안내하기 위해 노이즈가 섞인 실제 측정값을 축적하고 무거운 추론을 수행하여 지도를 구축한다. 장면 변화나 센서 설정 차이로 인해 세부 측정값은 달라질 수 있지만, 통행 가능한 통로의 고유한 위상 구조나 방들 간의 연결성은 지역 관측을 보완하는 별도의 학습이 필요 없는 지침을 제공할 수 있다. 우리는 정밀 매칭에 대한 필요성을 완화하여 계산 비용이 큰 부담을 줄이는, 강건한 실내 내비게이션을 위한 효율적인 구조 표현으로서 희소 토포메트릭 그래프를 제안한다.

items.title: PhysTrace: Interpretable Temporal Evaluation of Physical Consistency in Video Generative Models
items.abstract: World action models increasingly rely on pretrained video models assumed to capture physical dynamics for prediction, planning, and action generation. Existing evaluations assess plausibility, probe representations, or measure predictive surprise, but rarely identify which history-conditioned physical expectations conflict with observations. We introduce PhysTrace, a training-free framework aligning MLLM-generated, history-conditioned expectations with observed video windows to temporally localize physical violations and provide interpretable descriptions without task-specific probes or classifiers. We also introduce IntPhys2-Timing, adding violation intervals to IntPhys2. PhysTrace achieves a Hit Rate of up to 70.7% across physical principles on IntPhys2-Timing and outperforms the compared methods in overall possible-impossible discrimination accuracy on IntPhys2. Applied to reconstructed videos along the trajectories of pretrained diffusion/flow-based video models, PhysTrace reveals attribute- and noise-dependent patterns in physical violation localization, enabling interpretable physical consistency analysis across timesteps.
items.titleKo: PhysTrace: 비디오 생성 모델의 물리적 일관성에 대한 해석 가능한 시간적 평가
items.abstractKo: 세계 행동 모델은 예측, 계획 및 행동 생성을 위해 물리적 역학을 포착한다고 가정한 사전학습된 비디오 모델에 점점 더 의존하고 있다. 기존 평가는 타당성(plausibility)을 평가하거나 표현을 조사하거나 예측적 놀람(predictive surprise)을 측정하지만, 과거 관측에 조건화된 어떤 물리적 기대가 관측과 충돌하는지를 식별하는 경우는 드물다. 우리는 PhysTrace를 소개한다. PhysTrace는 학습이 필요 없는 프레임워크로, MLLM이 생성한 과거 관측에 조건화된 기대를 관측된 비디오 구간과 정렬하여 물리적 위반을 시간적으로 국지화하고 작업별 프로브나 ... 없이 해석 가능한 설명을 제공한다. (원문이 중단됨)

items.title: FastHarness: Experience-Driven Review Scheduling for Vision-Language-Action Policies
items.abstract: Agentic robot systems combine language-model reasoning with robot policies to monitor execution and recover from failures. However, reviewing every action chunk incurs substantial overhead, even in familiar situations. We introduce FastHarness, an experience-driven execution harness that adaptively schedules GPT-6 Astra supervision of a π0.5 policy. A fast path uses stage memory and reviewed outcomes to reduce review frequency as experience accumulates, while a complementary recovery path focuses supervision on correcting errors. Once recovery is verified, routine execution resumes, with failure experience retained to guide future interventions. The policy remains frozen and generates fresh actions from current observations. Across four simulated manipulation tasks, reviewer token use decreases by an average of 57.2% per task from the first evaluated episode to the mean of the final five episodes. Mean episode time decreases from 85.5 to 52.0 minutes over the same interval. On the same tasks, mean success increases from 80% for GPT-as-Policy (π0.5 + GPT-6 Astra) to 97.19% with FastHarness. These results highlight adaptive supervision as a practical route to more efficient agentic robotics without additional model training.
items.titleKo: FastHarness: 비전-언어-행동 정책용 경험 기반 검토 스케줄링
items.abstractKo: 에이전트형 로봇 시스템은 언어 모델 추론과 로봇 정책을 결합해 실행을 모니터링하고 실패로부터 복구한다. 그러나 모든 동작 청크를 검토하는 것은 친숙한 상황에서도 상당한 오버헤드를 초래한다. 본문에서는 FastHarness를 소개한다. FastHarness는 경험 기반의 실행 하니스로, π0.5 정책에 대한 GPT-6 Astra 감독을 적응적으로 스케줄링한다. 빠른 경로는 단계 메모리와 검토된 결과를 활용해 경험이 축적됨에 따라 검토 빈도를 줄이고, 보완적인 복구 경로는 오류 수정을 위해 감독을 집중한다. 복구가 확인되면 일상적인 실행이 재개된다. (원문이 'with failu'에서 중단되어 이후 문장이 누락됨)

items.title: FocusVLA: Future-Intent Guided Dynamic View Routing for Vision-Language-Action Models
items.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have become an important paradigm for robotic manipulation by unifying visual perception, language understanding, and action generation. Since reliable manipulation requires sufficient observation of objects, end-effectors, and their spatial relationships, multi-view inputs are widely used to provide complementary spatial information. However, our experiments show that existing VLA models do not fully exploit such multi-view complementarity. The policy tends to persistently rely on the wrist view, lacking the ability to dynamically adjust global-local view dependency across manipulation stages, which limits stage adaptability and robustness. To address this issue, we propose FocusVLA, a stage-aware multi-view routing framework. FocusVLA predicts future interaction intent from historical actions and uses it to guide dynamic view routing during action generation. By adaptively coordinating global and local observations across different task stages, FocusVLA improves multi-view utilization. On RoboTwin 2.0, FocusVLA improves the average success rate over the strongest baseline $π_{0.5}$ by 10.10 pp. In real-world evaluation, FocusVLA improves the success rate from 71.7\% to 85.0\%, achieving a 13.3\% gain over $π_{0.5}$. Moreover, the intent prediction and dynamic routing modules of FocusVLA can be integrated into existing VLA frameworks without modifying their core architectures.
items.titleKo: FocusVLA: 미래 의도 유도 동적 시점 라우팅을 이용한 비전-언어-행동 모델
items.abstractKo: 비전-언어-행동(VLA) 모델은 시각 인식, 언어 이해, 행동 생성의 통합을 통해 로봇 조작의 중요한 패러다임으로 자리잡았다. 신뢰할 수 있는 조작을 위해서는 물체, 엔드이펙터 및 이들 간의 공간적 관계를 충분히 관찰해야 하므로, 상호보완적인 공간 정보를 제공하기 위해 다중 시점 입력이 널리 사용된다. 그러나 우리의 실험은 기존 VLA 모델들이 이러한 다중 시점의 상호보완성을 완전히 활용하지 못함을 보여준다. 정책은 지속적으로 손목 시점에 의존하는 경향을 보이며, 글로벌-로컬 시점의 동적 조정 능력이 부족하다.

items.title: CoHelix: Event-Based Multi-Propeller Rotation-Rate Tracking with Shared Projective Geometry
items.abstract: Estimating propeller rates from a moving event camera requires separating blade rotation from the changing image geometry. Background activity mixes with blade events, while repeated blade appearances admit half- and double-rate ambiguities. We propose CoHelix, a recursive filter that estimates one shared homography and separate rotation states for four rigidly mounted, coplanar propellers. Each admitted event updates its assigned rotation state, and its accepted geometry measurements correct the shared homography used to interpret later events from every propeller. We report lock, the fraction of evaluated time for which an estimate remains within 2% of synchronized ground truth, because mean error alone does not show how long a tracker follows the true rate. With fixed-rate initialization, leave-one-recording-out evaluation on moving-camera data gives CoHelix 62.9% lock, compared with 39.8% for HelixTrack and 22.2% for EventPro. With other settings fixed, allowing four geometry contributors instead of one raises lock from 3.4% to 62.9%. On a private target-follower dataset with a different target quadcopter, CoHelix retains the measurement settings selected on moving-camera data and uses a fixed initial rate. It reaches 95.9% lock, compared with 56.2% for HelixTrack and 61.1% for EventPro.
items.titleKo: CoHelix: 공유 투영(호모그래피) 기하를 이용한 이벤트 기반 다중 프로펠러 회전 속도 추적
items.abstractKo: 움직이는 이벤트 카메라로부터 프로펠러 회전 속도를 추정하려면 블레이드의 회전과 변하는 영상 기하학을 분리해야 한다. 배경 활동이 블레이드 이벤트와 섞이고, 블레이드가 반복적으로 나타나면 절반 및 두 배 속도 모호성이 발생한다. 본 논문에서는 CoHelix를 제안한다. CoHelix는 하나의 공유 호모그래피와, 강체로 고정된 동일 평면상의 네 개 프로펠러 각각에 대한 개별 회전 상태를 추정하는 재귀 필터다. 각 허용된 이벤트는 할당된 회전 상태를 갱신하고, 수용된 기하학적 측정치는 이후 모든 프로펠러의 이벤트를 해석하는 데 사용되는 공유 호모그래피를 보정한다. (요약 원문이 중단됨)

items.title: Probabilistic Energy Modeling Unifies Versatile Swarm Control
items.abstract: Robotic swarms must coordinate across diverse missions, yet existing controllers often require redesign, retuning, or retraining when objectives change. Here we show that probabilistic energy modeling provides a unifying representation for versatile swarm control, in which diverse missions emerge from compositions of shared interaction principles rather than task-specific control formulations. By exploiting the correspondence between Gibbs random field energy minimization and structured reward maximization, we encode fundamental swarm behaviors as reusable energy terms within a unified probabilistic objective. Decentralized policies trained within this representation are composed into a single controller through lightweight policy gating, without retraining. An interpretable action-attention mechanism captures non-uniform local interactions, while dimensionless normalization supports transfer across swarm scales and platforms. Demonstrated on aerial swarms, the unified policy generalizes zero-shot across six mission classes, 10-100 agents, two hardware platforms, and indoor cluttered and GPS-denied woodland environments. Large-scale simulations achieve 0.96-1.00 task success rates with 1-10 ms per-agent inference latency, while physical deployments confirm zero-shot transfer to real platforms and unstructured environments. These results establish probabilistic energy modeling as a scalable and transferable framework for decentralized swarm control.
items.titleKo: 확률적 에너지 모델링이 다목적 스웜 제어를 통합하다
items.abstractKo: 로봇 스웜은 다양한 임무에 걸쳐 협력해야 하지만, 기존 제어기들은 목표가 바뀔 때 종종 재설계, 재조정 또는 재학습을 필요로 한다. 본 연구에서는 확률적 에너지 모델링이 다목적 스웜 제어를 위한 통합된 표현을 제공함을 보인다. 이 표현에서는 다양한 임무가 작업 특화 제어 공식이 아니라 공유된 상호작용 원리의 조합으로부터 나타난다. Gibbs 랜덤 필드의 에너지 최소화와 구조화된 보상 극대화 간의 대응관계를 활용하여, 우리는 기본적인 스웜 행동들을 통합된 probabi 내에서 재사용 가능한 에너지 항으로 인코딩한다.

items.title: Less Decoder is More Encoder: Geometric Representation Learning from Novel View Synthesis
items.abstract: This paper examines the role of Novel View Synthesis (NVS) in geometric representation learning. In principle, NVS should reason about 3D scene structure, thereby enabling transferable multi-view geometric representations. Yet, existing encoder-based NVS methods yield poor representations. This is not because of a lack of supervisory signal, but rather due to inconspicuous architectural choices: \textit{spatially expressive decoders} that dilute representational capabilities of the scene encoder, and \textit{low-level pixel-space targets} that hinder feature learning. We present SNAP, a self-supervised encoder-decoder transformer that addresses both through a pose-conditioned local decoder and a latent-space reconstruction objective. SNAP is task agnostic, and we show that it is competitive with special-purpose geometry-supervised methods. SNAP also performs competitively against self-supervised representations across five tasks: visual localization, pose estimation, point correspondence, depth estimation, and robot manipulation. Remarkably, SNAP's patch features exhibit emergent viewpoint invariance that approaches heavily supervised models despite lower compute and data budgets. Under camera shifts where standard 2D representations collapse, SNAP degrades more gracefully, revealing that restricting decoder expressivity actively prevents the suppression of transferable geometric structure. https://snap-nvs.github.io
items.titleKo: 디코더를 줄이고 인코더를 강화하라: 새로운 시점 합성에서의 기하학적 표현 학습
items.abstractKo: 본 논문은 기하학적 표현 학습에서 신규 시점 합성(Novel View Synthesis, NVS)의 역할을 검토한다. 원칙적으로 NVS는 3차원 장면 구조를 추론해야 하므로, 이를 통해 전이 가능한 다중 시점 기하학적 표현을 획득할 수 있다. 그럼에도 불구하고 기존의 인코더 기반 NVS 방법들은 열악한 표현을 산출한다. 이는 감독 신호의 부족 때문이 아니라, 눈에 띄지 않는 아키텍처적 선택들 때문인데: 장면 인코더의 표현 능력을 희석시키는 공간적으로 표현력이 강한 디코더(spatially expressive decoders)와 특징 학습을 저해하는 저수준 픽셀 공간 목표(low-level pixel-space targets)가 그 원인이다. 우리는 SNAP을 제안한다. (원문이 'self-s'에서 중단됨)

items.title: EyeRobot 2.0: Active Gaze for Precise Manipulation without Wrist Cameras
items.abstract: Inspired by human vision, we introduce a framework using active gaze to enable fine-grained bimanual manipulation with only a single stereo camera. EyeRobot 2.0 physically attends to a 3D fixation point in the scene by swiveling two eye viewpoints to center their gaze on it. The resulting images are processed foveally by allocating more visual tokens to the image centers, focusing computation on task-relevant features. Such Active Visual Fixation (AVF) requires carefully coordinated gaze during task execution, which we accomplish hierarchically by first training a low-level gaze servoing policy conditioned on a goal object, then training a target selector which emits fixation goals based on task progress. Both modules are trained with RL on real-world data: the first is trained with a dense geometric reward and the second co-trains with the BC gripper policy which allows it to discover fixation sequences that can resemble a human's fixation sequence while performing the task. EyeRobot 2.0 further takes advantage of fixation by canonicalizing gripper information into a fixation-relative SE(3) frame, which compacts the size of the action distribution to learn. We collect teleoperation data for 7 real-world and 6 simulated tasks, and conduct over 1000 physical and 1800 simulated robot trials comparing EyeRobot 2.0 against passive stereo and ego + wrist camera policies trained on the same data. Removing wrist cameras is costly for standard policies: with only passive stereo, real-world success drops from 52% to 27%. EyeRobot 2.0 closes this gap with only stereo, outperforming passive stereo by 40% in real and 20% in sim. It matches ego + wrist policies when their wrist views are clear (69% vs. 64%), and more than doubles their success when grasped objects occlude the wrist cameras (48% vs. 22%)
items.titleKo: EyeRobot 2.0: 손목 카메라 없이 정밀 조작을 위한 능동 시선
items.abstractKo: 인간의 시각에서 영감을 받아 단일 스테레오 카메라만으로 미세한 양수 조작을 가능하게 하는 능동 시선 프레임워크를 소개합니다. EyeRobot 2.0은 장면의 3차원 고정점에 물리적으로 주목하기 위해 두 개의 눈 시점을 회전시켜 시선을 그 점에 맞춥니다. 이렇게 얻은 영상은 중심부에 더 많은 시각 토큰을 할당하여 중심(foveal) 처리되며, 작업 관련 특징에 대한 계산을 집중합니다. 이러한 능동 시각 고정(Active Visual Fixation, AVF)은 작업 실행 중 정교하게 조율된 시선이 필요하며, 우리는 이를 계층적으로 달성하기 위해 먼저 저수준 시선 서보(gaze servoing) 정책을 학습시킵니다.

items.title: CORNAV: Construction-Aware Reasoning for Robot Navigation on Active Worksites
items.abstract: The construction industry faces persistent labor shortages, low productivity that costs the global economy over $1.6 trillion annually, and one of the highest injury rates among major industries. These factors motivate the use of autonomous robots to improve efficiency and worker safety. Existing language-grounded navigation systems, however, rely on semantic scene understanding alone and lack access to construction-specific context such as architectural plans, evolving work schedules, and safety constraints. As a result, they localize permanent building features unreliably and cannot safely navigate active jobsites. We present CORNAV, a blueprint-grounded, schedule-aware navigation framework that operates from 2D CAD drawings and project schedules without requiring a Building Information Model. CORNAV aligns architectural blueprints against hierarchical open-vocabulary 3D scene graphs to ground object queries, converts project schedules into time-varying navigation constraints, and validates requests through an LLM-based safety module that escalates hazardous zones before planning. An A* planner then enforces mandatory exclusion zones while preferentially avoiding higher-risk areas. Across an indoor office and a real construction site, blueprint grounding raises task success from 13.0% to 72.2% over semantic retrieval alone, schedule awareness eliminates all hard-zone violations, and the safety module correctly rejects hazardous requests arising from mislabeled project schedules.
items.titleKo: CORNAV: 가동 중인 건설 현장을 고려한 로봇 내비게이션 추론
items.abstractKo: 건설업은 지속적인 인력 부족, 연간 1.6조 달러가 넘는 전 세계적 경제 손실을 초래하는 낮은 생산성, 주요 산업들 중에서도 높은 부상률 등 문제에 직면해 있다. 이러한 여건은 효율성과 작업자 안전을 개선하기 위한 자율 로봇의 도입을 촉진한다. 그러나 기존의 언어 기반 내비게이션 시스템은 의미론적 장면 이해에만 의존하여 건축 도면, 변화하는 작업 일정, 안전 제약 등 건설 특화 맥락에 접근하지 못한다. 그 결과 이들 시스템은 영구적인 건축 요소의 위치를 신뢰성 있게 파악하지 못하고 안전하게 … (원문이 중단됨)

items.title: UniIntervene++: An Adaptive Intervention Agent for Efficient Real-World Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: Online reinforcement learning (RL) enables robot policies to improve through physical interaction, but the assistance they require changes as their competence evolves. Existing intervention strategies based on offline estimates or fixed decision rules can therefore become mismatched to the current policy. To address this, we propose UniIntervene++, an adaptive intervention agent that learns to allocate control between autonomous execution and heterogeneous assisted behaviors during online RL. Specifically, UniIntervene++ first formulates the evolving RL policy, trajectory correction, and a task-structured CodePolicy as Options in a unified semi-Markov decision process and learns their relative values online. Building on this, competence-adaptive intervention periodically probes the RL policy through unassisted execution, keeping control allocation responsive to its evolving capability. Finally, coupled experience learning allows assisted behaviors to improve the RL policy, whose evolving outcomes in turn reshape future intervention decisions. In this way, UniIntervene++ jointly determines when to intervene, how to intervene, and when to return control as the RL policy improves. Across five real-world manipulation tasks, UniIntervene++ achieves an average success rate of 89.67%, outperforming all baselines by at least 6 percentage points, while reducing human intervention to 0.77%, a relative reduction of at least 94.6% from the best baseline. Code is available in our \href{https://github.com/dannyyudong/An-Adaptive-Intervention-Agent-for-Efficient-Real-World-Reinforcement-Learning}{GitHub repository}.
items.titleKo: UniIntervene++: 실세계 강화학습의 효율성을 위한 적응형 개입 에이전트
items.abstractKo: 온라인 강화학습(RL)은 로봇 정책이 물리적 상호작용을 통해 개선되도록 하지만, 정책의 역량이 변함에 따라 필요로 하는 지원도 달라진다. 따라서 오프라인 추정치나 고정된 결정 규칙에 기반한 기존의 개입 전략은 현재의 정책과 불일치해질 수 있다. 이를 해결하기 위해 본 연구에서는 온라인 RL 수행 중 자율 실행과 이종(heterogeneous) 보조 행동 간의 제어 할당을 학습하는 적응형 개입 에이전트 UniIntervene++를 제안한다. 구체적으로 UniIntervene++는 먼저 진화하는 RL 정책, 궤적 보정(trajectory correction), 그리고 태스크…

items.title: LLA-MPC on Embedded Hardware: Rapid Adaptive Control with Thousands of Parallel Models
items.abstract: We present a generalized implementation of Look-Back and Look-Ahead Adaptive Model Predictive Control (LLA-MPC), a learning-free framework for real-time, rapid adaptive system identification and control. The original formulation was demonstrated only in simulation, for autonomous racing with a fixed model structure. Our implementation has modular dynamics and integrators, and we validate it on the F1TENTH platform under constrained computation and noisy state estimation. The system identifies tire parameters online by evaluating thousands of candidate models in real time on an embedded computer. Experiments with low-friction tires across changing surfaces show that LLA-MPC completes high-speed tracking tasks where a fixed nominal model fails. Code, videos, and our related work are available at: https://lla-control.github.io.
items.titleKo: 임베디드 하드웨어에서의 LLA-MPC: 수천 개 병렬 모델을 이용한 빠른 적응 제어
items.abstractKo: Look-Back and Look-Ahead 적응형 모델 예측 제어(LLA-MPC)의 일반화된 구현을 제시한다. LLA-MPC는 학습이 필요 없는 프레임워크로서 실시간으로 빠른 적응적 시스템 식별 및 제어를 가능하게 한다. 원래의 정식화는 고정된 모델 구조를 사용하는 자율 레이싱 시뮬레이션에서만 시연되었다. 본 구현은 동역학과 적분기를 모듈화하였고, 제한된 연산 자원과 잡음이 섞인 상태 추정 환경에서 F1TENTH 플랫폼을 통해 이를 검증하였다. 시스템은 임베디드 컴퓨팅 환경에서 실시간으로 수천 개의 후보 모델을 평가하여 타이어 파라미터를 온라인으로 식별한다.

items.title: Bridging Frontier Reasoning and Robot Execution: From Autonomous Demonstration Generation to Dense Language Supervision
items.abstract: Recent advances in frontier models enable robot manipulation from only a few demonstrations, but high inference latency limits their use for real-time robot control. To bridge this gap, we study two complementary approaches that connect frontier reasoning with low-latency local execution. First, we use a frontier model to autonomously generate demonstrations that supplement human demonstrations for training a fast local policy. We augment its in-context examples with corrective demonstration segments that show how to recover from physical errors, improving generation reliability. Generation time and cost decrease as successful examples accumulate in context, suggesting a path toward more efficient data collection. At deployment, a harness combines frontier-generated instructions with a fast local policy, enabling efficient execution while preserving the frontier model's ability to guide and correct actions. With low-latency execution delegated to the local policy, the bottleneck shifts to its capacity to reliably follow the frontier model's diverse instructions. Our second bridge introduces dense language supervision across three nested granularities---primitive, atomic, and composite---with multi-aspect descriptions at each level. Across long-horizon tasks in RoboCasa 365 and BEHAVIOR-1K, where instructions change as execution progresses, the combined supervision achieves the highest performance under both oracle and frontier-model instructors, demonstrating more reliable instruction following through the policy's language interface. Finally, we evaluate both bridges together on a crossword task that combines semantic planning and manipulation within a fixed time budget. These results support autonomous demonstration generation and dense language supervision as complementary components for connecting frontier reasoning to low-latency local execution.
items.titleKo: 프론티어 추론과 로봇 실행의 연결: 자율 시연 생성에서 고밀도 언어 감독까지
items.abstractKo: 프론티어 모델의 최근 발전으로 소수의 시연만으로 로봇 조작이 가능해졌지만, 높은 추론 지연은 실시간 로봇 제어에서의 활용을 제한한다. 이 간극을 메우기 위해, 우리는 프론티어 추론을 저지연의 로컬 실행과 연결하는 두 가지 상호보완적 접근을 연구한다. 첫째, 프론티어 모델을 이용해 자율적으로 시연을 생성하고, 이를 인간 시연과 함께 빠른 로컬 정책을 학습하는 데 보조적으로 사용한다. 우리는 문맥 내 예시를 오류 복구 시연 구간으로 보강하여 물리적 오류에서 회복하는 방법을 보여줌으로써 생성의 신뢰성을 향상시킨다. 생성 ti

items.title: World Action Learning via Interaction-Centric Spectral Latent Guidance
items.abstract: Learning general-purpose robot policies requires large-scale real-world interaction data, yet collecting robot demonstrations remains expensive and difficult to scale. Egocentric videos offer abundant human interaction experience with task-relevant semantics for robotic manipulation, but direct transfer is challenging for two reasons: latent actions inferred from frame reconstruction can be dominated by nuisance variation such as ego-camera motion, and human and robot behaviors often exhibit different temporal dynamics. We propose WING (World Action Learning via INteraction-Centric Spectral Latent Guidance), a framework for transferring interaction knowledge from egocentric videos to robot policies. WING first separates observer-induced motion from hand-object interaction and distills the interaction-centric component into latent actions. It then exploits the observation that cross-embodiment task semantics are concentrated in slowly varying temporal structures, identifying shared low-frequency components between egocentric latent actions and robot behaviors in the spectral domain and using them to guide action generation. WING achieves average success rates of 99.20% on LIBERO, 93.80% on RoboTwin 2.0, and 57.7% on RoboCasa-GR1, and also performs strongly across four real-world manipulation tasks under diverse generalization settings. These results show that interaction-centric spectral guidance provides an effective and scalable way to transfer physical interaction knowledge from human egocentric video to robot control. Project page: https://mikuz12.github.io/wing/
items.titleKo: 상호작용 중심 스펙트럴 잠재 가이던스를 통한 환경 행동 학습
items.abstractKo: 범용 로봇 정책을 학습하려면 대규모의 실제 상호작용 데이터가 필요하지만, 로봇 시연을 수집하는 것은 비용이 많이 들고 확장하기 어렵다. 에고센트릭 비디오는 로봇 조작에 필요한 과제 관련 의미를 담은 풍부한 인간 상호작용 경험을 제공하지만, 직접 전이하기에는 두 가지 이유로 어려움이 있다: 프레임 재구성에서 추론된 잠재 행동은 에고 카메라의 움직임과 같은 불필요한 변동(nuisance variation)에 의해 지배될 수 있고, 인간과 로봇의 행동은 종종 서로 다른 시간적 역학을 보인다. 우리는 WING (World Action Learning via INteraction-Centric Spectral La)을 제안한다.

items.title: AVL-JEPA: Preventing Causal Dynamics Information Collapse In Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture World Models
items.abstract: Joint embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) predict future latent representations without reconstructing observations, enabling world models to focus on high-level semantic dynamics. However, a JEPA can preserve high dimensional visual information while discarding information about the physical consequences of actions. We call this failure mode causal dynamics information collapse and propose action-grounded vision-invariance latent (AVL) to prevent this collapse. We first use the executed action as an auxiliary dynamics anchor that encourages the model to preserve dynamics information, and then use a vision-invariance pathway which aligns perturbed and clean latent predictions without discarding dynamics information, forcing the model to fully understand and utilize causal dynamics information. We validate AVL on four robotic control tasks (TwoRoom, PushT, OGBench Cube, and Reacher), showing that it substantially improves success rates under visual perturbations while preserving clean-environment performance. We further evaluate physical consequence alignment, clean-noisy dynamics consistency, and the causal effect of targeted transition subspace erasure. Collectively, these results indicate that dynamic information causally relevant to planning is preserved from collapse under AVL.
items.titleKo: AVL-JEPA: 공동 임베딩 예측 아키텍처 월드 모델에서 인과적 역학 정보 붕괴 방지
items.abstractKo: 공동 임베딩 예측 아키텍처(JEPA)는 관측값을 재구성하지 않고 미래의 잠재 표현을 예측하여 월드 모델이 고수준 의미론적 역학에 집중할 수 있게 한다. 그러나 JEPA는 고차원 시각 정보를 보존하는 반면 행동의 물리적 결과에 관한 정보를 버릴 수 있다. 우리는 이 실패 모드를 '인과적 역학 정보 붕괴(causal dynamics information collapse)'라고 명명하고, 이를 방지하기 위해 행동 기반 시각 불변 잠재(AVL)를 제안한다. 먼저 실행된 행동을 보조 역학 앵커로 사용하여 모델이 역학 정보를 보존하도록 유도한다.

items.title: A Unified Framework for Empowerment and Predictive Control
items.abstract: Sampling-based model predictive control (MPC) is a powerful approach to trajectory optimization, but its performance depends on an informative cost function that often requires substantial domain knowledge to design. An alternative is to derive objectives directly from the system dynamics. Empowerment, defined as the channel capacity between an agent's inputs and its future state, provides such a goal-agnostic objective and has been shown to produce useful behaviors across a range of domains. However, existing empowerment-based controllers have two key limitations: empowerment is estimated using a virtual probing policy distinct from the executed control policy, obscuring its connection to the resulting behavior; and its computation typically requires second-order derivatives of the dynamics, limiting compatibility with standard MPC methods. We formulate empowerment using a single policy for both probing and acting, directly linking the empowerment objective to the executed behavior. The resulting objective requires only first-order derivatives and can be optimized with standard MPC solvers, either alone or in combination with a task-specific cost. We evaluate the proposed approach on classical control tasks and show that combining empowerment with task costs matches or exceeds the success rate achieved by either objective alone. Our formulation provides a practical bridge between standard MPC and intrinsically motivated control.
items.titleKo: 임파워먼트와 예측 제어를 위한 통합 프레임워크
items.abstractKo: 샘플링 기반 모델 예측 제어(MPC)는 궤적 최적화에 강력한 접근법이지만, 그 성능은 대개 설계에 상당한 도메인 지식이 필요한 유의미한 비용 함수에 의존한다. 대안으로는 시스템 동역학으로부터 목적을 직접 도출하는 방법이 있다. 에이전트의 입력과 미래 상태 간의 채널 용량으로 정의되는 임파워먼트는 이러한 목표에 의존하지 않는 목적 함수를 제공하며, 다양한 영역에서 유용한 행동을 생성하는 것으로 입증되었다. 그러나 기존의 임파워먼트 기반 제어기에는 두 가지 주요 한계가 있다: 임파워먼트는 추정되...

items.title: RATE: Risk-Aware Tactile Encoding for Contact-rich Robotic Manipulation
items.abstract: Tactile sensing is particularly valuable for contact-rich robotic manipulation. Recent work has made substantial progress in tactile representation learning for robotic manipulation. However, similar tactile observations can arise from interaction conditions with very different task-risk implications, such as sensor noise, task-necessary variations, and emerging undesirable contact. Without context-grounded risk information, these cases can be ambiguous to downstream policies, leading to unnecessary corrections to benign variations or delayed responses to genuinely risky contact. To address this limitation, we propose Risk-Aware Tactile Encoding (RATE), which learns tactile representations that encode task-conditioned interaction risk. Specifically, history-conditioned prediction captures interaction context, while alert supervision associates this context with task-conditioned risk. The learned risk-aware representation complements conventional tactile features through a lightweight residual adapter. Experiments in both simulation and the real world demonstrate substantial improvements in task success, with controlled ablations confirming the complementary benefits of alert-guided learning and predictive temporal modeling.
items.titleKo: RATE: 접촉이 많은 로봇 조작을 위한 위험 인식 촉각 인코딩
items.abstractKo: 촉각 감지는 접촉이 많은 로봇 조작에서 특히 중요하다. 최근 연구들은 로봇 조작을 위한 촉각 표현 학습 분야에서 상당한 진전을 이루었다. 그러나 유사한 촉각 관측값은 센서 노이즈, 작업상 불가피한 변동, 새로 발생하는 바람직하지 않은 접촉 등 작업 위험도에 대해 매우 다른 함의를 가지는 상호작용 조건에서 나타날 수 있다. 맥락에 기반한 위험 정보가 없으면 이러한 경우는 하위 정책에 모호하게 작용하여 무해한 변화에 대해 불필요한 보정이 발생하거나 실제로 위험한 접촉에 대한 반응이 지연될 수 있다. 이를 해결하기 위해...

items.title: DR-IPC: Disturbance-Resilient Integrated Planning and Control for LiDAR-Based Quadrotor Navigation
items.abstract: LiDAR-based quadrotor navigation in cluttered environments remains challenging under external disturbances, particularly when obstacle-aware motion generation and disturbance-rejection control are handled in separate layers. This article presents disturbance-resilient integrated planning and control (DR-IPC), which combines lightweight path guidance with nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) to directly generate angular velocity and thrust. An interconnected extended Kalman filter and nonlinear disturbance observer jointly provide filtered state estimates and reconstructed disturbances for NMPC prediction. The resulting formulation unifies nonlinear quadrotor dynamics, actuator constraints, local motion generation, and penalised safe-flight-corridor residuals without requiring a separate trajectory-optimization stage. Gazebo and MARSIM simulations, together with indoor and outdoor experiments, validate DR-IPC under wind, suspended payloads, narrow passages, ball impacts and reactive avoidance of a dynamic obstacle. In multi-goal navigation with disturbances, DR-IPC increases the number of completed missions from 1/10 to 9/10 in Gazebo and reduces the altitude RMSE from 0.34 to 0.01 m in experiments. The complete system operates onboard at 100 Hz. Supplementary videos are available on the project page https://drpp316.github.io/DR-IPC-Page/, and the source code will be released.
items.titleKo: DR-IPC: LiDAR 기반 쿼드로터 내비게이션을 위한 외란 저항성 통합 계획 및 제어
items.abstractKo: 장애물이 많은 복잡한 환경에서 LiDAR 기반 쿼드로터의 내비게이션은 외부 외란 하에서 여전히 도전적이며, 특히 장애물 인지 기반의 모션 생성과 외란 억제 제어가 서로 다른 계층에서 처리될 때 문제가 된다. 본 논문은 경량 경로 유도(lightweight path guidance)와 비선형 모델 예측 제어(NMPC)를 결합하여 각속도와 추력을 직접 생성하는 외란 저항성 통합 계획·제어(DR-IPC)를 제안한다. 상호 연결된 확장 칼만 필터와 비선형 외란 관측기가 함께 필터링된 상태 추정치와 재구성된 외란을 제공하여

items.title: XGenAct: Geometry-Enhanced World Action Models through Cross-Task Generation
items.abstract: World action models (WAMs) have advanced robot control by predicting how observations and actions evolve over time. Despite this progress, RGB and action based future prediction does not explicitly address the spatial understanding needed for robot manipulation. Existing efforts often add a limited set of spatial prediction tasks through specialized heads or branches, leaving both the range of spatial supervision and the model architecture fragmented. We introduce XGenAct, a world action model that represents RGB observations, robot actions, metric depth, surface normals, and functional role segmentation as RGB videos through deterministic codecs. By sampling perception and action tasks during training, XGenAct uses one video diffusion transformer and one objective to learn temporal prediction across these spaces without modality specific learned heads. On held out RLBench tasks, structured perception training improves average closed loop success over RGB only training, and XGenAct achieves 52% success in the five task external comparison, versus 26% for the strongest evaluated baselines. It also predicts future depth and segmentation more accurately than the evaluated pipelines that generate RGB first and then apply a frozen perception expert.
items.titleKo: XGenAct: 교차 과제 생성을 통한 기하학 강화 월드 액션 모델
items.abstractKo: 월드 액션 모델(WAM)은 관찰과 행동이 시간에 따라 어떻게 변화하는지를 예측함으로써 로봇 제어를 발전시켜 왔다. 이러한 진전에도 불구하고 RGB 및 행동 기반의 미래 예측은 로봇 조작에 필요한 공간적 이해를 명시적으로 다루지 않는다. 기존 연구는 종종 특화된 헤드나 브랜치를 통해 제한된 범위의 공간 예측 과제만을 추가해 왔으며, 그 결과 공간적 감독의 범위와 모델 아키텍처가 단편화되어 있다. 우리는 RGB 관찰, 로봇 행동, 메트릭 깊이, 표면 법선, 그리고 기능적 역할을 표현하는 월드 액션 모델 XGenAct을 소개한다.

items.title: Detect and Suppress: A Mechanistic Defense against Adversarial Patches in VLA Models
items.abstract: Adversarial patches can disrupt Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models by manipulating visual observations, leading to failures in robot control. However, it remains poorly understood which internal mechanisms underlie these failures and how targeted interventions can mitigate them. In this work, we mechanistically analyze VLA representations using a sparse autoencoder (SAE) and identify a feature whose activation strongly correlates with the presence of an adversarial patch. Based on this analysis, we suppress the identified feature at inference time only when a linear probe detects an attack. This intervention improves robustness without the cost of fine-tuning the VLA. We evaluate our method against VLA adversarial patch attacks on LIBERO-10. Conditional intervention improves success rate under intermittent attacks, whereas continuously applying the same intervention substantially degrades policy performance. These results show that attack-related internal representations can provide useful targets for VLA adversarial defense and that controlling when to intervene is important for limiting disruption to nominal policy behavior.
items.titleKo: 탐지 및 억제: VLA 모델의 적대적 패치에 대한 기작 기반 방어
items.abstractKo: 적대적 패치는 시각 관측을 조작하여 비전-언어-액션(VLA) 모델을 교란시킬 수 있으며, 이는 로봇 제어 실패로 이어진다. 그러나 이러한 실패의 내부 기제가 무엇인지, 그리고 표적화된 개입이 이를 어떻게 완화할 수 있는지는 아직 잘 밝혀지지 않았다. 본 연구에서는 희소 오토인코더(SAE)를 이용해 VLA 표현을 기작적으로 분석하고, 적대적 패치 존재와 활성화가 강하게 상관되는 특징을 식별했다. 이 분석을 바탕으로 선형 프로브가 공격을 탐지할 경우에만 추론 시 해당 특징의 활성화를 억제한다.

items.title: MobiAgent: Dual-Loop Recursive Policy Self-Improvement for Long-Horizon Mobile Manipulation
items.abstract: Long-horizon mobile manipulation presents significant challenges due to compounding execution errors and capacity interference between locomotion and arm control. While recent Vision-Language-Action models excel at short-horizon tasks, they lack the hierarchical reasoning required for multi-stage objectives. Furthermore, existing hierarchical agents suffer from rigid sub-task mapping, inflexible replanning, and a lack of continuous learning. To address these limitations, we introduce MobiAgent, a dual-loop agentic framework that bridges robust deployment execution and recursive policy self-improvement. During deployment, the Inner Loop decouples high-level reasoning from low-level control through highly composable atomic skills. It employs Vision-Language models for receding-horizon planning and visual reflection, dynamically composing skills to ensure robust error recovery. These skills are executed by specialized flow-matching experts that share a unified VLM backbone, maximizing reusability while mitigating capacity interference. Concurrently, the Outer Loop drives automated lifelong learning by autonomously segmenting and verifying deployment rollouts, clustering them to discover atomic skills, and continuously fine-tuning the skill library without human annotations. Evaluations on RoboCasa, BEHAVIOR-1K, and real-world tasks demonstrate the effectiveness of MobiAgent. It outperforms $π_{0.5}$-TA by 22.5 percentage points on BEHAVIOR-1K and enables robust recovery from execution failures. Through autonomous data recycling, success improves from 7.50% to 27.50% on RoboCasa and from 32.5% to 57.5% on Astribot S1.
items.titleKo: MobiAgent: 장기 이동형 조작을 위한 이중 루프 재귀적 정책 자기개선
items.abstractKo: 장기 이동형 조작은 실행 오류의 누적과 이동성(주행)과 팔 제어 간의 제어 역량 간섭으로 인해 큰 과제를 제시한다. 최근의 시각-언어-행동(Vision-Language-Action) 모델은 단기 과제에서는 우수하지만, 다단계 목표에 필요한 계층적 추론 능력이 부족하다. 또한 기존의 계층형 에이전트들은 하위 작업의 경직된 매핑, 유연하지 못한 재계획, 그리고 지속적 학습의 부재 등의 문제를 안고 있다. 이러한 한계들을 해결하기 위해, 우리는 강인한 배포 실행과 재귀적 정책 자기개선을 연결하는 이중 루프 에이전트 기반 프레임워크인 MobiAgent를 제안한다.

items.title: I2CD: Direct Image-to-Convex Decomposition for Simulation-Ready Collision Geometry
items.abstract: Physics simulators and motion planners require convex collision geometry, yet image-to-3D generative models output dense, frequently non-manifold visual meshes. Bridging the two today takes a slow, brittle reconstruct-then-decompose pipeline of repair, decimation, and approximate convex decomposition. We present I2CD, which predicts a convex decomposition directly from a single RGB image. Rather than train a new image-to-3D model, I2CD freezes the pretrained Hunyuan3D-2 image-conditioned diffusion transformer and shape decoder and trains only a lightweight cross-attention head (38M parameters, under ten GPU-hours) whose learned "convex-slot" tokens emit the halfplane parameters of $K$ convex polytopes. The output is compact, convex by construction, and loads into physics engines without any post-processing, in ${\sim}0.5$s per image. On $227$ held-out OmniObject3D and Google Scanned Objects instances, I2CD attains the highest volumetric IoU among eight reconstruct-then-decompose pipelines while running $6$-$37\times$ faster end-to-end. In a cross-simulator study in MuJoCo, PyBullet, Genesis, and Isaac Sim, every engine uses I2CD geometry as delivered, whereas raw generated meshes "load" everywhere but are silently replaced by a different collision shape in most cases or need seconds to minutes of per-object preprocessing. On a physical xArm7, I2CD produces planner-ready geometry for a $20$-object cluttered scene in $11$s versus $328$s for the strongest baseline, at comparable pick-and-place execution success ($85$ vs. $90$ of $100$ trials).
items.titleKo: I2CD: 시뮬레이션 준비 충돌 형상을 위한 이미지 기반 직접 볼록 분해
items.abstractKo: 물리 시뮬레이터와 모션 플래너는 볼록 충돌 형상을 필요로 하나, 이미지-투-3D 생성 모델은 조밀하고 종종 비매니폴드인 시각적 메시를 출력한다. 이를 연결하려면 현재 수리, 폴리곤 수 감소(decimation), 근사 볼록 분해를 포함하는 느리고 취약한 '재구성 후 분해(reconstruct-then-decompose)' 파이프라인을 거쳐야 한다. 우리는 단일 RGB 이미지에서 직접 볼록 분해를 예측하는 I2CD를 제안한다. 새로운 이미지-투-3D 모델을 학습시키는 대신 I2CD는 사전학습된 Hunyuan3D-2 이미지 조건부 확산 트랜스포머와 형상 디코더를 고정하고 경량 크로스-어텐션 헤드(38M 매개변수)만 학습한다,

items.title: Bidirectional Voronoi-biased Exploration Curriculum for Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: Long-horizon tasks with sparse rewards pose an exploration bottleneck for goal-conditioned reinforcement learning: a policy started from the initial state rarely reaches the goal and receives no learning signal. Reference motions, hand-designed curricula, and shaped rewards supply this signal but require demonstrations or task-specific engineering; automatic start-state and goal curricula avoid this but typically expand from one side only, so the full distance to the target must be covered from that side. We propose the Bidirectional Voronoi-biased Exploration curriculum for Reinforcement learning (BVER), which expands from both ends at once. Inspired by bidirectional RRT planning, BVER grows start states outward from the goal and goals outward from the initial state distribution, biases both toward unexplored task space, and steers them toward each other, training one goal-conditioned policy on both. On point-mass mazes, quadrupedal box climbing, and robot-arm ring-on-peg transfer, BVER learns faster than all compared reference-free curricula. On box climbing, it reaches 95% success on a 0.4 m box in roughly 65% fewer iterations than the best of them, is the only one of them to learn to climb a 0.7 m box, and yields a policy robust to start, goal, and yaw variation. Without a demonstration, it approaches the sample efficiency of reference-based curricula on the 0.4 m box and on ring-on-peg transfer. Ablations show that expanding from both ends outperforms either direction alone.
items.titleKo: 강화학습을 위한 양방향 보로노이 편향 탐색 커리큘럼
items.abstractKo: 희소 보상을 갖는 장기간 과제는 목표 조건 강화학습에서 탐색 병목을 유발한다. 초기 상태에서 시작한 정책은 거의 목표에 도달하지 못해 학습 신호를 받지 못한다. 참조 동작, 수작업으로 설계된 커리큘럼, 그리고 보상 성형은 이러한 신호를 제공하지만 데모나 과제별 엔지니어링을 요구한다. 자동 생성되는 시작 상태 및 목표 커리큘럼은 이를 회피하지만 대개 한쪽에서만 확장되므로 목표까지의 전체 거리를 그 쪽에서만 커버해야 한다. 우리는 강화학습을 위한 양방향 보로노이 편향 탐색 커리큘럼을 제안한다.

items.title: Native Action-Prior Learning from Videos for World Action Models
items.abstract: World action models integrate future visual dynamics with robot action prediction, but their scalability remains limited by the need for action-annotated robot trajectories. Observation-only videos contain rich evidence about interaction dynamics, but existing approaches typically use them either to pretrain visual representations that must later be adapted for control, or to infer latent actions that are subsequently grounded to robot commands. We present NAVA-WAM, which introduces native action-prior learning by directly pretraining the action policy from observation-only videos, avoiding indirect representation-to-control transfer or a separate latent-action model. Our training consists of two stages. First, we pretrain on observation-only videos, where future-video flow-matching supervision over visual transitions is propagated through transition-structured joint attention to optimize the Action-DiT and learn action-relevant priors. Second, we use action-labeled demonstrations to post-train the Action-DiT for robot control through joint video--action flow matching, while asymmetric attention decouples the visual branch from iterative action denoising and enables efficient action-only inference. Extensive experiments show that NAVA-WAM consistently outperforms prior approaches under both in-distribution and out-of-distribution settings, while demonstrating strong action-label efficiency and effective real-robot generalization. These results establish native action-prior learning as an effective approach to directly pretrain action policies from observation-only videos, providing a scalable path beyond action-labeled robot data.
items.titleKo: 월드 액션 모델을 위한 비디오 기반 직접 행동 사전 학습
items.abstractKo: 월드 액션 모델은 미래의 시각적 역학과 로봇 행동 예측을 통합하지만, 행동 주석이 포함된 로봇 궤적의 필요성 때문에 확장성에는 여전히 한계가 있다. 관찰만으로 얻은 비디오는 상호작용 역학에 관한 풍부한 증거를 포함하고 있으나, 기존 접근법은 보통 이를 제어에 맞춰 나중에 적응시켜야 하는 시각 표현을 사전학습하는 데 사용하거나, 이후 로봇 명령에 연계되는 잠재 행동을 추론하는 데 사용해 왔다. 우리는 NAVA-WAM을 제안한다. NAVA-WAM은 관찰 전용 비디오로부터 행동 정책을 직접 사전학습함으로써 네이티브 행동 사전 학습을 도입하고, ...

items.title: KungfuAthleteBot: learning high-dynamic humanoid motion from video with unified robust recovery
items.abstract: Video is an abundant, inexpensive source of human motion data that is rich in extreme athletic behaviors. Making it usable for humanoid robots, however, is not a matter of simply retargeting a reconstructed trajectory: video-derived motion is physically inconsistent, devoid of actuation information, and says nothing about failure or recovery. We present KungfuAthleteBot (KAB), a framework that treats learning high-dynamic motion from video as the central problem and resolves each of these three failure modes in turn. (C1) We build the KungfuAthlete dataset from videos of national-level martial artists and introduce a physics-guided parabolic trajectory correction that removes height floating, ground penetration, and high-frequency jitter from reconstructed aerial and landing phases. (C2) Because video carries no force information, strict tracking of a reconstructed trajectory is dynamically infeasible, and error-driven initialization keeps re-launching the policy from infeasible aerial poses. We introduce physics-driven pseudo-low-kinetic-energy (LKE) sampling, our central mechanism for making such references learnable: it biases initialization towards dynamically feasible states, letting the policy discover feasible actuation patterns instead of imitating infeasible ones. (C3) Finally, we introduce a direct training paradigm in which disturbance rejection and fall recovery are learned inside the same policy that tracks the video motion, requiring no recovery reference data and no manual mode switching. On a humanoid robot, KAB learns dynamic skills from video and recovers from arbitrary falls in about 0.7 s, the fastest reported recovery for a unified policy. Ablations on the unified policy confirm the necessity of its components, supporting the view that repairing and compensating video data, rather than only collecting more of it, is what unlocks high-dynamic humanoid skills.
items.titleKo: KungfuAthleteBot: 비디오로부터 통합적이고 강건한 복구를 통해 고역학적 휴머노이드 동작 학습
items.abstractKo: 비디오는 극한의 운동 행태가 풍부하게 담긴 인간 동작 데이터의 풍부하고 저비용인 원천이다. 그러나 이를 휴머노이드 로봇에 적용 가능하게 만드는 것은 단순히 재구성된 궤적을 리타겟팅하는 문제가 아니다. 비디오에서 유래한 동작은 물리적으로 일관성이 없고 구동 정보가 결여되어 있으며 실패나 복구에 대해서는 아무것도 알려주지 않는다. 우리는 KungfuAthleteBot(KAB)를 제안한다. 이 프레임워크는 비디오로부터 고역학적 동작을 학습하는 것을 중심 문제로 삼고 이 세 가지 실패 모드를 차례로 해결한다. (C1) 우리는 국가대표급 무술 비디오로부터 KungfuAthlete 데이터셋을 구축한다

items.title: Equivariant Visual-Tactile Diffusion Policy for Contact-Rich Manipulation
items.abstract: Imitation learning for contact-rich manipulation requires high-quality expert data that is expensive to obtain. This makes learning a sample-efficient policy a key issue. To address this, we propose VISTA, a workspace-level equivariant visuotactile diffusion policy for data-efficient contact-rich imitation learning. VISTA projects visual and tactile observations into spherical tokens, injects tactile contact cues into visual spherical directions through permutation-equivariant spherical fusion, and rotates the fused harmonic representation using the end-effector orientation. The resulting representation conditions an equivariant diffusion policy to predict spatially consistent actions. Extensive experiments in both simulation and real-world robotic settings show that VISTA substantially improves data efficiency over strong visuotactile imitation learning baselines. Project website: https://vista-paper.github.io/
items.titleKo: 접촉이 풍부한 조작을 위한 공변적 시각-촉각 확산 정책
items.abstractKo: 접촉이 풍부한 조작을 위한 모방 학습은 고품질의 전문가 시연 데이터가 필요하며, 이는 획득 비용이 높다. 따라서 샘플 효율적인(policy) 학습이 핵심 문제로 대두된다. 이를 해결하기 위해 우리는 데이터 효율적인 접촉 풍부 모방 학습을 위한 작업 공간 수준의 공변적 시각-촉각 확산 정책 VISTA를 제안한다. VISTA는 시각 및 촉각 관측을 구면 토큰으로 투영하고, 순열 공변적 구면 융합을 통해 촉각 접촉 신호를 시각적 구면 방향에 주입하며, 엔드이펙터의 자세를 이용해 융합된 하모닉 표현을 회전시킨다. 그 결과 표현은

items.title: Reconstruct, Practice, Go Real: Guided Self-Improvement for Embodied Agents
items.abstract: Building reliable robot capabilities across diverse tasks requires substantial human effort to develop and maintain skills, design rewards, and integrate perception with control.
